contentBlocks.heading: What Changes for an MYP Student Between August and the Spring Term
contentBlocks.body:
An MYP 1 student in August is mostly doing broad, concept-based classroom work, inquiry questions, unit statements, command terms like 'evaluate' and 'justify' that feel unfamiliar next to a CBSE or ICSE vocabulary. By March, the same student is expected to produce criterion-referenced evidence: work assessed against A, B, C, D strands with specific descriptors, not a single mark out of 100. That shift catches a lot of Chandigarh families off guard, especially those moving in from a board-heavy school or relocating from Delhi or Ludhiana mid-cycle.

For MYP 4 and MYP 5 students the arc is sharper still. The year opens with subject content and closes with eAssessment preparation, onscreen papers, structured tasks, timed practice, plus, for many, a Personal Project that needs a supervisor's sign-off and a genuine record of process, not a finished product handed in at the last minute. Grade 1 to Grade 12 sits inside IB Gram's review scope, so a family can get support whether the concern is a Grade 6 struggling with Individuals and Societies vocabulary or a Grade 10 student six weeks from eAssessment.

But a tutor who only knows 'help with homework' misses this. What matters is a tutor who reads a rubric the way the school does, and can tell a parent honestly which strand is weak and why.

MYP 4-5: criterion-based assessment tightens

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions, Online Sessions, or Splitting the Week Between Both
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring makes sense in Chandigarh when travel is short and the schedule is predictable. A tutor working Sector 8 and Sector 9 together, close to Madhya Marg, can usually hold a fixed evening slot without traffic eating into session time. Sector 15, near Panjab University and Sector 11, works the same way for a tutor already based in that corridor.

Mohali and Panchkula are a different calculation. SAS Nagar and Airport Road on one side, Sector 5 and Zirakpur on the other, a home tutor covering both sides of the tricity in one evening is fighting traffic more than teaching. This is where online tutoring earns its place, not as a compromise but as the better option for a specific subject: an HL Math tutor based in one sector can teach a Mohali student online with zero travel loss, and often more consistently than a home visit squeezed between other bookings.

Hybrid plans are common by MYP 4. A weekly in-person session builds structure and keeps a younger student accountable, while a second online session in the same week handles doubt-clearing or eAssessment drilling with a subject specialist who isn't necessarily local. Families should be honest about which mode their household schedule can actually sustain before committing; a schedule built on optimism about traffic rarely survives a full term.

Online: Mohali and Panchkula specialist access without commute loss
Hybrid: one in-person plus one online session weekly
Scheduling built around school timings, not fixed slots
Honest read on what the family's week can actually sustain

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth That Carries Forward Into DP Levels
contentBlocks.body:
MYP doesn't test subjects the way DP does, but the eight subject groups, Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, Design, are where DP subject choices get shaped. A student weak in MYP Individuals and Societies vocabulary is not going to walk comfortably into DP Economics two years later; a student who never built confident scientific writing in MYP Sciences will find HL Biology or Chemistry lab reports harder than they should be.

IB Gram's tutor pool includes people who teach at DP level in Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English A, and several of them work with MYP students specifically because they can see where the gaps will show up later. That matters most for a Grade 9 or 10 student choosing between Math AA and Math AI for DP, or deciding whether Economics or Business is the better Individuals and Societies fit going forward.

Design and Arts support exists too, though it depends more on individual tutor availability than the core academic subjects, worth checking directly during the review call rather than assuming it, since specialist coverage for these two groups is thinner than for Sciences or Mathematics across most cities, Chandigarh included.
items: Language and Literature: English A foundation
Sciences: lab writing and command-term practice
Individuals and Societies: Economics, Geography, History base
Mathematics: Math AA versus Math AI readiness
Design and Arts on request, subject to availability

Families in Zirakpur, New Chandigarh, Kharar and Aerocity fall slightly outside the tightest home-tutoring pockets. That's not disqualifying. Some tutors do cover these routes, but it's more realistic to expect online tutoring or a hybrid plan there, especially for a specialist subject where the right tutor for the level might not live nearby at all. contentBlocks.heading: PYP Through DP, Where an MYP Student Sits in the Longer Arc
contentBlocks.body:
MYP sits between two programmes families often understand better. The Primary Years Programme, roughly ages 3 to 12, is where inquiry habits and early literacy and numeracy get built, a PYP student typically needs gentle reading support or unit-of-inquiry help, not subject tutoring in the DP sense. The Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, is where subject choices narrow to six subjects at HL or SL, IAs get written, and the two-year clock toward May or November exam sessions starts running.

MYP, roughly ages 11 to 16, is the bridge. Grade 6 through Grade 10 students are meant to leave with broad subject fluency, comfort with criterion-referenced feedback, and, by MYP 5, a completed Personal Project and eAssessment results that some schools use as a signal for DP subject placement.

IB Gram reviews requests across Grade 1 to Grade 12, so a family with one child finishing PYP and another starting MYP, or an MYP 5 student about to choose DP subjects, can work with one process rather than starting over for each programme. The transition points, end of PYP, MYP 5 into DP, are usually where a short, focused review is more useful than ongoing weekly tutoring, and it's worth saying so rather than selling a longer plan than the moment calls for.
items: PYP (ages 3-12): inquiry, reading, numeracy foundations
MYP (ages 11-16): Grade 6-10, criterion fluency, Personal Project
DP (ages 16-19): HL/SL subjects, IAs, May and November sessions
Grade 1 to Grade 12 reviewed under one process
Transition points often need short focused support, not a long plan

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor Actually Gets Matched to Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
The process starts with a review call, not a sign-up form. A parent describes the student's grade, subject group or specific subject, current school, and what's actually going wrong, a Grade 8 student who can't structure an Individuals and Societies response, say, or a Grade 10 student anxious about eAssessment timing. That detail matters more than a generic 'need a tutor' request, because MYP tutoring quality depends on whether the tutor actually understands criterion language for that subject and grade.

From there, IB Gram shortlists tutors based on subject background, MYP or DP teaching experience, mode (home, online, hybrid) and realistic availability for the area, Sector 9 is not the same shortlist as Zirakpur. A tutor's match is never presented as final before a first session; it's a starting point subject to how that first session actually goes.

So the first session itself is diagnostic, not just introductory: the tutor works through recent school material with the student, notes where the gaps are against the actual MYP criteria, and shares that read with the parent afterward. Four weeks in, there's a checkpoint, what's improved, what hasn't, and whether the plan needs adjusting. None of this is guaranteed to produce a specific outcome; what's guaranteed is that the process is visible to the parent at each stage, not hidden behind vague progress updates.

Shortlist by subject depth, mode and area availability

contentBlocks.heading: Academic Honesty Is Not Optional in How IB Tutoring Works
contentBlocks.body:
IB assessment is criterion-based, which means a tutor's job is narrower than it sounds. A tutor can explain what a command term like 'discuss' or 'evaluate' actually requires, can show a student how a criterion descriptor maps to their draft, and can run practice questions under timed conditions. A tutor cannot write, correct into final form, or substantially rewrite work that will be submitted for assessment, that's a line MYP coordinators watch for, and schools do check for it.

IB Gram screens tutors on this specifically: not just subject knowledge, but whether they understand the difference between helping a student think through a Personal Project and doing the thinking for them. A tutor who doesn't respect that distinction is a liability to the family, not a shortcut, because MYP coordinators are trained to notice work that doesn't match a student's classroom voice.

And this shows up in smaller ways too, a tutor should be teaching command-term language explicitly (what 'analyse' asks for versus 'describe'), working from the actual criterion strands the school uses, and being upfront with a parent when a piece of work is genuinely the student's own effort versus still needing independent practice. Parents can and should ask a prospective tutor directly how they handle graded coursework; a tutor who gets defensive about that question is not the right one.
items: Command-term teaching, not command-term substitution
No rewriting or completing assessed work
Criterion strands checked against the actual school rubric
Personal Project: guidance on process, not the product
Ask directly how a tutor handles graded coursework

Families around Sectors 8, 9, 15 and the nearby central sectors tend to be looking for tutors comfortable with a mixed cohort, some students who've been in the IB system since PYP, others who joined mid-MYP from a board school and are still adjusting to criterion feedback.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Shortlisted
contentBlocks.body:
Subject knowledge is the easy part to check; MYP-specific readiness is harder, and that's where most of the actual screening effort goes. Every tutor considered for an MYP request is reviewed for subject background at the level they'll teach, a tutor teaching MYP 5 Individuals and Societies should have depth well beyond the syllabus a Grade 10 student is working through, not just familiarity with it.

Beyond subject knowledge, tutors are checked for whether they can read and apply criterion descriptors accurately, whether they know current command-term usage (IB updates and clarifies these periodically), and whether they've actually supervised or supported Personal Project work before, not just heard of it. And communication matters too: a tutor needs to be able to tell a parent plainly where a student stands, including bad news, rather than defaulting to vague reassurance.

None of this produces a guarantee. Tutor availability shifts, a subject specialist for a rare Individuals and Societies elective may be limited in a given month, and a first-session fit that looks right on paper sometimes still doesn't click with a particular student. What IB Gram controls is the review process itself, checking background, checking criterion fluency, checking honesty around assessed work, and being transparent with parents about what's confirmed versus what's still being verified.
items: Subject depth checked above the level actually taught
Criterion-descriptor and command-term fluency verified
Personal Project supervision experience checked
Communication style assessed, not assumed
Availability and fit remain variable, stated honestly

contentBlocks.heading: Starting Before the Next Report Card or eAssessment Window
contentBlocks.body:
The easiest time to start is before a specific deadline creates pressure, a term report, a Personal Project checkpoint, or, for MYP 5, the onscreen eAssessment window. Starting six weeks out gives a tutor room to run an honest diagnostic first session and actually adjust before the pressure sets in. Starting the week before an eAssessment paper limits what any tutor, however good, can realistically change; that's worth saying plainly rather than promising a turnaround that isn't credible.

Before the review call, it helps to have the student's most recent report or feedback in hand, a rough sense of which subject or criterion is the actual concern, and, if relevant, the Personal Project topic and current stage. None of this needs to be polished; a parent describing 'Criterion C keeps coming back low in Individuals and Societies' is more useful than 'my child needs an IB tutor.'

From there, IB Gram reviews the request against tutor availability for the area and mode, Sector 9 home tutoring, Mohali online, or a Panchkula hybrid plan, and proposes a shortlist. Nothing is locked in until a family has spoken with a shortlisted tutor and both sides agree it's a reasonable fit for the term ahead.
items: Start 4-6 weeks before a report or eAssessment window ideally
Bring recent feedback and the specific concern to the call
Personal Project stage matters if applicable
Shortlist proposed by area, mode and subject
Nothing locked in before both sides agree on fit

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP tutor in Chandigarh actually do differently from a regular school tutor?
faqs.answer: An MYP tutor works from the school's actual criterion strands, the A, B, C, D descriptors, rather than generic worksheets. That means explaining command terms like 'evaluate' or 'justify' the way the school expects them, checking a student's draft against real assessment criteria, and building toward eAssessment or Personal Project readiness rather than just clearing homework. A regular tutor without MYP exposure can still help with content, but the criterion-mapping and academic-honesty boundary usually takes IB-specific experience to get right.

faqs.question: We're in Sector 15, is home tutoring realistic, or should we go online?
faqs.answer: Sector 15, near Panjab University and Sector 11, sits inside a workable home-tutoring pocket for tutors already based in that corridor, so a regular in-person slot is usually realistic. For a specialist subject where the strongest local tutor happens to be based elsewhere in the tricity, online may still be the better fit despite the short distance. IB Gram can review the specific subject and grade before recommending a mode rather than assuming home tutoring by default.

faqs.question: How much does IB MYP tuition cost in Chandigarh?
faqs.answer: There's no fixed number here, fees depend on the subject, the student's grade, session mode (home, online or hybrid) and the individual tutor's experience, and get discussed directly once a shortlist is proposed. A Grade 6 general MYP session and a Grade 10 subject-specialist session ahead of eAssessment are priced differently for good reason. IB Gram doesn't publish a flat rate because doing so would misrepresent what different families actually end up paying.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for MYP, or is home tutoring always better?
faqs.answer: It depends on what's needed. A younger MYP 1-3 student often benefits from the structure and accountability of a home session. An MYP 4-5 student needing a specific subject specialist, urgent doubt-clearing, or eAssessment drilling often does better online, where the right tutor for that level is reachable regardless of which sector they live in. Home tutoring isn't automatically superior, for specialist subjects in a spread-out city like this, online is frequently the stronger option.

faqs.question: What happens if there's no real improvement after a month?
faqs.answer: There's a check-in around week four specifically to catch this. If a student's criterion scores, confidence or engagement haven't moved, the parent and tutor discuss whether the issue is pacing, fit, or something outside tutoring's control, like an unrelated school stressor. IB Gram can help arrange a different tutor if the mismatch is about fit rather than effort. No plan guarantees a specific improvement, but a stalled month shouldn't go unexamined for a full term.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors if the first one isn't working out?
faqs.answer: Yes. A first match is a starting point, not a commitment for the term. If a student and tutor aren't clicking, teaching style, pacing, personality, whatever the reason, a family can ask for a different tutor, and IB Gram will shortlist again based on what didn't work the first time. It helps to say specifically what felt off, since 'change it' without detail makes the second match no more reliable than the first.

faqs.question: How is eAssessment prep for MYP5 different from normal revision?
faqs.answer: eAssessment is onscreen, timed, and structured around specific task types the paper-based system doesn't use in quite the same way, so a student needs practice with the actual interface and pacing, not just content review. Preparation usually means working through structured tasks and past material under timed conditions, tightening command-term responses, and identifying which subjects need the most runway. Starting this six to eight weeks out gives more room than starting two weeks before the window.

faqs.question: Do you cover the Personal Project?
faqs.answer: A tutor can support the process, helping a student narrow a topic, structure the process journal, and reflect against the assessment criteria, but cannot write it or substantially shape the final product, since that would cross into academic dishonesty a school would likely catch. Support is strongest earlier in the timeline, when topic selection and planning happen, rather than in the final weeks when the work is mostly the student's own to finish.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with schools in Mohali or Panchkula?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and isn't officially affiliated with any school in Mohali, Panchkula or elsewhere in the tricity unless a specific tutor profile states otherwise. References to school clusters on this page describe where requests commonly come from, not a partnership. Families should treat any tutor's claimed school connection as something to verify directly rather than assume from this page.

faqs.question: We're in Zirakpur or Kharar, are we too far out for this to work?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but it changes the realistic mode. These areas sit outside the tightest home-tutoring pockets around the central sectors, so online or a hybrid plan is usually the more dependable option rather than counting on a regular home visit. IB Gram can still review a home tutoring request for these areas; whether it's workable depends on a specific tutor's travel radius, which is worth confirming directly during the review call rather than assuming either way.

contentBlocks.heading: The Hidden Cost of Switching PYP Tutors Halfway Through a Unit
contentBlocks.body:
Chandigarh parents rarely go looking for a new IB tutor at a convenient moment. It usually starts when a tutor moves cities, a schedule stops working, or a child's confidence quietly drops mid-unit. What follows is often worse than the original problem, because a new tutor has to relearn a child's habits, the current unit of inquiry, and where exactly the gaps are, before any real teaching can resume.

In the IB Primary Years Programme, this handover matters more than parents expect. PYP does not run on chapters and test dates the way a board syllabus does. A Grade 3 student working through a unit on "How We Organise Ourselves" needs continuity in how ideas connect across subjects, not a tutor who restarts with a generic worksheet. Academic honesty and concept-based learning are built into how IB expects a child to think, so a tutor who does not understand that framework can accidentally undo months of habit-building in a few sessions.

IB Gram exists for exactly this transition. Families across Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula come to the platform not just to find a first tutor, but to replace one without losing a term's progress. The process starts with a short conversation about the child's current unit, reading level and confidence, not a generic subject label. This page explains how that matching actually works for PYP specifically, what home and online tutoring each do well in this city, and what a parent should reasonably expect after the first month.

PYP has no board-style syllabus to fall back on for continuity

contentBlocks.heading: Reading, Numeracy and the Six Units of Inquiry
contentBlocks.body:
At the primary level, IB does not separate a child's day into isolated subjects the way a conventional school timetable does. A PYP tutor works across language, mathematics, science, social studies, arts and personal-social-physical education, tying each back to a transdisciplinary theme such as "Who We Are" or "Sharing the Planet." For a Chandigarh parent used to board-style subject tuition, this can feel unfamiliar at first. The tutor's job in Grade 1 through Grade 5 is less about drilling a chapter and more about building reading fluency, number sense and the habit of asking a good question during an inquiry cycle.

Even so, foundational skill gaps do not fix themselves through inquiry alone. A child weak in phonics or basic multiplication still needs direct, patient practice alongside the inquiry work, and a good PYP tutor knows when to step outside the unit and drill a skill plainly.

IB Gram's Chandigarh network also carries specialists further along the same IB pathway, which matters if a family is planning years ahead rather than one term at a time. The same platform supports Diploma-level subjects such as Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology and English A once a student reaches Grade 11 or 12, so a family can, in principle, stay within one matching process from Grade 1 through the Diploma years rather than restarting the search at every transition.
items: Language, maths, science, social studies, arts and PSPE taught through units of inquiry
Reading fluency and number sense remain the practical backbone under Grade 5
Direct skill drilling still has a place alongside inquiry-based learning
Same tutor network extends into MYP and DP subjects for later grades
Transdisciplinary themes replace isolated chapter-by-chapter teaching

contentBlocks.heading: From Primary Years Through to the Diploma
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram works with families anywhere between Grade 1 and Grade 12 in Chandigarh, which covers all three IB programmes end to end: the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19. Understanding where a child sits in this sequence changes what "tutoring" should even mean.

A PYP student, by definition, is not preparing for an internal assessment, an extended essay or a Theory of Knowledge exhibition; those belong to later stages of the programme and should not be forced onto a nine-year-old's tutoring plan. What does carry across all three programmes is IB's expectation of concept-based learning, academic honesty and criterion-related assessment, so a PYP tutor who explains why an idea matters, rather than just what the answer is, is preparing a child for how MYP and DP will later assess them.

Further up the pathway, IB Gram's Chandigarh tutors support Diploma students heading into the May 2026 and November 2026 exam sessions, including IA structure, EE mentoring, TOK support, school assignment review and mock exam planning. None of that applies to a Grade 2 student today, but it explains why the platform treats programme stage as the first filter in any match, ahead of subject or location, and why a tutor comfortable with PYP inquiry is not automatically right for a DP HL subject three years later.

MYP: ages 11-16, criterion-related assessment becomes more formal
DP: ages 16-19, includes IA, EE, TOK and May/November exam sessions
Concept-based learning and academic honesty run through all three stages
Programme stage is checked before subject or location in any match

contentBlocks.heading: Home Sessions, Screen Time and the Sectors Where Each Works
contentBlocks.body:
For a Chandigarh family with a Grade 2 or Grade 3 child, the mode of tutoring matters as much as the tutor. Home tutoring can be reviewed for requests across Sector 8, Sector 9, Sector 15, Mohali and Panchkula and nearby residential pockets, and for a younger PYP learner, having someone physically present at the table often works better than a screen. Younger children lose focus faster online, and a tutor who can point at a worksheet, sit through a reading struggle, and read a child's body language in the room has a real advantage at this age.

Online tutoring, on the other hand, is available city-wide and tends to be the stronger option for accessing a specialist who is not based near your sector, for revision-heavy periods, or for urgent doubt-clearing between sessions. It also removes the traffic problem: getting a tutor from one side of the tricity to a home in Mohali or Zirakpur during evening traffic is not always realistic, and pretending otherwise sets up cancelled sessions.

Hybrid arrangements are common in practice, pairing a home tutor for weekly reading and numeracy accountability with occasional online check-ins from a specialist for a particular gap. IB Gram does not push families toward one mode by default; the honest answer depends on the child's age, the sector, and how much in-person support genuinely changes learning outcomes at that age. A five-year-old and a Grade 6 student rarely need the same arrangement.

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Actually Pairs a Tutor With Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
The matching process starts with specifics, not a subject dropdown. A parent describes the child's grade, current unit of inquiry or subject struggle, preferred mode, and rough weekly availability. IB Gram reviews this against tutors familiar with PYP's inquiry structure and, where relevant, with the transdisciplinary themes a Chandigarh school is currently teaching.

What gets checked before a suggestion is made includes academic background, prior experience with IB specifically rather than board curricula alone, and comfort with command-term language and criterion-related thinking even at the primary level, since habits formed early carry into MYP. Availability is always conditional; a tutor's slots, sector reach, and current caseload can change, so any suggestion is subject to tutor availability at the time of enquiry rather than a guaranteed roster.

A first session is treated as a diagnostic, not a straight jump into teaching. It typically covers a short reading or number-sense check, a conversation about the child's confidence and attention span, and a look at any recent school feedback or report comments the parent can share. From that, the tutor proposes a simple plan for the first few weeks rather than an open-ended commitment.

If the fit is wrong, whether a personality clash, pacing that is too slow or too fast, or a mode that is not working, IB Gram treats a tutor change as a normal part of the process, not a failure, and the same matching criteria apply again rather than starting from zero.

contentBlocks.heading: Sector 8 to Zirakpur: Reading the Tricity Map Honestly
contentBlocks.body:
Chandigarh tutoring does not stop at the city's own sectors. Families in Sector 8, close to Sector 9 and Madhya Marg, and in Sector 9 itself near Sector 10 and Rose Garden, are within a reasonable home-tutoring radius of each other. Sector 15, close to Panjab University and Sector 11, sits in a slightly different pocket, useful to know if a tutor's other commitments are on that side of the city.

Mohali, including SAS Nagar and the Airport Road stretch, and Panchkula, including Sector 5 and Zirakpur, are both part of what most families here call the tricity rather than treating Chandigarh as a standalone city. A tutor comfortable travelling within one of these clusters is not necessarily practical for the other; Sector 8 to Zirakpur on a weekday evening is a real ask, not a formality.

Beyond the premium pockets, IB Gram also receives enquiries from Sector 10, Sector 11, Sector 17, New Chandigarh, Kharar and Aerocity, areas close enough to the main clusters that online tutoring, or an occasional in-person session, usually makes more sense than a strict weekly home commitment. Families relocating from Ludhiana, Dehradun or Delhi sometimes carry over a tutor relationship online rather than restarting locally, which IB Gram can also support where the tutor is willing to continue remotely. Geography here is less about distance on a map and more about which side of tricity traffic a family and tutor sit on.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Meets Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Trust in a tutoring arrangement is built before the first session, not discovered afterward. IB Gram reviews a tutor's academic qualifications, subject background relevant to the grade and programme they will teach, and prior familiarity with IB specifically: its command terms, its emphasis on process over final answers, and its way of assessing against criteria rather than simple marks out of ten.

For a PYP tutor, this also means checking comfort with younger children directly: patience with a child who cannot sit still for forty minutes, the ability to explain a concept three different ways, and an understanding that a six-year-old's "wrong answer" is often a reasoning problem, not a knowledge gap. None of this is measurable with a single certificate, so IB Gram treats the first few sessions as part of the verification itself, not just the paperwork stage.

Parents are not asked to take any of this on faith. A short background conversation before matching, visibility into the tutor's proposed plan for the first weeks, and an open channel to raise a concern early are all part of the process. If something about a tutor's approach does not sit right after the first session or two, that is useful information, and IB Gram would rather hear it in week one than in week eight.

One limitation worth stating plainly: no verification process can guarantee personality fit. A tutor can be well-qualified and still be the wrong match for a particular child's temperament, which is exactly why the first sessions are treated as a trial, not a commitment.

contentBlocks.heading: What Four Weeks of PYP Tutoring Should Actually Show
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram will not promise a grade jump or a guaranteed outcome, because no honest tutoring process can promise that for a young child still developing basic learning habits. What can be promised is a visible process: a plan a parent can see, weekly academic goals stated in plain language rather than vague progress notes, and a tutor willing to say clearly when something is not working.

By the end of four weeks, a parent should reasonably expect to see three things. First, some concrete evidence of the starting point: which reading level, which numeracy gaps, which part of the current unit of inquiry the child struggled with. Second, a simple record of what changed week to week, even if the change is small, such as a child now finishing independent reading without prompting or attempting a maths problem a different way. Third, an honest note from the tutor about anything that is not moving, rather than blanket reassurance.

If none of that is visible by week four, that itself is useful information for a parent to raise directly rather than waiting through the term. A tutoring relationship that cannot show any concrete change in a month, for a child this young, is worth questioning early rather than persisting out of politeness. Genuine progress in PYP is often quiet, a child asking a better question, or noticing a pattern unprompted, and a good tutor should be able to name that specifically rather than gesture at general improvement.
items: No guaranteed grade jumps or score promises, ever
Parent-visible weekly goals in plain language, not vague progress notes
Starting point documented: reading level, numeracy gaps, unit-of-inquiry struggles
Week-to-week change recorded, even when small
Tutor should flag what is not working rather than reassure blankly

The first session is a diagnostic, not a locked-in commitment, so there is room to see whether the tutor's pace and approach actually suit the child before agreeing to anything longer term. Fees can be reviewed once the grade, subject scope, mode and weekly hours are clear, since a once-a-week online numeracy session and a twice-weekly home arrangement across two subjects are simply different commitments.

For a family currently dealing with a tutor handover mid-unit, the same process applies, with one difference: the first conversation should include exactly where the previous arrangement stopped, so the new tutor is not guessing.

faqs.question: What does an IB PYP tutor actually do differently from a normal school tutor in Chandigarh?
faqs.answer: A PYP tutor works within the current unit of inquiry rather than a fixed textbook chapter, connecting language, maths, science and social studies back to whatever transdisciplinary theme, such as "How We Organise Ourselves", the school is teaching that term. Instead of drilling answers, they focus on reasoning: why an approach works, not just whether the final number is correct. For a Chandigarh family used to board-style tuition, this can initially look less structured, but it mirrors exactly how MYP and DP will later assess the same child, so the habits built now carry forward.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring or online tutoring better for a Grade 2 or Grade 3 PYP student in Chandigarh?
faqs.answer: For most children this young, an in-person tutor at the table works better, since attention spans are short and body language matters when a child is struggling. Home tutoring can be reviewed for Sector 8, Sector 9, Sector 15, Mohali, Panchkula and nearby pockets. Online tutoring becomes more useful once the child is a little older, needs a specific specialist not available nearby, or during a period when travel across tricity traffic genuinely is not realistic for a weekly commitment.

faqs.question: How much does IB PYP tutoring cost in Chandigarh?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the grade, subject scope, mode (home, online or hybrid) and number of weekly sessions, so there is no single number that applies to every family. A once-a-week online numeracy session costs differently from a twice-weekly home arrangement covering reading and a unit of inquiry. IB Gram reviews fees once these specifics are clear, rather than quoting a flat rate up front, because two families asking for "PYP tutoring" can genuinely need very different amounts of a tutor's time.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not the right fit for my child?
faqs.answer: A mismatch is treated as normal information, not a failure on anyone's part. The first sessions function as a trial specifically so this can surface early: pacing too slow, personality clash, or a mode that is not working. If that happens, the same matching process runs again using what was learned from the first attempt, so the second match starts better informed rather than from zero. Parents are encouraged to raise a concern after the first or second session rather than waiting through a full term.

faqs.question: We are switching tutors mid-unit. What should the first session with the new tutor cover?
faqs.answer: The first session should establish exactly where the previous tutor left off: which unit of inquiry, which reading level, which specific gaps, and any recent school feedback. A rushed start that skips this step is the single biggest cause of lost progress during a handover. IB Gram encourages parents to share this context upfront rather than letting the new tutor rediscover it over several sessions, which wastes time the child does not have.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram only work with certain schools in Chandigarh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any school in Chandigarh, Mohali or Panchkula unless specifically stated for a particular tutor. Enquiries commonly come from families connected to sector-based schools, the Mohali international learner cluster and the Panchkula-Zirakpur school corridor, but the platform works with any family following the IB Primary Years Programme regardless of which specific school the child attends.

faqs.question: Can a PYP tutor help if my child is not struggling academically but seems to have lost confidence?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is a common reason families reach out. A PYP tutor's role is not limited to fixing wrong answers; it includes rebuilding a child's willingness to attempt an inquiry question without fear of being wrong. Sessions in this situation often focus more on process and encouragement than content coverage, at least initially. Parents should mention this context clearly when describing what they need, since it changes how a tutor is matched.

faqs.question: How do I know a tutor actually understands IB and is not just teaching board-style content?
faqs.answer: IB Gram checks a tutor's prior familiarity with IB specifically, including comfort with command-term language, concept-based teaching and criterion-related assessment, rather than assuming board tutoring experience transfers automatically. A useful check for parents is to ask a prospective tutor directly how they would approach a specific unit of inquiry, or how they would respond if a child gave a reasoned but factually incorrect answer. A vague answer to that question usually means limited IB-specific experience.

faqs.question: My family recently moved to Chandigarh from Delhi. Can we continue with our previous tutor online?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, if the tutor is willing to continue remotely. IB Gram supports online continuity for families relocating from cities such as Delhi, Ludhiana or Dehradun, since restarting a tutoring relationship from scratch after a move adds unnecessary disruption on top of the move itself. Where the previous tutor cannot continue, the same matching process applies, using the child's current unit and progress history as the starting point rather than beginning blind.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring actually effective for a young PYP child, or is that just a convenience claim?
faqs.answer: It depends heavily on the child's age and attention span, and it would be dishonest to claim online works equally well for every PYP student. For a five- or six-year-old, in-person tutoring is usually more effective when it is available. For an older PYP student, or for short, focused sessions such as a specific numeracy gap, online tutoring can work well. The honest answer is that mode should follow the child's age and the specific need, not a general preference either way.

contentBlocks.heading: What Changes This Week, This Month and This Term
contentBlocks.body: Parents rarely start looking for an IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutor in Chennai because everything is fine. Something has surfaced: a Math AA HL test that went worse than expected, an IA draft that came back with more comments than the student expected, or a school report that quietly flags 'needs more consistency.' The honest answer to 'when should we start' depends on what the actual problem is. A stuck IA data table or a confusing command term in an English A essay is a this-week problem, and a single focused session can usually unblock it. A pattern of shaky Paper 2 structure across two or three internal tests is a this-month problem, needing four to six weeks of scheduled practice before it shows up in a mock. A student heading into the May 2026 or November 2026 session with real gaps in Physics or Chemistry data-based questions is a this-term problem, and pretending otherwise wastes the time that is actually available. IB Gram works across Grade 1 to Grade 12, but DP families searching this page usually sit in the Grade 11 and Grade 12 band, where IA timelines, EE deadlines and TOK exhibition dates compress an already tight school calendar. Good IB tutoring respects concept-based learning, academic honesty and criterion-related assessment. It does not mean a tutor drafting a paragraph a student then submits as their own. The tutor's job is to build the thinking, not skip it.

contentBlocks.heading: Where DP Sits Inside the Wider IB Continuum
contentBlocks.body: The Diploma Programme does not exist in isolation. IB Gram supports the full continuum used by Chennai's international schools: the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19. A parent searching for a DP tutor has usually already been through, or watched a sibling go through, the earlier stages, so it helps to be clear about what changes at each one. PYP support tends to be gentle: reading fluency, numeracy and unit-of-inquiry projects, with a tutor acting more like a patient guide than a subject examiner. MYP support shifts toward turning broad classroom ideas into criterion-ready work, where a student has to show specific skills against specific rubric strands rather than just get the right answer. DP is different again. A DP tutor for Math AA HL or Physics HL is a subject specialist first, someone comfortable with Higher Level or Standard Level depth, command-term precision and the internal assessment process, not a generalist who can cover any grade. The transition from MYP to DP catches some families off guard, because the jump from criterion bands to IA and EE expectations is real, and a student who coasted through Grade 10 sometimes needs deliberate support building study habits fit for DP workload before subject content becomes the main issue at all.

Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16: criterion-ready coursework and rubric literacy
Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19: HL/SL subject depth, IA, EE and TOK
MYP to DP transition is where study-habit gaps often surface first

contentBlocks.heading: Adyar to Velachery: Reading the Map Before Choosing a Mode
contentBlocks.body: Chennai's international school families are not concentrated in one part of the city, and that shapes what a realistic tutoring plan looks like. Adyar, including Besant Nagar and Indira Nagar, sits close to older, established school clusters, and home tutoring inside this pocket is usually straightforward to schedule. Anna Nagar, together with Shenoy Nagar and Kilpauk, forms a similar central cluster where a tutor can reasonably build a weekly home-visit routine. Velachery, alongside Guindy and Taramani, works the same way for families in the city's southern-central belt. OMR, covering Thoraipakkam and Sholinganallur, and ECR, covering Neelankarai and Injambakkam, are a different story. These corridors have grown fast, distances between pockets are longer, and Chennai traffic during school-pickup hours can turn a short-looking map distance into an hour each way. IB Gram can review home tutoring requests across all five of these areas and nearby residential pockets, but for OMR and ECR specifically, online or hybrid tutoring is often the more realistic answer for a rare DP subject combination or a tutor who genuinely fits the level needed. Nearby areas including Nungambakkam sit close enough to central clusters to be reviewed case by case. Families relocating from or comparing against Bangalore, Hyderabad or Coimbatore should expect a similar pattern: dense central clusters favour home visits, sprawling newer corridors favour online specialist access instead.

Anna Nagar (Shenoy Nagar, Kilpauk): similar central cluster
Velachery (Guindy, Taramani): southern-central, workable for home tutoring
OMR (Thoraipakkam, Sholinganallur) and ECR (Neelankarai, Injambakkam): online or hybrid usually more realistic
Nungambakkam and other nearby pockets reviewed case by case

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth: From Math AA HL to English A Paper 2
contentBlocks.body: A DP subject list looks short on paper and is not short in practice. IB Gram works with tutors across Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English A, and the depth required differs sharply by subject and level. Math AA HL is proof- and technique-heavy, and a tutor needs to be fluent enough in the syllabus to explain why a method works, not just how to execute it. Math AI HL leans more applied, with technology use and modelling that a generalist Class 12 tutor rarely practises regularly. Physics and Chemistry both carry a strong data-based-question component in Paper 2 and Paper 3, and this session's exam focus for Chennai DP students includes specific attention to science data questions, since that is where marks are lost even by students who know the theory. Biology tends to reward precise terminology and command-term discipline as much as raw content knowledge. Economics needs a tutor who can move between diagrams, evaluation paragraphs and real-world application without the answer turning generic. English A analytical writing is its own challenge this session, with structured attention to how a student builds a literary or textual argument rather than just summarising plot or content. Assessment support across all of these includes IA structure guidance, EE mentoring, TOK support, review of school-set assignments, past-paper revision and mock exam planning, with weekly academic goals visible to the parent rather than hidden inside a tutor's private notes somewhere.
items: Math AA HL: proof technique and method reasoning, not just answers
Math AI HL: applied modelling and technology use
Physics and Chemistry: data-based questions in Paper 2/3, a specific focus this session
Biology: command-term precision and terminology discipline
Economics: diagrams plus evaluation, not generic answers
English A: analytical writing structure for Paper 1 and Paper 2

contentBlocks.heading: Matching a Tutor to Your Child's Actual School Calendar
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram groups Chennai's DP families loosely by school corridor, because a tutor's usefulness depends heavily on fitting a specific calendar of mocks, IA deadlines and holidays rather than a generic exam season. The South Chennai international learner cluster spans Adyar, Velachery and Besant Nagar, and families here tend to want a tutor who can attend consistently through the term without long commute gaps. The OMR and ECR school corridor covers OMR, ECR and Sholinganallur, where school timings plus commute distance usually push families toward online or hybrid support, especially once IA season starts and last-minute sessions matter more than physical presence. Central Chennai premium school families, spread across Anna Nagar, Nungambakkam and Kilpauk, sit in a cluster where both home and hybrid tutoring tend to work, since distances are shorter and school pickup patterns are more predictable. None of this is about which school is academically stronger; it is about logistics that actually determine whether a tutoring plan survives a full term. To be direct, IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any school unless specifically stated on a school-specific page. A tutor is matched to your child's subject, level and calendar, not to a school's own IB coordinator or programme office, and any claim to the contrary from a tutor should be treated as a warning sign rather than a reassurance.

OMR/ECR corridor: OMR, ECR, Sholinganallur, online or hybrid usually fits IA season better
Central Chennai cluster: Anna Nagar, Nungambakkam, Kilpauk, home or hybrid both workable
IB Gram is independent and not affiliated with any school unless stated

contentBlocks.heading: How a Match Actually Gets Made
contentBlocks.body: The process starts with specifics, not a form asking for a general subject name. A parent shares the exact subject and level, since Math AA HL is not the same request as Math AI SL, along with the grade, the target exam session, and what has actually gone wrong or feels shaky. That last part matters more than families expect: 'weak at Physics' and 'can solve textbook problems but freezes on unfamiliar data-based questions' point toward different tutors entirely. IB Gram reviews this against subject background, exam-board familiarity and area or online availability before suggesting a match, rather than sending the first available person. A first session is diagnostic by design. It is not a sales pitch and not a random worksheet; a good tutor spends part of it finding out exactly where the gap is, what the student's school has already covered, and how the student explains their own thinking, since command-term precision only improves once a tutor sees the actual pattern of mistakes. From there, a short plan gets set: what the next four weeks look like, which specific skills or content areas come first, and what a parent should expect to see change. Around the four-week mark, that plan gets reviewed against what actually happened, not against a vague sense of things going well. If a tutor is not the right fit after a genuine attempt, IB Gram treats a switch as a normal part of matching, not as a failure to be avoided at all costs.
items: Parent shares exact subject, level, grade and target session, not a general request
First session is diagnostic: finds the actual gap, not a generic worksheet
A four-week plan sets specific skills, not just 'improve overall'
Week-four review checks the plan against what actually happened
Switching tutors is treated as normal, not as failure

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid: Picking the Right Shape for DP
contentBlocks.body: There is no single right answer here, and any page claiming otherwise is not being straight with you. Home tutoring works well inside tight clusters; Adyar, Anna Nagar or Velachery are the clearest examples, where a tutor can build a predictable weekly visit into their own travel route without half the session's value getting eaten by traffic. It also tends to suit younger learners who benefit from someone physically present to hold attention and structure. Online tutoring is often the stronger choice for DP specifically, for a few concrete reasons. Rare subject-level combinations like Math AI HL or a specific Economics teaching-style gap are easier to match without geography as a constraint. IA review sessions often need to happen on short notice rather than on a fixed weekly slot. And during exam season, continuity matters more than physical presence: a student stuck on a Chemistry data question at 9pm before a mock benefits more from a quick online session than waiting three days for the next scheduled home visit. Hybrid plans try to take the best of both, a regular in-person session for accountability and structure, plus online access to a specialist for particular subjects or urgent doubts. Families in OMR and ECR, where commute distance works against frequent home visits, often land on hybrid or fully online plans by necessity rather than preference, and that is a reasonable trade-off, not a compromise to feel bad about.
items: Home tutoring: best inside Adyar, Anna Nagar, Velachery clusters; good for younger learners
Online tutoring: often stronger for rare DP subjects, IA review and urgent doubts
Hybrid: in-person accountability plus online specialist access
OMR/ECR families often choose hybrid or online for practical, not preferential, reasons

contentBlocks.heading: The Limits of What Any Tutor Can Honestly Promise
contentBlocks.body: It is worth being plain about what a page like this will not say. IB Gram will not promise a specific grade, a 7 in Math AA HL, or a guaranteed percentage improvement, and any tutor or platform that does is making a promise it cannot actually control; a student's own effort, school context and starting point matter more than any single tutor can override. There is no tutor-count figure quoted here either, because a headline number says nothing about whether the right person is available for your specific subject, level and area this month. Availability is genuinely conditional and depends on subject, level and tutor schedule at the time you ask. What IB Gram can commit to is the process: matching based on actual subject and level fit, checking background before a suggestion is made, and being honest when a request is hard to fill immediately rather than forcing a mediocre match to close the loop quickly. IB Gram is also not affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge, or Pearson Edexcel, and does not claim insider access to any exam board; a tutor's exam-board familiarity comes from experience teaching the syllabus, not from any official relationship. Concept-based learning, academic honesty and criterion-related assessment are treated as non-negotiable inside every session, which sometimes means a tutor pushes a student to redo their own IA section rather than fix it for them, even when that is the slower option in the short term.
items: No guaranteed grades, no invented statistics, no tutor-count headline
Availability is conditional on subject, level and schedule, stated honestly
Not affiliated with IB Organization, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel
Academic honesty enforced even when it is the slower option

contentBlocks.heading: The Checks Behind Every Tutor Suggestion
contentBlocks.body: Matching only works if the checking behind it is real, so here is what that actually looks like. Every tutor considered for a DP request is reviewed against the specific subject and level combination first; a tutor comfortable with Math AA SL is not automatically suited to Math AA HL, and IB Gram treats that distinction as a filtering criterion, not a footnote. Qualifications and subject background are checked against what the request needs: a Physics tutor for HL data-based-question support is a different profile from one who mainly handles conceptual revision. Exam-board familiarity matters specifically for IB, since command terms, criterion-related mark schemes and the IA/EE process are distinct from a typical board syllabus, and a tutor who has only taught CBSE or state-board Class 12 content is not treated as automatically interchangeable with a DP specialist. Past experience with the specific assessment components a student needs, whether that is IA structuring, EE mentoring, TOK support, or Paper 3 case-study practice, is weighed against the actual request rather than assumed from a general IB-tutor label. None of this is presented as a score or a badge; it is a filtering process applied before a name is ever suggested to a parent, and it is also why a request for an unusual subject-level combination can take longer to fill than a common one, since IB Gram would rather say a match needs more time than send someone under-qualified for the specific level required.
items: Subject and level checked as one unit: HL and SL are treated as different requests
Qualifications matched against the specific request, not a generic profile
Exam-board familiarity with IB command terms and criterion-related marking specifically
Experience with the exact assessment component needed: IA, EE, TOK or Paper 3
Uncommon subject-level requests may take longer to fill rather than being rushed

contentBlocks.heading: Starting This Week Without Overcommitting
contentBlocks.body: A parent does not need to commit to a term-long plan before finding out whether a tutor is the right fit. The realistic first step is to describe the actual situation: subject, level, grade, area or online preference, and what specifically has gone wrong or feels shaky, and let IB Gram review that against current tutor availability rather than starting with a long-term contract. A single diagnostic session is usually enough to tell whether the fit is right. Does the tutor ask about what the school has already covered? Do they focus on the actual gap rather than a generic syllabus tour? Does the student's confidence look different by the end of it, even before content has visibly improved? From there, a four-week plan with specific goals gives both the parent and the tutor something concrete to check against, rather than a vague sense of whether things are going well. For a family currently deciding between an Adyar home tutor, an OMR online specialist, or a hybrid plan around Anna Nagar, the honest answer is that the right shape depends on the exact subject, the target exam session and how much travel is realistic on a school-day evening. That is a conversation worth having before committing, not after three months of a plan that never quite fit the student in front of it.
items: Start with specifics: subject, level, grade, area or online preference
One diagnostic session shows fit before any long-term commitment
Four-week plan with named goals, checked rather than assumed
Right mode depends on subject, exam session and realistic travel time

faqs.question: How much do IB DP tutors in Chennai charge?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by subject, level and mode, and IB Gram does not publish one flat number because a Math AA HL specialist with strong IA and EE experience is priced differently from tutoring for a less specialised subject, and online sessions are often priced differently from home visits inside Adyar or Anna Nagar. Rather than quote a misleading average, IB Gram shares specific tutor fees once your subject, level, grade and preferred mode are known, so you can compare against what that tutor actually offers before committing. Ask directly during the first conversation; a clear fee structure with no hidden add-ons is a reasonable thing to expect upfront.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors if it isn't working out?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it happens more often than families expect, especially for a subject as specific as Math AI HL or Economics HL where teaching style matters as much as content knowledge. IB Gram treats a mismatch as a normal part of the process rather than something to apologise for. The useful approach is to give a genuine attempt, usually a few weeks with clear goals, before deciding, since some friction early on is just adjustment, not incompatibility. But if a student's confidence keeps dropping, or sessions consistently miss the actual gap despite feedback, say so directly and a different tutor can be suggested based on what specifically did not work.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for something like Physics HL or Chemistry HL?
faqs.answer: For most DP subjects, yes, particularly for IA review, doubt-solving and revision, where screen-sharing a data table or a past-paper question works about as well as doing it on paper across a table. Where online is genuinely weaker is hands-on lab technique discussion and some younger-learner attention-holding, which is why home tutoring still suits certain PYP and MYP situations better. For a Grade 12 student preparing Physics HL or Chemistry HL Paper 3 case-study questions before May 2026 or November 2026, online sessions are often the more practical choice, especially for families in OMR or ECR where travel time would otherwise eat into study time.

faqs.question: What if there's no real improvement after a few months?
faqs.answer: This is worth asking honestly rather than assuming a plan is failing on its own. First, the four-week check-in should already have flagged whether the plan's specific goals were met, so a genuine no-improvement situation after months usually means that review did not happen properly, or the goals were too vague to check against. Second, some subjects show slower visible movement; EE and TOK development is gradual by nature, unlike a Paper 1 score. If a parent is not seeing change against a plan's stated goals, the right response is a direct conversation and, if needed, a different tutor, not simply continuing and hoping.

faqs.question: Do tutors help specifically with the IA and EE, or just regular subject content?
faqs.answer: Both, but differently. Regular subject sessions cover content, past-paper technique and command-term practice. IA and EE support is mentoring, not writing: a tutor helps a student choose a workable research question, structure the investigation or essay, and understand what the criteria actually reward, while the analysis, argument and final writing stay the student's own work. This distinction matters for academic honesty, and IB Gram is direct with families about it upfront. A tutor drafting content a student submits as their own is not a service offered here, regardless of how tight a deadline looks.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic for a family in OMR or ECR?
faqs.answer: It can be, but distance and Chennai traffic are real constraints worth being upfront about. OMR, including Thoraipakkam and Sholinganallur, and ECR, including Neelankarai and Injambakkam, cover a lot of ground, and a tutor's travel time during school-pickup hours can turn a workable-looking plan into missed or shortened sessions. IB Gram can review a home tutoring request in these corridors, but for a specialist DP subject or an urgent IA week, online or hybrid tends to be the more dependable option, and being honest about that upfront avoids a plan that quietly falls apart after a month.

faqs.question: How is a DP tutor different from a regular Class 12 tutor?
faqs.answer: A CBSE or state-board Class 12 tutor is usually strong on a fixed syllabus and a known exam pattern. DP asks for something else: comfort with command-term language, criterion-related mark schemes, Higher Level versus Standard Level depth in the same subject name, and the internal assessment process that a board exam simply does not have. A tutor who has only taught board syllabuses can still be a capable subject expert, but exam-board familiarity with IB specifically is checked separately, because a student loses marks in DP exams for reasons that have nothing to do with subject knowledge and everything to do with command-term and criterion mismatches.

faqs.question: What happens if my child is behind with only a few months left before the exam session?
faqs.answer: Say so plainly when you reach out, because the plan for eight months of runway looks nothing like the plan for eight weeks. Close to May 2026 or November 2026, the useful focus is usually narrower: past-paper practice targeted at specific weak question types, particularly the science data-based questions and English A analytical writing that tend to cost marks even for students who know the content, plus a realistic view of which topics still need full teaching versus which just need revision. A tutor should be honest about what is achievable in the time left rather than promising a turnaround that isn't realistic.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have any connection to my child's school or to the IB Organization?
faqs.answer: No, and it is worth being direct about this. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform, not affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel, or any specific school in Chennai unless explicitly stated on that school's own page. A tutor is matched based on your child's subject, level and situation, not through any relationship with a school's IB coordinator. If a tutor or platform claims official school or IB Organization backing, that claim should be treated with scepticism rather than as reassurance.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover multiple DP subjects, like Math and Physics together?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, but it should not be assumed. Some tutors genuinely cover two closely related subjects well; Math AA HL and Physics HL is a common enough pairing given the overlap in problem-solving style. But Economics and Biology, for instance, need different enough thinking that combining them with one tutor is usually a compromise on depth for convenience. IB Gram checks the actual combination requested against a tutor's real subject strength rather than assuming any science or math background transfers automatically, since a Grade 12 student preparing HL-level papers cannot really afford a tutor who is only moderately strong in one of the two subjects.

contentBlocks.heading: What an MYP Tutor Actually Does That a School Teacher Doesn't
contentBlocks.body:
A school teacher in an IB Middle Years Programme classroom has twenty-five students, a syllabus map to finish before the term ends, and criteria to grade against a fixed timetable. A tutor has one student and no deadline pressure from the school calendar. That difference decides almost everything about what tutoring should look like for a Grade 6 to 10 learner in Chennai.

Inside a classroom, a teacher explains a concept once, checks understanding with a show of hands, and moves on because thirty other students are waiting. A tutor sitting with your child can stop mid-explanation, ask what confused them about the command term 'evaluate' versus 'discuss', and rebuild the idea from wherever it broke down. That is not remedial catch-up. It is closing a specific, named gap in criterion understanding before it compounds across Individuals and Societies, Sciences and Language and Literature.

An MYP tutor in Chennai worth hiring will read the actual task sheet the school issued, map it against the criterion strands the subject uses, and work backward from there. A generic tuition teacher, however capable, often teaches the subject in general rather than the assessment sitting in front of the student. That distinction is the whole case for tutoring at this stage.
