faqs.question: What does an IB DP tutor in Dehradun actually cover in a session?
faqs.answer: A typical session covers one DP subject at the level the student is actually studying — say Physics HL or Math AI HL — with time split between clearing a specific doubt, working through past-paper questions under time pressure, and reviewing recent school assignments or IA drafts against IB criteria. Sessions are not generic revision; they follow what the student's school has already taught and what the mock or paper schedule requires next. A parent can ask for a brief note after each session covering what was worked on.

faqs.question: How much does IB DP tutoring cost in Dehradun?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on subject, level, tutor experience and whether sessions are home-based or online, so IB Gram does not quote a single fixed number. HL science and Math AA HL, being harder to source specialists for, typically sit at a different rate than a general subject. The proposed match includes the tutor's rate upfront, before any commitment, so a family can compare it against their budget and decide, rather than discovering it after a first session.

faqs.question: Can we switch tutors if the first match is not working?
faqs.answer: Yes. A first session or two is meant to show whether the fit is right — subject depth, teaching pace and how the student responds to the tutor's style all matter. If it is not working, say so plainly rather than persisting through a term hoping it improves; IB Gram reviews the concern and looks at alternative tutors for the same subject and level. Switching costs some continuity, so it is worth raising a concern early rather than after several sessions.

faqs.question: Does online IB DP tutoring actually work as well as home tutoring?
faqs.answer: For most DP subject work — past-paper practice, IA review, doubt-clearing — yes, particularly with screen-sharing and a digital whiteboard. Where online is genuinely weaker is with a younger or less self-directed student who needs someone physically present to hold focus for a two-hour block. For boarding students, rare HL subjects, or the final weeks before a May or November paper, online is often the more reliable option simply because it does not depend on Dehradun traffic or a fixed travel route.

faqs.question: We live near Sahastradhara Road — is home tutoring realistic for us?
faqs.answer: It can be reviewed, but honestly, Sahastradhara Road sits further from where most DP tutors travel regularly compared to Rajpur Road or Dalanwala, so home-tutoring options may be fewer and slots tighter. Online tutoring is usually the more dependable route for a family in this pocket, especially for a specialist HL subject, since it removes the travel question completely. A hybrid plan — occasional in-person sessions plus a regular online slot — is worth asking about too.

faqs.question: My son is starting DP Math AA HL in Grade 11 — is he in the right level?
faqs.answer: That depends on his comfort with abstract, proof-style algebra and where he wants to study after Grade 12; AA HL suits engineering and quantitative degree paths, while AI HL suits applied, calculator-active mathematics. A subject tutor can usually tell within the first two or three sessions whether the level fits, based on how he handles unfamiliar problem types rather than familiar ones. Flagging a mismatch in Grade 11, not after a poor mock, is what actually saves the year.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no real progress after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: By four weeks, a parent should see something concrete — an IA outline, a specific mock score, or command terms answered correctly that were not before. If none of that shows up, that is the signal to review the match rather than wait out the term. IB Gram will look again at subject fit, pace and whether the mode — home, online or hybrid — actually suits the student, rather than assuming more time alone will fix it.

faqs.question: How does IA and EE support work without the tutor doing the work themselves?
faqs.answer: IB's academic honesty rules mean a tutor can discuss structure, mark schemes and criteria, and point out where an argument is weak or a source is misused, but cannot write or substantially rewrite the assessed work itself. In practice this looks like reviewing a draft against the specific criterion it is being marked on, asking questions that expose a gap in the student's own reasoning, and flagging citation or command-term issues — the student still produces every sentence that gets submitted.

faqs.question: How do we start if we are not in Dehradun ourselves but our child boards there?
faqs.answer: The same way: share the subject, level and preferred exam session, and note that the student boards in Dehradun so home tutoring may not be practical. Online tutoring is usually the right default here, and IB Gram can coordinate scheduling around the school's boarding timetable rather than a home address. Outstation and overseas parents — including those checking in from Chandigarh, Ludhiana or Delhi — commonly use this route for exactly this reason.

contentBlocks.heading: What Actually Breaks When an MYP Tutor Changes Mid-Year
contentBlocks.body:
A tutor change midway through an MYP unit is more disruptive than it looks from outside. The new tutor needs to know which criteria the student's Individuals and Societies assignment was marked against last term, which command terms the science teacher expects an answer to open with, and how far into a Mathematics unit the class actually got before the handover happened. Miss that context and the first few sessions go into re-diagnosing rather than teaching — time a Dehradun family juggling school assessments and a tight calendar rarely has to spare.

This is common enough in Dehradun's MYP households that it shapes how IB Gram approaches a first match. Boarding-school terms end abruptly, families relocate between postings, and a tutor who suited a student two years ago may not suit the same student now that the work has shifted toward criterion-heavy Individuals and Societies or Science tasks. So the request form asks for more than subject and level: current unit, recent criterion feedback, and what the previous arrangement covered, if there was one.

A tutor who inherits that context can pick up mid-unit without the student repeating work already understood. One who does not spends the first month catching up instead of moving forward, and a parent notices the difference within a few sessions, not a few months. That gap is exactly what a good handover is meant to close.
items: Criterion feedback from the previous term carried into the first session
Command-term conventions the student's current school expects
Unit progress noted so nothing is repeated or skipped
A short settling-in session before new material starts

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or a Hybrid Plan for an MYP Household Here
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring can be reviewed in central residential pockets of Dehradun, and it tends to work best for younger MYP students and families living close to a tutor's travel routes — someone already in Dalanwala or Vasant Vihar is a more realistic ask than someone crossing town after school hours and evening traffic. For a student still building study habits, having a tutor physically present at the table, checking notebook organisation and reading body language, often matters more than subject depth alone.

Online tutoring stays available across Dehradun and tends to suit different situations better: a boarding student who is only home during vacations, a subject where strong local tutors are thin on the ground, or a period right before a school assessment when a same-evening doubt-clearing session matters more than travel convenience. It also holds up well for MYP eAssessment preparation, where past-paper familiarity and screen-based practice are part of the point.

Hybrid plans are common once a student is deeper into MYP — an in-person session most weeks for accountability and structure, with an online slot added around a school assessment or exam block for extra practice. None of these is automatically better. A family close to Rajpur Road with flexible evenings might prefer home tutoring throughout; a boarding family with a child at school near Mussoorie Road might need online-only from day one. What gets reviewed is the schedule, the subject and the student, not a default assumption.

contentBlocks.heading: Why Subject Choice Now Shapes the Diploma Later
contentBlocks.body:
MYP does not carry HL and SL labels the way the Diploma Programme does, but the subject groups a student works through here set up exactly those choices. A student comfortable with Individuals and Societies argument structure in MYP is the one who later manages Economics essays without relearning how to build an argument from scratch. A student who has only ever done mechanical Mathematics without concept-based reasoning often struggles once Math AA HL or Math AI HL demands exactly that reasoning under exam conditions.

IB Gram's tutor pool for Dehradun families spans the subjects that matter across this transition: Math AA HL and Math AI HL pathways, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology and English A. A tutor working with an MYP student in one of these areas is not simply teaching content ahead of syllabus; they are building the habits — evidence use, command-term precision, structured written response — that carry straight into DP assessment criteria two or three years on.

This matters more in a city like Dehradun, where an international-school student may sit MYP eAssessment on-screen at the end of Year 5 and move into Diploma subject selection almost immediately after. A tutor who only drills the current unit and ignores that trajectory is doing a narrower job than the family actually needs. Subject depth here means understanding where a topic is headed, not just where it currently sits in the term's syllabus.

contentBlocks.heading: How MYP Connects to What Came Before and What Comes Next
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram supports families across Grade 1 to Grade 12 in Dehradun, which in IB terms spans three connected programmes: the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19. A student does not experience these as separate boxes — the inquiry habits built in PYP shape how comfortably a child handles MYP's more structured criteria, and MYP's criterion-related assessment is what the Diploma Programme later assumes a student already knows how to do.

This is why an MYP tutor's job is not just subject coaching. It involves respecting concept-based learning rather than reducing a unit to memorised answers, holding a firm line on academic honesty when a student is tempted to lean too heavily on a tutor's phrasing, and teaching command-term language precisely — the difference between explain and evaluate is not decorative in MYP marking, it changes what the criteria expect on the page.

A tutor who treats MYP as a watered-down version of GCSE or a warm-up for the Diploma misses what the programme actually asks for. The work is to help a student think through a problem using the command term given, not to hand them a polished answer that looks right but was never actually theirs.

Once a match is suggested, subject to tutor availability and schedule, a first session is set up to confirm fit before any commitment is made. That first session is diagnostic as much as instructional — it tells both sides whether the pace, communication style and teaching approach actually work for this particular student, not a hypothetical average one. contentBlocks.body:
A tutor's qualifications and subject background are reviewed before a match is suggested, along with familiarity with the specific exam board the family needs — IB in this case, since IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with the IB Organization. That distinction matters practically: a tutor's understanding of criterion-related assessment and command-term language comes from working with MYP material directly, not from a certificate claiming an official IB endorsement that does not exist for individual tutors.

No page on this platform will promise a guaranteed score, a fixed grade jump or a specific improvement percentage, because no honest tutor can promise that for a subject as dependent on a student's baseline, effort and school context as this one is. What can be reviewed honestly is process: whether a tutor's approach fits the student's current level, whether the schedule is realistic given school timings and travel, and whether progress is visible to the parent on a weekly basis rather than only showing up at report-card time.

Parent-visible weekly academic goals are part of that process — a short note on what was covered, what the student struggled with, and what the next session will target. It is a smaller thing than a guarantee, but it is the thing that is actually true and actually useful week to week.

contentBlocks.heading: By Week Four, Something Concrete Should Be Visible
contentBlocks.body:
By the end of four weeks, a parent should be able to point to something specific rather than a general sense that things are going fine. That might be a criterion score that moved from a 3 to a 5 on a rubric the school itself uses, a student who now opens an Individuals and Societies response with the right command-term structure without being reminded, or simply a student who no longer needs a parent to sit alongside them to start homework. Vague reassurance is not enough at this stage; something concrete should be visible.

Weekly notes should show what was covered against what was planned, and where the plan changed and why — a tutor who never deviates from a rigid plan regardless of what the student actually struggled with that week is often not paying close attention. For an older MYP student approaching the Diploma, early conversations about IA structure, subject-level choices or the kind of thinking TOK asks for are reasonable even before the formal DP transition happens, since criterion-related thinking builds gradually rather than switching on overnight.

If none of this is visible by week four — no measurable shift, no adjusted plan, no clearer written response — that is the honest signal to revisit the match rather than wait another term hoping it corrects itself.

introSummary: Searching for an IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) tutor in Dehradun usually means one of two things: a child is struggling with reading, writing or numeracy inside an inquiry-based classroom, or a family new to the IB system wants someone who understands concept-based learning rather than rote drilling. IB Gram reviews the request, checks grade, subject focus and preferred mode, then shortlists tutors familiar with PYP's unit-of-inquiry approach for home tutoring in central Dehradun pockets or online anywhere in the city, including for boarding and outstation families.

contentBlocks.heading: Inside a First IB PYP Session in Dehradun
contentBlocks.body:
A first session should never feel like a sales pitch. For a PYP-age child in Dehradun, it should feel more like a quiet diagnostic: the tutor asks the child to read a paragraph aloud, look at a recent piece of writing, work through a few numeracy questions pitched slightly above and below grade level, and talk through whatever unit of inquiry the class is currently on. None of this is assessed formally in the way a Diploma Programme paper is; PYP runs on ongoing, criterion-related assessment built into the classroom, not external exams. So the tutor's job in session one is to notice, not to test.

Parents often expect a demonstration lesson. What actually happens is closer to a short interview, sometimes fifteen minutes with the child and fifteen with the parent, covering the school's current reporting period, the child's confidence level, and anything the class teacher has flagged. A tutor who cannot explain concept-based learning, the PYP learner profile, or the difference between helping a child think through a unit-of-inquiry task and simply doing it for them, is the wrong match regardless of how strong their subject knowledge looks on paper. Academic honesty starts early in the IB system, even at age seven.

By the end of session one, a parent should have a plain-language note: what was observed, what the next four weeks will focus on, and how progress will be checked.

A quick look at a recent writing sample or workbook page
Numeracy questions pitched around and slightly beyond grade level
A conversation about the current unit of inquiry

A written, plain-language note on what comes next

contentBlocks.heading: Reading, Numbers and Units of Inquiry: Where PYP Tutoring Actually Helps
contentBlocks.body:
PYP does not split into separate subjects the way the Diploma Programme does. Most tutoring requests in Dehradun fall into three overlapping areas: literacy (reading fluency, comprehension, and writing structure), numeracy (number sense, operations, and problem-solving language), and support with whatever transdisciplinary unit the class is working through, which might touch science, social studies, or both in the same week. A child who is fine at mechanical reading but struggles to answer inference questions needs a different kind of session than one who reads slowly but understands everything.

Command-term language matters even here. PYP tasks increasingly use words like 'explain', 'compare' and 'reflect', and a child who has never been taught what those words are asking for will lose marks on classroom assessment regardless of subject knowledge. A tutor who has actually taught inside an IB PYP classroom, or trained specifically for it, tends to catch this faster than someone applying a general tutoring background.

There is also a pathway worth mentioning honestly: the same Dehradun tutoring network that supports Math AA HL, Physics, Chemistry and English A learners in the Diploma years exists because those students needed foundations built years earlier. A family thinking two or three years ahead sometimes asks for a tutor who can, in principle, continue past PYP into MYP. That continuity is worth asking about directly rather than assuming it, since it depends on tutor availability and subject match at the time.
items: Reading fluency and comprehension, not just decoding
Writing structure: paragraphs, sequencing, editing habits
Numeracy: number sense, operations, word problems
Unit-of-inquiry support spanning science and social studies themes
Command-term literacy: what 'explain' or 'compare' is actually asking

contentBlocks.heading: From PYP to the Diploma Years: One Grade Range, Three Programmes
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram's Dehradun tutor network works across the full IB pathway: the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19, together spanning roughly Grade 1 through Grade 12 depending on when a school transitions a student between stages. The programmes overlap by a year or two at each boundary, which is precisely where a lot of parent confusion comes from — a Grade 6 student might already be in MYP at one school and still finishing PYP at another.

For a PYP family, this matters less for today's session and more for planning ahead. A tutor who understands where PYP's inquiry habits are meant to lead — toward MYP's criterion-based subject work, and eventually DP's IA, EE and TOK components — tends to build habits early that do not need unlearning later. Even so, that is not a reason to introduce DP-style rigour into a seven-year-old's homework; the pacing has to match the child in front of the tutor, not the programme five years away.

Families relocating from other cities sometimes ask whether a Dehradun-based network can help mid-transition between programmes. It usually can, since matching is based on grade and subject rather than a fixed classroom, but the honest answer is that continuity depends on tutor availability at the time a family reaches out, not a guarantee made in advance.

MYP: ages 11 to 16, criterion-based subject work
DP: ages 16 to 19, IA, EE, TOK and final exams

Matching based on grade and subject, not a fixed classroom

contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits, Online Sessions and the Hybrid Option
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring can be reviewed in central Dehradun pockets — areas close enough to a tutor's travel route that regular, on-time sessions are realistic. For a younger PYP learner, there is a real argument for this: a consistent adult showing up at the same time each week, working at the kitchen table with the same books, builds routine in a way a screen sometimes does not for a six- or seven-year-old. Online tutoring, meanwhile, works from anywhere in the city and beyond, which matters for boarding-school families, for outstation or overseas parents who want visibility into sessions, and for vacation catch-up when a family is travelling.

Neither mode is automatically better. A family living well outside the reviewable home-tutoring pockets, or somewhere traffic makes a fixed weekly slot unreliable, is usually better served online even if their first instinct was to ask for someone to come home — an honest trade-off worth raising early rather than after a few missed sessions. A hybrid plan, most commonly a weekly home session plus a shorter online check-in for homework or a tricky unit-of-inquiry task, suits families who want the in-person routine but also occasional flexibility.

Whichever mode a family chooses, it is reviewed against tutor availability at the time of the request; nothing here is promised in advance of that check.

Online tutoring: available city-wide, no travel dependency
Hybrid: a weekly home session plus an online check-in

Best for boarding, outstation or travelling families: online

contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with specifics, not a general request for 'a good tutor'. IB Gram asks for the child's grade, current school, whether the need is literacy, numeracy or unit-of-inquiry support, and whether the family wants home, online or hybrid sessions. That request is checked against tutors' subject background, IB familiarity, and — for PYP specifically — comfort working with young children, since patience and classroom-style engagement matter as much as academic depth at this age.

A shortlist typically follows within a short window, subject to tutor availability for the requested area or time slot. Parents are encouraged to speak with a shortlisted tutor before committing, not just accept a name; a five-minute call usually reveals whether a tutor's communication style suits a particular child, especially a shy reader or an easily distracted eight-year-old. IB Gram treats this conversation as part of matching, not a formality to skip.

If the first match does not work — and sometimes it genuinely does not, because a child's classroom personality does not translate the same way one-on-one — the process allows for a tutor change without treating it as a failure. Match quality is judged over the first two to three sessions, not assumed correct from a resume. This flexibility exists precisely because subject expertise alone does not guarantee a good working relationship with a nine-year-old who has had a long school day already.

contentBlocks.heading: Before Any Tutor Meets Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Vetting for a PYP tutor is not identical to vetting a Diploma Programme specialist, and it should not be. Subject depth matters less here than it does for, say, a Math AA HL request; what matters more is verified academic background, some demonstrated understanding of how PYP's inquiry-based classroom actually works, and communication that suits young children specifically — not just competence with the material, but the ability to hold a seven-year-old's attention for forty-five minutes without losing the thread of a lesson.

IB Gram checks a tutor's academic qualifications, relevant teaching or tutoring experience, and familiarity with IB-specific ideas: concept-based learning, the learner profile, criterion-related assessment, and academic honesty expectations that apply even to a nine-year-old's project work. Tutors are expected to know the difference between guiding a child through a unit-of-inquiry task and doing the thinking for them, since the latter defeats the purpose of PYP assessment and, frankly, does not help the child in the next unit.

None of this produces a public rating or a number attached to a tutor's profile — IB Gram does not publish tutor counts, ratings or guaranteed outcomes, and would rather a parent judge fit from an actual conversation and the first few sessions than from a badge. What is checked, and how a tutor is expected to behave around academic honesty specifically, is something IB Gram will explain directly if a parent asks.

What a tutor can genuinely offer is familiarity with the kind of coursework and reporting cycles common to schools in that cluster — built from experience working with multiple families in the area — not privileged information about any single school's internal assessment.

contentBlocks.heading: Four Weeks In: What Progress Actually Looks Like
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram will not promise a grade jump, a particular reading level by a set date, or any guaranteed outcome — that kind of promise does not fit how a seven- or ten-year-old actually learns, and any tutor who makes it should raise a flag rather than reassure a parent. What can be promised instead is visibility: a parent-facing note after each session, or at minimum each week, stating what was covered, what the child found difficult, and what is planned next.

By the end of four weeks, a parent should be able to point to something concrete: a reading level that has moved from hesitant to reasonably fluent on grade-appropriate text, a numeracy gap that has closed on a specific operation, or a unit-of-inquiry project the child can now explain in their own words rather than copying from a worksheet. If none of that is visible after a month, that is a legitimate reason to raise it directly with IB Gram rather than assuming the child simply needs more time — sometimes they do, but sometimes the tutor is not the right fit, and four weeks is usually enough to tell the difference.

One honest limitation worth stating plainly: PYP carries no external exam to benchmark against, unlike DP's May and November sessions later in a student's schooling. Progress here is judged against the school's own reporting cycle and the tutor's direct observation, which asks more of a parent's trust in the process than a mock-exam score would. That is simply the nature of assessment at this stage, not a gap in how the tutoring is run.

Four-week markers: reading fluency, closed numeracy gaps, independent explanation of a unit project
A direct route to raise concerns if progress is not visible

contentBlocks.heading: Getting an IB PYP Tutor Started in Dehradun
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is simpler than most parents expect, and it does not require deciding everything upfront. Share the child's grade or age, current school if comfortable naming it, the specific concern — reading, numeracy, writing, or a particular unit-of-inquiry struggle — and a rough sense of whether home, online or hybrid sessions suit the household's schedule and location within Dehradun. From there, expect a shortlist rather than a single name, subject to who is actually free that week. Speaking with a shortlisted tutor briefly before the first paid session is worth doing every time, even if it feels like an extra step; a five-minute conversation about the child's personality and current struggles tells a parent more than a tutor's stated experience does on its own. First sessions are diagnostic, not a demonstration lesson, and the plan that comes out of it should be specific enough to act on within a week.

Families comparing options from Chandigarh, Ludhiana or Delhi, or families local to Dehradun who are simply unsure whether their area qualifies for home tutoring, can ask directly rather than guessing — service-area fit is checked case by case, not assumed from a locality name alone. faqs.question: What is the difference between IB PYP and just regular tutoring for a young child?
faqs.answer: Regular tutoring for a young child often focuses on getting through homework or drilling a weak topic. IB PYP tutoring works differently because PYP itself works differently: assessment is concept-based and tied to a unit of inquiry rather than a fixed syllabus, and children are expected to explain their thinking, not just produce a correct answer. A tutor unfamiliar with this approach may over-correct toward rote practice, which can actually work against how the child is being assessed at school. IB Gram matches based on PYP familiarity specifically, not general tutoring experience alone.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram offer home tutoring in every part of Dehradun?
faqs.answer: No, and it would be dishonest to say otherwise. Home tutoring requests can be reviewed across central pockets — Rajpur Road, Dalanwala, Mussoorie Road, Vasant Vihar and Prem Nagar, along with nearby areas like Jakhan, Ballupur and EC Road — because these sit within a range a tutor can reliably travel each week. Outside these pockets, or in areas where traffic makes a fixed weekly slot unreliable, online tutoring is the more realistic option. It is worth asking directly rather than assuming either way, since availability also depends on which tutors are free at the time.

faqs.question: How much does an IB PYP tutor in Dehradun cost?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by tutor experience, mode (home tutoring generally costs more than online because of travel time), session length and how many sessions a week the family wants. IB Gram does not publish a single fixed rate because a fair price depends on these specifics rather than a flat citywide number. When a family submits a request, shortlisted tutors' fee expectations are shared upfront before any commitment, so there are no surprises after the first session. Parents comparing home and online options should factor in that the fee difference between the two can be meaningful over a school term.

faqs.question: My child is shy and does not talk much in class. Will that make tutoring harder?
faqs.answer: It is worth mentioning at the matching stage rather than after a few awkward sessions. A shy child often needs a tutor who slows down, asks smaller questions, and does not expect immediate verbal answers to the kind of open-ended prompts a PYP unit of inquiry uses. This is exactly the sort of fit issue a short parent-tutor call before the first paid session is meant to catch. If a match still is not working after two or three sessions despite genuine effort on both sides, changing tutors is a reasonable next step, not an admission of failure.

faqs.question: Can a tutor really help with something as open-ended as a unit of inquiry?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the help looks different from subject tutoring. A tutor cannot hand a child the 'answer' to an inquiry task, since PYP assessment is built around the child's own thinking and academic honesty expectations apply even at this age. What a tutor can do is ask better questions than a busy evening at home usually allows, help the child organise scattered ideas into a structure, and check that written work actually reflects what the child understands rather than what a parent typed for them. That distinction is worth being clear about before sessions start.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring actually effective for a primary-age child, or is that mainly for older students?
faqs.answer: It works for primary-age children too, though the session usually needs to be shorter and more interactive than an online DP session — think twenty-five to thirty minutes with frequent small tasks, not a long lecture-style call. It suits boarding families, households managing a tight evening schedule, and vacation periods when a family is travelling but does not want a break in reading practice. For a child who needs the routine of someone physically present, home tutoring is generally the better starting point where it can be reviewed; online is not a lesser option, just a different one.

faqs.question: What happens if we are not happy with the tutor after starting?
faqs.answer: Say so directly and early rather than waiting out a term hoping it improves on its own. IB Gram treats the first two to three sessions as a trial window precisely because fit between a young child and a tutor is not always obvious from a resume or a first call. A mismatch gets addressed by proposing an alternative tutor rather than treating the original match as final. This is a normal part of the process, not an exception, and raising it early is far easier to act on than raising it after months of a routine that was not working.

faqs.question: Do you work with international or boarding schools directly?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not affiliated with any school, boarding or day, in Dehradun or elsewhere, unless a specific page states otherwise. What the network does have is experience working with families whose children attend schools across the Rajpur Road, Central Dehradun and West Dehradun clusters, which means familiarity with common reporting cycles and school-timing patterns in those areas — not any formal relationship with the schools themselves. Parents are welcome to name their child's school for scheduling purposes; it does not imply partnership.

faqs.question: Our family is relocating to Dehradun from Chandigarh mid-year. Can tutoring help with the transition?
faqs.answer: It can, though the honest answer depends on how different the two schools' approaches to PYP actually are, since implementation varies even within the same programme. A tutor can help a child adjust to new command-term expectations, a different unit-of-inquiry theme sequence, and unfamiliar classroom routines faster than the child would adjust alone. Starting sessions a few weeks before the move, where the family's schedule allows it, tends to work better than starting only after arrival, when everything else is also new at once. Online sessions from Chandigarh beforehand are a practical way to begin.

faqs.question: How do you decide between home tutoring and online for a PYP-age child specifically?
faqs.answer: Location within Dehradun is the first filter — home tutoring is only reviewed for central pockets like Rajpur Road, Dalanwala and Vasant Vihar and areas near them, because a tutor's weekly travel has to be realistic. Within that, age and temperament matter: a younger child, or one who needs consistent in-person routine, usually does better with home sessions where they are reviewable; an older PYP child comfortable with a screen, or a family managing boarding or travel schedules, often does fine online. Neither is a default answer, and the right one usually becomes clear after describing the actual situation.

heroTitle: IB DP Tutoring in Delhi, Built Around Your Evening
heroSubtitle: For Delhi families preparing for the May 2026 or November 2026 IB Diploma sessions, IB Gram matches students with tutors who know Math AA/AI, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A, and can work around school timings, home tutoring in select South Delhi pockets, or online sessions anywhere in the city.
introSummary: It's 8 pm on a school night in Vasant Vihar, and a Grade 11 student still has an unfinished Math AA HL problem set due before the next class discussion. This is the ordinary reason families start searching for an IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutor in Delhi, not a crisis, just a gap between how a subject is taught at school and how much practice a particular student needs before the May or November exam session. IB Gram matches Delhi students with tutors for DP subjects, IA and EE support, mock revision and past-paper practice, arranged around each family's evening.

contentBlocks.heading: The Shape of DP Tutoring Demand in Delhi
contentBlocks.body: Delhi's demand for DP tutoring is not uniform, and treating it as one market misses how differently families approach it. Embassy postings and international school enrolments cluster around Chanakyapuri, while established South Delhi pockets such as Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash and Saket send a steady stream of requests for tutors who can visit in the evening. Families further out, in Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad, tend to ask for online support by default, because a two-hour round trip for a ninety-minute session rarely survives a second term. What is fairly constant across all of these groups is the subject mix: depth in Math AA HL or Math AI HL, Physics HL/SL, Chemistry HL/SL and Economics, alongside English A and humanities writing that schools mark on IB rubrics rather than CBSE or ICSE ones. Assignment planning matters as much as subject teaching. A student juggling an IA deadline, a TOK presentation and a school hockey commitment needs a tutor who can sequence the work, not just explain the content twice. Some families come early, before an MYP submission turns into a crisis; others only notice a gap after a mock paper returns with a mark nobody expected in Physics or a thin essay structure in Economics. Both are normal starting points, and neither is too late to act on.

contentBlocks.heading: Math AA, Math AI, the Sciences and the Writing Subjects
contentBlocks.body: Six subjects account for most of the tutoring requests IB Gram sees from Delhi: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics and English A. Math AA and Math AI are not interchangeable, and a family that has picked the wrong one for their child's actual strengths will keep struggling no matter how good the tutor is, so matching the subject to the student's aptitude for calculus-heavy proof work versus applied modelling matters before any tutoring plan is written. Physics and Chemistry students in Delhi mostly ask for help closer to Paper 2 and Paper 3 style questions, where marks are lost to method rather than final answers, and a tutor who marks like an IB examiner rather than a school teacher tends to close that gap faster. And Economics tutoring in Delhi leans heavily on essay structure: evaluation paragraphs, diagram labelling and the command terms IB examiners actually reward, which is different from how the subject is taught for board exams. English A support covers both the literary analysis expected in internal assessments and the paper-based commentary work, and Delhi students juggling English alongside three other HL subjects often need help with time allocation as much as content. An IB DP tutor in Delhi worth hiring should be able to talk about which paper a student is losing marks on, not offer a generic doubt-solving session with no plan behind it.
items: Math AA HL for proof-heavy calculus routes, Math AI HL for applied and modelling routes
Physics and Chemistry: Paper 2/3 method marks over final-answer marks
Economics: evaluation paragraphs, diagrams and command-term precision
English A: internal assessment analysis plus paper-based commentary timing
Subject fit checked before a tutoring plan is written, not after

contentBlocks.heading: How PYP, MYP and DP Connect Across Grade 1 to 12
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram supports the full run from Grade 1 to Grade 12 in Delhi, which in IB terms spans the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19. A parent searching specifically for an IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutor is usually thinking about the last two years of school, but the earlier stages shape how ready a student is for it. PYP habits around inquiry and self-management either transfer into MYP or need rebuilding once assignments get longer and less scaffolded. MYP is where subject-specific writing and early IA-style thinking should start forming, well before DP officially begins, and families who wait until Grade 11 to address a weak MYP foundation in, say, mathematics or written English often spend the first DP term catching up rather than progressing. DP itself carries its own internal structure: HL and SL subject choices, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service alongside a full academic timetable. A tutor who has only ever taught DP subjects in isolation, without understanding what a student's MYP years should have covered, sometimes overestimates how much can be fixed in one term. IB Gram's matching considers where a student sits on this continuum, not only their current grade.
items: PYP (ages 3-12): inquiry habits and early self-management
MYP (ages 11-16): subject-specific writing, early IA-style thinking
DP (ages 16-19): HL/SL choices, Extended Essay, TOK, CAS

contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits, Online Sessions and the Hybrid Middle Ground
contentBlocks.body: Home tutoring in Delhi through IB Gram may be possible in select South Delhi pockets, central Delhi and nearby residential areas, arranged around school timings and subject to tutor availability and travel distance. It is not offered as a blanket service across the whole city, and pretending otherwise would set the wrong expectation from the start. Online tutoring, by contrast, is available across Delhi for every supported IB programme and subject, and it tends to be the better choice whenever the priority is a specific subject specialist rather than proximity: a strong Math AI HL tutor who lives across town is more useful over video call than a generalist who happens to be nearby. Many Delhi families end up choosing a hybrid arrangement without planning to. A student might see a home tutor twice a week for ongoing subject teaching and add an online session before a mock exam when a particular concept needs a specialist the local pool does not have. Short revision cycles before school mocks work well online because they do not require building a long-term local relationship. Longer weekly plans for a student rebuilding foundations across a full year can go either way. So the honest answer is that traffic and travel time should decide the mode, more than any general preference for one option over the other.

Online tutoring: available citywide, any supported DP subject
Hybrid: home teaching plus an online specialist before mocks
Short revision cycles suit online; year-long rebuilds suit either
Traffic and travel time decide the mode, not preference alone

contentBlocks.heading: From Request to Shortlist: What Matching Involves
contentBlocks.body: Matching starts with specifics, not a general request for 'a good tutor'. IB Gram asks which subject and level (Math AA HL versus Math AI HL changes the shortlist entirely), what the student's current grade and school assessment cycle look like, and whether the family needs home tutoring, online tutoring, or is open to either depending on tutor fit. From there, a small number of tutors whose subject background and exam-board familiarity match the request are proposed, rather than a long list a parent has to filter through alone. A first session is treated as a diagnostic, not a sales pitch: the tutor reviews recent schoolwork, asks about the IA or EE topic if one exists, and identifies where the actual gap sits, whether that is content, exam technique, or pacing under time pressure. Families should expect a plan for the coming four weeks out of that first session, not vague reassurance. At the four-week mark, the honest check is whether the student's independent work has changed: are they attempting past paper questions without being told to, is homework arriving with fewer blank sections, has a teacher commented on improved classwork. If none of that has shifted, the right response is not to keep the arrangement running out of politeness. It is to revisit the match, sometimes with a different tutor for the same subject, because personality fit and teaching pace matter as much as qualifications on paper.

contentBlocks.heading: South Delhi, Central Delhi and the NCR Commute Question
contentBlocks.body: Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri are where most home-tutoring requests for DP subjects originate, and it is worth being honest about why: these are areas with a concentration of international-curriculum families and, in Chanakyapuri's case, proximity to schools like The British School New Delhi and the American Embassy School. Nearby pockets, Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh, get covered on a case-by-case basis depending on which tutor is available and how the traffic pattern between the two points actually behaves at the time a session would run, since Delhi's evening traffic does not treat every few kilometres equally. A family in Green Park asking for a 6 pm session should expect a different answer than one asking for a 4 pm slot, purely because of school pickup and office-return traffic overlapping in the late afternoon. Families in Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad are technically outside the areas where home tutoring is realistic, and IB Gram does not pretend a tutor can cross that distance twice a week reliably. Online tutoring is the practical answer for these NCR families, and it is not a downgrade for subject teaching: a Math AI HL tutor is equally effective on a screen as in a living room for most of what DP tutoring actually involves, which is worked examples, past-paper walkthroughs and feedback on written work.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Shortlisted
contentBlocks.body: Every tutor proposed for a Delhi DP tutoring request is reviewed against a specific set of criteria before being shortlisted, not judged on a general impression. IB Gram checks subject-matter qualifications relevant to the exact DP subject and level requested; a Math AA HL request is not filled with a tutor whose background is in Math AI, even if both are labelled 'IB Maths' loosely. Exam-board familiarity is checked separately from subject knowledge: understanding how IB mark schemes reward method, how IA and EE are assessed against official criteria, and how TOK essays are structured are different skills from simply knowing the content. Teaching experience specific to the IB syllabus, rather than general tutoring experience adapted on the fly, is treated as a meaningful signal, because DP assessment language (command terms, rubric bands, moderation) is not intuitive even to a strong subject expert coming from a different curriculum. But none of this is expressed as a score or a star rating, because IB Gram does not publish invented ratings or manufactured testimonials. What a parent gets instead is a clear account of a tutor's relevant background for the specific request, and the option to ask direct questions before the first session is booked. If a tutor's fit does not hold up once teaching actually starts, the review process continues past the first shortlist rather than stopping there.

Exam-board familiarity assessed separately from raw subject knowledge
IB-specific teaching experience weighted over general tutoring experience

contentBlocks.heading: Where DP Is Taught in Delhi, and What That Means for Tutoring
contentBlocks.body: Delhi's Diploma Programme cohort is concentrated in a handful of schools, including The British School New Delhi and the American Embassy School, both in Chanakyapuri, and DPS International in Saket. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated; naming them here is about cohort context, not endorsement. Students from these schools tend to arrive with fairly similar structural expectations, HL/SL subject splits, TOK and EE deadlines set by the school calendar, and CAS logging, but their individual gaps vary a great deal even within the same school and the same subject. Two students from the same Chanakyapuri school taking Math AA HL can need completely different tutoring: one might be strong on technique but slow under exam time pressure, the other might understand concepts but lose marks on notation the school's internal marking is lenient about but IB moderation is not. A tutor familiar with a particular school's assessment calendar has a practical advantage, knowing when mocks land, when the EE first draft is due, when TOK presentations are scheduled, because it lets tutoring line up with school deadlines instead of competing against them. Where a family's school is not in this list, the same principle still applies: sharing the school's internal deadlines and grading habits with a matched tutor early makes the first few weeks noticeably more useful than treating tutoring and school as separate tracks.

contentBlocks.heading: Fees, Fit and Being Honest About What Changes in a Month
contentBlocks.body: Fees for DP tutoring in Delhi depend on subject, level, tutor experience and whether the arrangement is home or online, and IB Gram does not publish a single fixed rate because a Math AA HL specialist and a general English A tutor are not priced the same way, nor should they be. What a parent can reasonably ask upfront is how the fee structure works for the specific subject and tutor being proposed, and whether it changes for exam-season intensives versus regular weekly sessions. Value in DP tutoring is not really about price per hour; it is about whether the sessions change what a student does independently between them. A tutor who explains a concept well but leaves no shift in how the student attempts homework or past papers on their own is not adding much, regardless of the fee. It is worth saying plainly: tutoring does not fix a scheduling problem the family has not addressed. A student with four HL subjects, a sport commitment and a two-hour daily commute has a limited number of usable hours, and no tutor changes that arithmetic. The honest role of tutoring here is to make the hours that do exist count for more, not to manufacture additional ones. Starting late, in the last few months before a May exam session with weak foundations, also limits what is realistically achievable, and a tutor who promises otherwise is not being straight with the family.
items: Fees vary by subject, level, tutor experience and mode; ask upfront for the specific tutor proposed
Exam-season intensives usually priced differently from regular weekly sessions
Value equals change in independent work between sessions, not price per hour
Tutoring cannot fix a schedule with no usable hours left
Starting a few months before May exams with weak foundations limits outcomes

contentBlocks.heading: Starting the Search for the Right Tutor in Delhi
contentBlocks.body: Starting is simpler than most families expect once the noise of choosing between many options is taken out of it. The useful first step is naming specifics: the exact subject and level (Math AA HL or Math AI HL, not just 'maths'), the current grade, whether the school session is closer to May 2026 or November 2026, and whether home tutoring in a South Delhi or central pocket is realistic on the family's schedule or online support fits better. From there, IB Gram proposes a small shortlist matched on subject background and exam-board familiarity rather than a long list to sort through. The first session functions as a working diagnostic, reviewing recent schoolwork, checking the IA or EE topic if one is already assigned, and setting a concrete four-week plan rather than an open-ended commitment. Parents should feel free to ask direct questions at this stage: what the tutor has taught before, how they mark practice papers, how they would handle a student who is behind on an EE draft. A mismatch after the first few sessions is not a failure to plan around; it is normal, and the right response is a fast re-match rather than persevering out of politeness or sunk cost. Delhi's traffic and school calendars will not get simpler on their own, so the plan that survives is usually the one built around them from week one, not adjusted after the fact.
items: Name the exact subject, level and target exam session first
State home vs online preference and the realistic weekly schedule
Expect a small matched shortlist, not an open list
First session sets a concrete four-week plan
Re-match quickly if fit is off; no sunk-cost persistence

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP tutor in Delhi cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject, the level (HL usually costs more than SL because the syllabus and marking depth are heavier), the tutor's experience, and whether sessions are home-based or online. IB Gram does not fix one citywide rate because a Math AA HL specialist and a general English A tutor are priced differently, and that difference is legitimate rather than arbitrary. The practical approach is to ask for the fee structure of the specific tutor proposed for your subject, and to check whether it changes during exam-season intensives compared with regular weekly sessions.

faqs.question: Is online IB DP tutoring actually as effective as home tutoring?
faqs.answer: For most DP subject teaching, yes: worked examples, past-paper walkthroughs and feedback on written IA or essay drafts translate well to a screen. Where home tutoring has a real edge is with younger students who need more structure to stay focused, or families who specifically want a tutor building rapport with the student in person. For NCR families in Gurugram, Noida or Ghaziabad, online is usually the only realistic option twice a week, and it is not a compromise for subject-level teaching in Physics, Chemistry, Economics or the Maths routes.

faqs.question: Can I get a home tutor in Vasant Vihar or Saket for DP subjects?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring may be possible in these South Delhi pockets, subject to which tutor is available for your specific subject and how their schedule and travel pattern line up with the time slot you need. It is not guaranteed for every subject or every timing, particularly for less common subject-level combinations. If a home match cannot be arranged quickly for the exact slot you want, online tutoring is available immediately for the same subject and level, and many families end up combining both rather than waiting for one option.

faqs.question: My child is confused between Math AA and Math AI. Can a tutor help decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is worth sorting out before committing to a term of tutoring in the wrong route. Math AA suits students comfortable with abstract proof-style work and calculus depth; Math AI suits students who work better with applied, modelling-based problems and technology use. A tutor can review recent classwork and a few practice questions from each route to see which one matches how your child actually thinks, rather than which one sounds more prestigious. Getting this decision right early saves far more time than any amount of tutoring can recover later in the DP.

faqs.question: What happens in the first tutoring session?
faqs.answer: The first session works like a diagnostic rather than a lesson delivered at full speed. The tutor goes through recent schoolwork, asks about the IA or EE topic if one has already been assigned, and figures out whether marks are being lost to weak concepts, poor exam technique, or running out of time under paper conditions. By the end of it, you should have a concrete plan for the next four weeks, not a general sense that things will improve. If that plan does not come out of the first session, that itself tells you something about the match.

faqs.question: What if there is no improvement after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Four weeks is usually enough to see whether a student is attempting past papers without prompting, submitting homework with fewer blank sections, or getting different feedback from their school teacher. If none of that has shifted, the honest response is to revisit the match rather than continue out of politeness. Sometimes the subject knowledge is fine but the teaching pace or personality fit is not, and a different tutor for the same subject solves it faster than persisting with an arrangement that is not moving the student forward.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with IA, EE and TOK, or only subject content?
faqs.answer: Both are covered, and for DP students the assessment support usually matters more than content-only coaching in the final two years. Tutors work on IA planning against the specific subject's assessment criteria, EE mentoring on structuring an argument and managing the research question, TOK support for structured thinking across the exhibition and essay, and general school assignment planning alongside mock revision and past-paper practice. A tutor who only teaches content and ignores how DP actually grades this coursework is missing a large share of where marks are gained or lost.

faqs.question: We are starting late, only a few months before the May 2026 exams. Is it worth it?
faqs.answer: It can be, but the honest answer depends on how weak the foundations are and how many subjects need attention at once. A few months is enough to sharpen exam technique, close specific gaps in one or two subjects, and improve IA or EE drafts that are already underway. It is not enough to rebuild two years of missed foundational content across four HL subjects from nothing. A first diagnostic session will usually make clear which of these situations applies, and a tutor should say so plainly rather than promising a turnaround that timing does not support.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors if the first one is not the right fit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is treated as a normal part of the process rather than an inconvenience. Subject knowledge is only part of a good match; teaching pace, communication style and how a tutor handles a student who is anxious about a subject all matter too. If a mismatch becomes clear in the first few sessions, tell IB Gram directly rather than waiting it out. A faster re-match usually costs less time overall than persevering with a tutor who is not working for the student.

faqs.question: Do you cover schools like DPS International Saket or the American Embassy School specifically?
faqs.answer: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with DPS International Saket, The British School New Delhi, the American Embassy School or any other school. Tutors are matched to a student's subject, level and school assessment calendar rather than to a school partnership. Because a meaningful share of Delhi's DP cohort attends these schools, tutors familiar with their general timelines for mocks, EE deadlines and TOK submissions are available, but that familiarity comes from experience with students from these schools, not from any formal school relationship.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring available in areas outside South Delhi, like Noida or Gurugram?
faqs.answer: Not as home tutoring in the way it can be arranged in South Delhi or central Delhi pockets; the distance and traffic between those cities and where tutors are typically based make a reliable weekly commute impractical. Online tutoring is available across Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad for every supported DP subject, and for subject-heavy teaching like Math AA HL, Physics or Economics essay work, the format makes little practical difference. Families in these cities are matched the same way as Delhi families: by subject, level and schedule, just without a home-visit option.

heroTitle: MYP Tutoring in Delhi, Planned Around Your Commute
heroSubtitle: For Grade 6 to Grade 10 students, covering eAssessment prep, the Personal Project, IA-style investigations and school assignments — with home tutoring where South Delhi travel makes sense, and online tutoring for everyone else, including families in Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad.
introSummary: Searching for an IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) tutor in Delhi usually means one of two problems: a Grade 7 or 8 student who needs steady criterion-based practice, or a Grade 10 student staring down eAssessment and the Personal Project with a few months left. Either way, the tutor needs to know MYP assessment language specifically, not just general IB experience picked up from DP tuition. IB Gram matches families across Delhi — home tutoring in pockets like South Delhi where travel is realistic, online tutoring everywhere else — based on grade, subject and how the school actually assesses.

contentBlocks.heading: Getting MYP Help Without Losing Every Evening to Traffic
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi is not a city where you casually add a six o'clock tutoring slot to a teenager's week. If school ends around 3:30 and the drive from Chanakyapuri toward Vasant Vihar or Saket eats forty minutes on a bad evening, a home tutor crossing town for one hour can show up late, tired, or not at all. That's worth planning around before subjects or syllabus even enter the conversation.

This is where mode matters more than most parents expect. For families in South Delhi pockets close to the tutor, home tutoring works well — there's value in someone sitting across the table while a Grade 8 student works through a Criteria B investigation. For everyone else, and for subjects where the right specialist isn't local, online tutoring closes the gap without losing ninety minutes to the Ring Road.

MYP students in Delhi are typically Grade 6 to Grade 10, working through criterion-based units, interdisciplinary tasks, and, for Grade 10s, the Personal Project. Add school deadlines and an ordinary Delhi weekday's unpredictability, and the real question isn't only whether a tutor is good — it's whether the arrangement can run every week without quietly falling apart by week three.

contentBlocks.heading: Where MYP Students Usually Need the Most Help
contentBlocks.body:
Ask ten Delhi parents what their MYP child struggles with and you'll get variations on the same handful of things: Mathematics problem sets that suddenly expect reasoning and communication, not just a correct answer; Science investigations that need a proper method and analysis section; and English A responses that read like summaries instead of analysis. None of this is unusual — it's exactly what Criteria A to D are designed to test.

Individuals and Societies work leans on source evaluation and structured argument, which trips up students used to fact-recall from earlier grades. Grade 10 brings the Personal Project, an independent piece of work that many students underestimate until the process journal is due and there's not much written in it. A tutor's job here isn't to write it for them — it's to keep the timeline honest and the reflection genuine.

There's also a forward-looking pattern we see often in Delhi: families using MYP years to build a base in Math AA, Math AI, Physics, Chemistry or Economics before Diploma subject selection arrives. That head start matters more than it sounds — a student comfortable with algebraic reasoning by Grade 10 has a real advantage picking Math AA HL two years later instead of scrambling into it unprepared.
items: Mathematics — Criteria A to D, not just right answers
Sciences — investigation design and analysis write-ups
English A — textual analysis over summary
Individuals & Societies — source evaluation and argument structure

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor Actually Gets Matched to Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
The process starts with specifics, not a form asking for vague preferences. We need the grade, the subject, the school's curriculum board where relevant, and — honestly the most useful bit — what's actually going wrong right now. 'Struggling with Physics' tells us little. 'Can't structure a Criteria C investigation write-up' tells us exactly who to shortlist.

From there we shortlist tutors who've specifically worked with MYP assessment criteria, not general IB tutors who mostly teach Diploma content and treat MYP as a warm-up. The first session is a diagnostic more than a lesson — the tutor reviews recent schoolwork, asks questions, and works out where the actual gap sits before deciding what to teach next week.

You get a short note after that first session describing what was found and what the plan looks like. If the fit feels wrong — personality, pace, teaching style, it happens — you can switch within the first couple of sessions without an argument about it. Matching well matters more than matching fast, though we try to do both.
items: share grade, subject and school board upfront
shortlisting favours MYP-specific experience over general IB tutoring
session one is a diagnostic, not a lecture
a short note after session one on what was found
free switch within the first couple of sessions if needed

contentBlocks.heading: South and Central Delhi Pockets We Can Reach for Home Sessions
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring works best where the tutor doesn't lose an hour of the lesson just getting there. In Delhi, that realistically means South and Central pockets: Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket and Chanakyapuri, along with Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park and Jor Bagh. If you're in one of these areas, ask about home tutoring first — it often turns out to be workable.

Outside these pockets, home tutoring becomes a gamble against traffic more than a teaching decision, and we'd rather say that plainly than promise something that falls apart by the third session. Families in Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad — genuinely close on a map, genuinely far in rush hour — are almost always better served online, where the tutor's location stops mattering and subject expertise becomes the variable worth optimising for.

This isn't a rule we apply mechanically. A student five minutes from a tutor in Saket gets a different offer than one an hour away in outer Delhi, even though both are technically 'in Delhi.' We'll say honestly whether home tutoring is realistic for your address before recommending it, rather than booking a slot that quietly stops happening after two weeks.

contentBlocks.heading: From PYP to the Diploma — Where MYP Sits in Between
contentBlocks.body:
The IB isn't one exam, it's three programmes stitched together, and where your child sits changes what 'good tutoring' even means. The Primary Years Programme runs roughly age 3 to 12, built around inquiry rather than subject silos. The Middle Years Programme, roughly age 11 to 16, is where your child likely is now — criterion-based, subject-specific, and considerably more structured than PYP.

The Diploma Programme, age 16 to 19, is a different animal again: Higher Level and Standard Level subjects, external exam grades from 1 to 7, an Extended Essay and TOK alongside six subjects. Parents sometimes ask us to prepare an MYP student 'DP-style,' and we'd gently push back — the assessment language, the criteria, even the vocabulary examiners expect are genuinely different between the two programmes.

What does carry over is the habit MYP is meant to build: structured, criteria-aware written work, and the eAssessment format at the end of Grade 10 — an on-screen exam quite unlike a traditional board paper. Students who've never sat a timed on-screen assessment before Grade 10 often need a session or two just on the format, separate from the subject content itself.
items: Primary Years Programme — roughly age 3 to 12
Middle Years Programme — roughly age 11 to 16
Diploma Programme — roughly age 16 to 19
MYP eAssessment — on-screen format at the end of Grade 10

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Checked Before a Tutor Is Introduced to You
contentBlocks.body:
A resume with 'IB experience' printed on it doesn't tell us much on its own. So before any tutor is offered to a family, there's a subject-matter interview specifically about MYP — can they explain what a Criteria B response actually needs, do they know the difference between a Personal Project process journal and a DP Extended Essay outline, that kind of practical, hard-to-fake detail.

We also ask for a short sample teaching walkthrough — not a rehearsed pitch, but a real explanation of how they'd approach a specific weak spot, like a Grade 9 student who keeps losing marks on evaluation in Individuals and Societies. Identity and background details are verified before any home visit is arranged, which matters more in a city where 'nearby' can still mean a stranger entering your home.

None of this guarantees chemistry between tutor and student — that's still something only the first session reveals. But it does mean the shortlist you're offered has already cleared a subject-competence bar, not just a general willingness to tutor. We also track feedback after sessions, so a tutor who consistently underdelivers doesn't stay on the shortlist by default.
items: subject-matter interview focused on MYP criteria, not general IB claims
sample teaching walkthrough on a real weak spot
identity and background verification before home visits
ongoing feedback tracked after sessions
no guarantee of chemistry — that's tested in session one

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online, or a Mix — What Actually Works Here
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi families tend to land on one of three setups, and none is objectively 'better' — it depends on address, subject, and how the student actually concentrates. Home tutoring suits students who need someone physically present to stay on task, and it's realistic mainly in South and Central Delhi where travel time stays under control. Beyond that radius, it becomes unreliable fast.

Online tutoring removes the travel problem entirely and opens up the full pool of subject specialists, which matters a lot for something like Math AI HL groundwork or a strong Economics teacher who happens to live across town. Some students settle into it faster than parents expect; a few genuinely do better with a person in the room, and there's no shame in saying that upfront rather than discovering it after three wasted sessions.

Hybrid setups are common too — home tutoring for a subject where focus is the issue, online for one where expertise is the issue. Session rhythm also shifts by purpose: short, intensive blocks before a school mock, versus a slower weekly rhythm for a student rebuilding a shaky foundation from Grade 7 or 8 onward. We'll ask which situation you're actually in before recommending a shape.

online tutoring — available anywhere in Delhi and NCR
hybrid — home for focus, online for specialist subjects
short revision blocks before school mocks
longer weekly plans for rebuilding a weak foundation

contentBlocks.heading: Schools Whose MYP Calendars We See Often in Delhi
contentBlocks.body:
Certain school calendars come up repeatedly when Delhi parents get in touch — not because we're affiliated with them, but because their MYP timelines shape when families reach out. The British School New Delhi and American Embassy School, both in Chanakyapuri, run assessment cycles that tend to cluster requests around the same few weeks each term. DPS International Saket follows its own rhythm, slightly offset.

Knowing a school's general pattern helps us plan ahead — booking a Personal Project mentor before the process journal deadline creeps up, rather than after a student is already behind. It doesn't mean we know your child's specific school portal or internal deadlines; you'll still need to share those directly, and the tutor works from what you and the student provide rather than assuming.

IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. We are not officially affiliated with The British School New Delhi, American Embassy School, DPS International Saket, or any other school named on this page, unless specifically stated elsewhere. Students from many other Delhi and NCR schools running the MYP use these same tutors and the same matching process.
