contentBlocks.heading: What You Should Actually See After Four Weeks
contentBlocks.body:
We won't tell you a tutor guarantees a Level 7 or a particular grade before anyone has even met your child — anyone who promises that upfront is guessing, not assessing. What we will commit to is a process: a clear diagnostic in session one, a plan tied to your child's actual school criteria rather than a generic worksheet pack, and honesty about what's realistic in the time available.

By the fourth session, you should have a written update — not a vague 'going well,' but something specific: which criterion improved, what's still shaky, what the next few weeks focus on. If a student started in October chasing a mock exam in December, we'll say plainly whether that's a comfortable runway or a tight one, because starting late genuinely does limit what any tutor can rebuild in time.

If four weeks in there's been no real movement, that's a conversation worth having directly rather than quietly continuing out of politeness — sometimes it's pace, sometimes it's fit, occasionally the student needs a different kind of support altogether. Changing tutors at that point isn't a failure; it's the system working as intended.
items: no promised grade or score before session one
written update after every fourth session, not a vague check-in
honesty about tight timelines, including late starts
criteria-specific plan, not a generic worksheet pack
changing tutors is normal, not a failure

contentBlocks.heading: What Happens if You Reach Out This Week
contentBlocks.body:
Getting started doesn't need a long form or a sales call. Tell us the grade, the subject, the school, and roughly what's going wrong — a Personal Project stuck at the proposal stage, a Grade 8 student losing marks on Criteria D reflection, whatever the real issue is. That detail is what lets us shortlist a tutor who's actually dealt with it before, instead of a generalist figuring it out on your child's time.

We shortlist within a short window, though exact timing depends on subject and tutor availability at that moment — some subjects have more specialists free than others in a given week. The first session gets scheduled around school timings, not the other way round, because a tutoring slot that fights the school day rarely survives past a fortnight.

With May and November 2026 school assessment cycles ahead, earlier starts leave more room for the Personal Project and eAssessment prep to happen without last-minute pressure. That's not urgency for its own sake — a student who begins in August has considerably more breathing room than one who starts in March, and we'd rather you know that now than after the fact.
items: share grade, subject, school and the actual problem
shortlist ready within a short window, subject to availability
first session scheduled around school timings, not against them
you decide after session one whether to continue
earlier starts leave more room before assessment cycles

faqs.question: How much does an IB MYP tutor in Delhi cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on subject, grade, whether it's home or online, and the tutor's experience — a Grade 6 general session and a Grade 10 Personal Project specialist aren't priced the same, and home tutoring in South Delhi typically costs more than online given the travel involved. We don't quote one number upfront because it would be misleading; you'll get an exact figure once we know the subject and mode, usually within the first conversation, so there's no vague 'starting from' teaser to work around later.

faqs.question: Can you actually find a home tutor in Vasant Vihar or Greater Kailash?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes — these are among the pockets where home tutoring is most realistic for us, subject to which specific subject you need and tutor availability that week. If nobody suitable is free for home sessions right now, we'll say so plainly and offer online as the alternative rather than making you wait weeks for a slot that may not open up. Availability shifts, so the honest answer is 'likely, but let's check' rather than a blanket yes.

faqs.question: What if the tutor we're matched with isn't the right fit?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it's not something you need to push through politely. You can request a change within the first couple of sessions, no lengthy justification required — sometimes it's pace, sometimes teaching style, sometimes the student just doesn't open up to that particular person. We'd rather hear about it early than have three sessions of quiet disengagement before anyone says anything. A second match is arranged as quickly as availability allows.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for MYP, or is home tutoring better?
faqs.answer: Both work, for different students. Online tutoring gives access to a wider pool of subject specialists and removes travel entirely, which suits self-directed students well. Younger students, or ones who get distracted easily on a screen, sometimes concentrate better with a tutor physically present — that's a real trade-off, not a sales point either way. If you're unsure, we'll suggest based on the student's age and how they've responded to online classes at school so far.

faqs.question: What does MYP eAssessment preparation actually involve?
faqs.answer: MYP eAssessment is an on-screen exam at the end of Grade 10, and the format itself trips students up as much as the content does — navigating on-screen tools, managing time without a physical paper in front of them, structuring criterion-based responses under exam conditions. Preparation covers both: timed practice using the actual on-screen interface where possible, and criteria-specific feedback on written responses, alongside subject content review for whichever groups your child is being assessed in.

faqs.question: My child is starting the Personal Project — can a tutor help with that?
faqs.answer: Yes, though the help looks like mentoring, not ghostwriting — a tutor can guide topic selection, keep the process journal honest and regularly updated, and give feedback on structure and reflection quality. What they won't do is write the product or the report for your child; the Personal Project is meant to demonstrate independent skills, and an examiner can usually tell when it hasn't been. Starting the mentoring early, well before the deadline crunch, makes the biggest difference.

faqs.question: We live in Gurugram or Noida — can we still book a tutor through IB Gram?
faqs.answer: Yes, online. Home tutoring across NCR distances rarely stays reliable once you factor in Delhi traffic both ways, so for Gurugram, Noida and Ghaziabad families we typically recommend online sessions rather than promising home visits we can't consistently deliver. Subject access is actually broader this way too, since the tutor's location stops being a constraint. If a specific situation genuinely needs an in-person tutor, we'll say so honestly rather than force-fitting an online plan.

faqs.question: What happens if there's no real progress after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: We'd want to know, first — a written update after every fourth session is meant to surface exactly this, not hide it. If progress is genuinely stalled, the options are usually adjusting the plan, changing tutor, or in some cases addressing something upstream that isn't about tutoring at all, like burnout closer to exams. We won't keep billing sessions that clearly aren't working without flagging it, and a change of tutor at that stage is treated as routine, not a failure.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with the IB Organization or with my child's school?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform, not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate Organization, and not officially affiliated with schools like The British School New Delhi, American Embassy School or DPS International Saket unless specifically stated. Tutors are familiar with IB and MYP assessment expectations because of their teaching and tutoring background, not because of any institutional partnership. It's worth knowing that distinction upfront, rather than assuming a formal tie that doesn't exist.

introSummary: Parents searching for an IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) tutor in Delhi often assume the job is extra worksheets and homework supervision. It isn't, at least not if it's done well. PYP runs on Units of Inquiry, not chapter-by-chapter drilling, so a tutor who doesn't understand the programme's transdisciplinary themes can end up confusing a Grade 3 student more than helping. What actually works: a tutor who reinforces the same inquiry-based thinking the school uses, whether that's over home tutoring in South Delhi or online sessions from Grade 1 through Grade 5.

contentBlocks.heading: When a PYP Tutor Actually Helps, and When It's Overkill
contentBlocks.body:
Most Delhi parents who search for an IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) tutor are picturing something close to CBSE-style tuition: extra worksheets, chapter tests, a stricter version of what school already does. That is usually the wrong starting point. PYP runs on Units of Inquiry: six transdisciplinary themes a year, taught through inquiry rather than textbook chapters, and a tutor who doesn't understand that structure can end up teaching against the school's method instead of alongside it.

That doesn't mean tutoring is unnecessary. A Grade 2 student who is behind on reading fluency needs direct, structured practice, inquiry framework or not. A Grade 4 student preparing for a Unit of Inquiry presentation benefits from someone who can ask the right questions rather than hand over answers. Where support usually adds real value: reading and writing fluency in English A, number sense and problem-solving in Math, and confidence building before a Grade 5 exhibition.

Where it's genuinely overkill: a five-year-old in Nursery or KG who is developmentally on track rarely needs a formal tutor at all, and pushing academic drilling that early can work against what PYP is trying to build. Age and actual gaps should decide this, not habit.
items: Reading fluency and comprehension in English A
Number sense and problem-solving in Math
Confidence and structure before the Grade 5 exhibition
Support for Units of Inquiry projects and presentations
Not recommended for developmentally on-track Nursery or KG children

contentBlocks.heading: How We Match an IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) Tutor in Delhi to Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with a short call, not a form. We ask what school your child attends, which grade and Unit of Inquiry theme they're on, whether the concern is a specific subject (usually English or Math) or something broader like organisation and independent work habits. For younger children, we also ask how much parent involvement the family wants during sessions, a Grade 1 student often needs a parent or helper nearby, while a Grade 5 student usually doesn't.

From there we shortlist tutors based on grade band experience, not just IB familiarity in general. A tutor who has taught DP Economics is not automatically the right fit for a seven-year-old working through a Sharing the Planet unit; primary-age teaching is its own skill, closer to early years pedagogy than exam coaching. We look for tutors who have worked inside an inquiry-based classroom or IB-affiliated school, or who can demonstrate they understand the transdisciplinary approach in a trial session.

The first session is diagnostic, not instructional. The tutor spends most of it listening: reading a paragraph aloud with the student, working through a few Math problems, watching how the child approaches an open-ended question. What that reveals shapes the plan for the following weeks, which is reviewed with you afterward rather than assumed in advance.
items: Initial call covers school, grade and current Unit of Inquiry
Tutors shortlisted by grade-band experience, not IB familiarity alone
First session is diagnostic: reading, Math problem-solving, open-ended questions
Plan for following weeks shared with parents, not assumed upfront

contentBlocks.heading: Inside the PYP Framework: Where Students Usually Need Support
contentBlocks.body:
PYP doesn't split the day into Math period and Science period the way most Indian curricula do. Learning is organised around six transdisciplinary themes: Who We Are, Where We Are in Place and Time, How We Express Ourselves, How the World Works, How We Organise Ourselves, and Sharing the Planet. Language, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies, Arts, and Personal, Social and Physical Education (PSPE) are woven through each unit rather than taught as separate periods.

In practice, most tutoring requests in Delhi fall into two buckets. The first is Language: reading fluency, comprehension, and the writing structure PYP expects even from a Grade 3 student, since IB writing tasks ask for reasoning and reflection earlier than most CBSE or ICSE equivalents. The second is Mathematics, particularly number sense, place value, and word-problem reasoning, where a student can know the mechanics but struggle to explain their thinking, which is exactly what PYP assessment looks for.

Science and Social Studies support usually shows up around a specific unit, not as ongoing weekly tuition, since these are inquiry-driven and project-based. A tutor's job there is less about content delivery and more about helping a child structure research, ask better questions, and present findings clearly.
items: Language: reading fluency, comprehension, structured writing
Mathematics: number sense, place value, word-problem reasoning
Science and Social Studies support tied to the current unit
PSPE and Arts rarely need formal tutoring
Focus on explaining thinking, not just getting the right answer

contentBlocks.heading: From PYP to MYP to DP: What Comes Next for Delhi Students
contentBlocks.body:
A PYP student today is, on the IB continuum, three programmes away from IA and EE season. Delhi families sometimes ask about the same tutor across grades. Someone who works with a family from Grade 2 through Grade 10 stays alongside a Middle Years Programme (ages 11 to 16) transition, and eventually a Diploma Programme (ages 16 to 19) run that brings Math AA or Math AI, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, and English A into the picture, along with Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, and Theory of Knowledge.

None of that is urgent for a PYP parent right now, and we won't pretend otherwise. What matters at this stage is different: independent reading habits, comfort with open-ended questions, and the ability to plan a small project without a parent managing every step. Those habits, more than any specific fact recalled, are what MYP and DP later reward.

If continuity across programmes matters to you, mention it during matching. Some families prefer a tutor who can plausibly continue for years; others deliberately want different tutors at each stage, since a PYP specialist and a DP Math AA HL specialist are rarely the same person, and pretending otherwise does nobody's child any favours.
items: PYP: ages 3 to 12, transdisciplinary Units of Inquiry
MYP: ages 11 to 16, subject-based with personal projects
DP: ages 16 to 19, IA, EE, TOK, Papers 1-3
Same tutor across stages is possible, not guaranteed or required
PYP habits that matter most: independent reading, open-ended thinking

contentBlocks.heading: South Delhi, Central Delhi and the Areas We Can Realistically Reach
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring for PYP-age children works best when travel time is short, both for the tutor's schedule and because a tired tutor arriving after an hour in Delhi traffic isn't going to run a good session with a six-year-old. That's why home visits are currently realistic mainly in South Delhi and parts of central Delhi: Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket, and Chanakyapuri, along with nearby pockets like Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony, Panchsheel Park, Green Park, and Jor Bagh.

Outside that radius, online tutoring is usually the more reliable option, not a compromise version of it. A PYP tutor teaching Grade 2 Math over a screen, with a parent seated nearby to help the child navigate the platform, works fine for most families once the first two sessions settle into a rhythm. Families in Gurugram, Noida, and Ghaziabad who search for IB tutors in Delhi because that's where the nearest specialists are typically go this route by default.

Be honest with yourself about which one your week can actually sustain. A home tutor twice a week sounds appealing until a Tuesday evening gets eaten by traffic on Aurobindo Marg, and the session either gets cancelled or starts twenty minutes late with a frazzled five-year-old.
items: Home tutoring: Vasant Vihar, Greater Kailash, Saket, Chanakyapuri
Nearby pockets: Defence Colony, Hauz Khas, New Friends Colony
Also covered: Panchsheel Park, Green Park, Jor Bagh
Online tutoring: all of Delhi, plus Gurugram, Noida, Ghaziabad
Home visits depend on realistic travel time, not just distance on a map

contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits, Online Sessions, or a Mix That Fits Your Week
contentBlocks.body:
For PYP-age children, mode matters more than it does for an older DP student who can run their own online session unsupervised. A six or seven-year-old in an online class needs a parent within earshot, not hovering, but available if the connection drops or the child gets stuck navigating a shared worksheet. Families who can't offer that are often better served by home tutoring, where it's geographically realistic, or by weekend sessions when a parent is around.

Home tutoring has real advantages at this age: physical manipulatives for Math, printed reading material, a tutor who reads a child's body language and adjusts pace mid-session rather than relying on a webcam angle. It also has a real cost, mainly a tutor's travel time, which limits how many Delhi families it can serve well.

Online tutoring scales better and opens up a wider pool of tutors, which matters if you want someone experienced with PYP rather than IB in general. Most Delhi families we work with settle into a hybrid: home sessions when schedule and location allow it, online sessions to fill gaps or hold continuity when travel isn't possible that week. Neither mode is inherently better. The right one depends on your child's age, your street's traffic pattern, and how much supervision a weekday evening allows.
items: Home tutoring: physical materials, real-time body-language cues
Online tutoring: wider tutor pool, more schedule flexibility
Young children need a parent or guardian within earshot online
Hybrid plans are common: home when possible, online to fill gaps

contentBlocks.heading: The School Calendars Behind Delhi's IB PYP Families
contentBlocks.body:
Delhi's PYP families tend to cluster around a handful of schools: The British School New Delhi and American Embassy School, both in Chanakyapuri, and DPS International in Saket, among others across the city. Each runs its own version of the PYP calendar, with different half-term breaks, different exhibition dates for Grade 5, and different expectations for how much homework accompanies a Unit of Inquiry. A tutor who has worked with families from a specific school before isn't essential, but it does shorten the settling-in period, since they already know roughly what a typical week looks like for that student.

To be clear about something families sometimes assume incorrectly: IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform. We are not affiliated with The British School New Delhi, American Embassy School, DPS International Saket, or any other school named on this page, unless we say so specifically. Tutors we work with may have taught at or attended these schools, and we mention school names only because they shape what a family in that catchment area typically needs, not because of any formal relationship.

If your child's school isn't listed here, that changes nothing about how matching works. We ask about your specific school's calendar and expectations regardless.

contentBlocks.heading: What We Check Before a Tutor Is Introduced to Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor is shown to a Delhi family, we look at three things: subject and grade-band background, familiarity with the IB framework specifically, and how they explain their own teaching approach when we ask direct questions about it. For PYP tutors, that last part matters more than a long resume. Someone can have taught Math for a decade in a CBSE school and still not know what a Unit of Inquiry is, or how PYP assessment differs from a chapter test.

We ask for teaching background, references where available, and in most cases a short trial session with the actual student before anything is confirmed as ongoing. That trial isn't a formality. It's where we, and you, find out whether a tutor's style suits a specific seven-year-old rather than a hypothetical average one.

Identity and contact details are verified before a tutor is introduced to any family. Beyond that, we're straightforward about what we can and can't guarantee: tutor availability depends on grade, subject, location, and timing, and a strong tutor for one child isn't automatically the right one for another, even in the same class at the same school. If a match isn't working after the first few sessions, tell us. Switching tutors is normal, not a failure of the process.
items: Subject and grade-band background checked, not just IB familiarity
Teaching approach discussed directly, not assumed from a resume
Trial session with the actual student before anything is confirmed
Identity and contact details verified before introduction
Switching tutors after a poor match is normal and expected

contentBlocks.heading: Four Weeks In: What a Parent Should Actually See
contentBlocks.body:
PYP doesn't hand out percentages or ranks, so parents sometimes ask us what "progress" even looks like at this level. Fair question. By the end of four weeks, you should see something concrete, not a vague reassurance that things are "going well."

For a reading-focused plan: the child should be picking up books slightly above their comfort level without resistance, and be able to talk about what they read in more than one or two sentences. For Math: fewer errors on problems the child already understood the mechanics of, and more willingness to explain a wrong answer instead of guessing again silently. For a Unit of Inquiry project: a student who asks a follow-up question unprompted is usually a better sign than one who has simply memorised more facts.

Ask the tutor directly what changed in four weeks, and ask your child separately. The two answers should roughly agree. If they don't, or if a parent's honest read is that nothing has shifted, that's worth raising with us immediately rather than waiting out a full term hoping it corrects itself. We would rather hear about a stalled plan in week five than in week fifteen, when far more time and money have gone into something that wasn't working.
items: Reading: tackling slightly harder books, talking about them in detail
Math: fewer mechanical errors, more willingness to explain reasoning
Units of Inquiry: unprompted follow-up questions, not just memorised facts
Tutor's account and child's account should roughly agree
Raise concerns at week four, not after a full term

contentBlocks.heading: Getting Started With an IB PYP Tutor in Delhi
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is simple on our end: tell us your child's school, grade, and what's actually prompting the search, whether that's a specific subject gap, an upcoming exhibition, or just a sense that reading or Math confidence has stalled. We'll ask a few follow-up questions about schedule and preferred mode, home, online, or a mix, and suggest tutors based on that, not a generic list.

Availability depends on grade, subject, location, and time slot, and is subject to tutor availability at the point you ask; we won't promise a same-day match for every combination, especially for less common requests like a specific afternoon slot in a far corner of the city. What we can promise is a straight answer about what's realistic for your situation, including if the honest answer is that online is your only practical option this term.

From there, expect a short call, a shortlist within a few days, and a trial session before anything is confirmed as an ongoing arrangement. Fees vary by tutor experience, subject, and session length, and are discussed upfront before you commit to anything, not buried until after a first session. If a plan clearly isn't working after a few weeks, say so. Adjusting a mismatch early costs far less, in time and money, than waiting it out.
items: Tell us school, grade, and the actual concern
We suggest tutors matched to that, not a generic list
Short call, shortlist within days, trial session before confirming
Fees discussed upfront, based on tutor experience and session length
Switching tutors early costs less than waiting out a mismatch

faqs.question: Does my child really need a tutor if they're already doing fine in school?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and we'll say so on a call if that's what a school report and a short conversation suggest. Tutoring in PYP tends to help most when there's a specific gap, reading fluency lagging behind the rest of the class, Math word problems causing more anxiety than they should, or a Unit of Inquiry project the child can't structure independently. If your child is meeting expectations and simply enjoys the subject, extra practice can still help, but it isn't urgent the way it would be for a genuine gap.

faqs.question: How much does an IB PYP tutor in Delhi cost?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on the tutor's experience, whether sessions are home or online, and how many sessions a week you want. A newer tutor working with a Grade 1 student on general reading and Math support typically costs less than an experienced PYP specialist handling a Grade 5 exhibition or a child with a specific learning gap. We share exact rates for shortlisted tutors before you commit to anything, not after, so you can compare before deciding rather than being surprised later.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring actually effective for a 6 or 7 year old?
faqs.answer: It can be, but only with the right setup. A young child needs a parent or guardian nearby to help with the platform and to keep attention from drifting, and sessions usually need to be shorter and more interactive than they would be for a Grade 9 student. Where online genuinely struggles is with children who need physical materials, like counting blocks for early Math, or constant redirection; for those cases, home tutoring, where geographically realistic, tends to work better.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and my child don't get along?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it isn't a failure on either side. Tell us within the first two or three sessions rather than waiting it out hoping it improves on its own. We'll ask what specifically felt off, pace, personality, teaching style, and shortlist a different tutor based on that. Switching tutors for a PYP-age child is common enough that we don't treat it as unusual; a seven-year-old's comfort with an adult matters as much as that adult's qualifications.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help with the Grade 5 PYP exhibition?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, if you plan ahead. The exhibition is a term-long, student-led inquiry project, so a tutor who has supported a child through one before can help with research structure, presentation practice, and pacing, without doing the work for the student, which would defeat the point of the exhibition. It works best when arranged a few months in advance rather than two weeks before the presentation date, since the exhibition timeline is set by the school, not by us.

faqs.question: Do you offer home tutoring in Saket or Greater Kailash specifically?
faqs.answer: Home tutoring is possible in both, along with Vasant Vihar, Chanakyapuri, and nearby pockets like Defence Colony and Panchsheel Park, but it's confirmed case by case based on which tutors are available for your child's grade and schedule, not guaranteed automatically because you're in the right neighbourhood. If a home match isn't available when you need it, online tutoring is offered as the alternative rather than leaving you without an option while you wait for the right in-person fit.

faqs.question: What if my child is behind because they moved from a CBSE school mid-year?
faqs.answer: This comes up often in Delhi, given how many families move between school systems. The main adjustment usually isn't content, most PYP-age Math and reading skills transfer fine, it's the shift from marks-based feedback to inquiry-based, narrative assessment, which can confuse a child who's used to knowing exactly where they stand. A tutor experienced with this transition focuses on rebuilding comfort with open-ended tasks first, then closes any real content gaps, rather than assuming the child simply needs to catch up on facts.

faqs.question: How is IB PYP tutoring different from regular tuition?
faqs.answer: Regular tuition in Delhi is often built around a textbook and a test date. PYP has neither in the usual sense, so a tutor's job shifts from covering chapters to reinforcing the thinking skills the programme actually assesses: asking good questions, explaining reasoning, connecting ideas across subjects within a Unit of Inquiry. A tutor who only knows how to drill for a test can still help with raw skills like spelling or times tables, but won't reinforce what the school is actually building toward.

faqs.question: What if there's no visible progress after a few months?
faqs.answer: Then something in the plan needs to change, and we'd rather hear that from you directly than have you quietly give up on tutoring altogether. Sometimes it's the wrong tutor for the child's personality; sometimes the goal was unclear from the start, general improvement is hard to track, a specific skill like reading fluency isn't. mainEntity.name: Does my child really need a tutor if they're already doing fine in school?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily, and we'll say so on a call if that's what a school report and a short conversation suggest. Tutoring in PYP tends to help most when there's a specific gap, reading fluency lagging behind the rest of the class, Math word problems causing more anxiety than they should, or a Unit of Inquiry project the child can't structure independently. If your child is meeting expectations and simply enjoys the subject, extra practice can still help, but it isn't urgent the way it would be for a genuine gap.

mainEntity.name: How much does an IB PYP tutor in Delhi cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fees depend on the tutor's experience, whether sessions are home or online, and how many sessions a week you want. A newer tutor working with a Grade 1 student on general reading and Math support typically costs less than an experienced PYP specialist handling a Grade 5 exhibition or a child with a specific learning gap. We share exact rates for shortlisted tutors before you commit to anything, not after, so you can compare before deciding rather than being surprised later.

mainEntity.name: Is online tutoring actually effective for a 6 or 7 year old?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be, but only with the right setup. A young child needs a parent or guardian nearby to help with the platform and to keep attention from drifting, and sessions usually need to be shorter and more interactive than they would be for a Grade 9 student. Where online genuinely struggles is with children who need physical materials, like counting blocks for early Math, or constant redirection; for those cases, home tutoring, where geographically realistic, tends to work better.

mainEntity.name: What happens if the tutor and my child don't get along?

acceptedAnswer.text: It happens, and it isn't a failure on either side. Tell us within the first two or three sessions rather than waiting it out hoping it improves on its own. We'll ask what specifically felt off, pace, personality, teaching style, and shortlist a different tutor based on that. Switching tutors for a PYP-age child is common enough that we don't treat it as unusual; a seven-year-old's comfort with an adult matters as much as that adult's qualifications.

mainEntity.name: Can the same tutor help with the Grade 5 PYP exhibition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes, if you plan ahead. The exhibition is a term-long, student-led inquiry project, so a tutor who has supported a child through one before can help with research structure, presentation practice, and pacing, without doing the work for the student, which would defeat the point of the exhibition. It works best when arranged a few months in advance rather than two weeks before the presentation date, since the exhibition timeline is set by the school, not by us.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer home tutoring in Saket or Greater Kailash specifically?

acceptedAnswer.text: Home tutoring is possible in both, along with Vasant Vihar, Chanakyapuri, and nearby pockets like Defence Colony and Panchsheel Park, but it's confirmed case by case based on which tutors are available for your child's grade and schedule, not guaranteed automatically because you're in the right neighbourhood. If a home match isn't available when you need it, online tutoring is offered as the alternative rather than leaving you without an option while you wait for the right in-person fit.

mainEntity.name: What if my child is behind because they moved from a CBSE school mid-year?

acceptedAnswer.text: This comes up often in Delhi, given how many families move between school systems. The main adjustment usually isn't content, most PYP-age Math and reading skills transfer fine, it's the shift from marks-based feedback to inquiry-based, narrative assessment, which can confuse a child who's used to knowing exactly where they stand. A tutor experienced with this transition focuses on rebuilding comfort with open-ended tasks first, then closes any real content gaps, rather than assuming the child simply needs to catch up on facts.

mainEntity.name: How is IB PYP tutoring different from regular tuition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regular tuition in Delhi is often built around a textbook and a test date. PYP has neither in the usual sense, so a tutor's job shifts from covering chapters to reinforcing the thinking skills the programme actually assesses: asking good questions, explaining reasoning, connecting ideas across subjects within a Unit of Inquiry. A tutor who only knows how to drill for a test can still help with raw skills like spelling or times tables, but won't reinforce what the school is actually building toward.

mainEntity.name: What if there's no visible progress after a few months?

acceptedAnswer.text: Then something in the plan needs to change, and we'd rather hear that from you directly than have you quietly give up on tutoring altogether. Sometimes it's the wrong tutor for the child's personality; sometimes the goal was unclear from the start, general improvement is hard to track, a specific skill like reading fluency isn't. We'll revisit the plan, set a narrower, checkable goal, and adjust the tutor if needed. A stalled plan is a reason to change something, not a reason to stop.

introSummary: By Grade 11, IB Diploma students in Faridabad are juggling six subjects, an Extended Essay, TOK and internal assessments with real deadlines, not vague homework. That is a different rhythm from Middle Years work, and it changes what a good IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutor in Faridabad actually does: less re-teaching, more structured practice with command terms, timed papers and IA checkpoints. IB Gram helps parents in Faridabad match a DP student to a subject specialist, home-based or online, based on HL/SL level, target session and how much runway is left before mocks.

contentBlocks.heading: What Changes for Students Once DP Begins
contentBlocks.body:
The jump from MYP to the Diploma Programme catches many Faridabad families off guard. A Grade 10 student used to broad, exploratory MYP tasks suddenly has six subjects at HL or SL, an Extended Essay topic to defend, Theory of Knowledge essays with their own command-term logic, and internal assessments due on a school calendar that does not wait for anyone. Revision habits that worked for board-style tuition rarely transfer cleanly. IB examiners reward precise responses to command terms like 'evaluate' or 'discuss', criterion-by-criterion structure, and evidence of independent thinking rather than memorised answers. That is why a generic subject tutor is not always the right fit for DP work.

Faridabad's IB tutoring demand sits inside the wider NCR market. Parents here are not shopping for a board tutor with an IB label; they are comparing a local home tutor against online specialists working across Delhi, Gurugram and Noida who may know a specific HL syllabus or IA rubric in more depth. Neither option is automatically better. A capable Faridabad-based tutor who can visit twice a week has advantages for consistency and accountability. An online specialist may be stronger for a rare HL combination or last-minute IA feedback. IB Gram's matching starts by understanding which of these two problems your family is actually trying to solve.

Extended Essay, TOK essay and exhibition, and IAs across subjects
Command terms like 'evaluate', 'discuss' and 'to what extent' drive marks

contentBlocks.heading: How IB Gram Matches a Tutor to Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with a short conversation, not a form to fill blind. A parent tells us the programme level (in this case DP), the subjects and levels involved — Math AA HL is a very different ask from Math AI SL — the target exam session (May 2026 or November 2026), and roughly how the student is doing right now: comfortable but slow, confused on one paper type, or behind after a mid-year gap. We also ask about area in Faridabad and how much travel is realistic on a school evening, since that changes whether home tutoring is practical or online makes more sense.

From there we shortlist tutors whose subject background and IB experience match the request, and check availability against the family's preferred days and school timings. A first session is treated as a diagnostic, not a sales pitch: the tutor reviews recent school work, a past paper attempt or an IA draft, and tells the parent honestly what is strong and what needs structured work. If the fit is wrong after that first session, families are not locked in. We would rather re-match early than have a student sit through weeks with the wrong tutor.

contentBlocks.heading: Where DP Sits Inside a Longer IB Journey
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram works with Faridabad families across the full run of the IB, not only the Diploma years. The Primary Years Programme covers roughly ages 3 to 12, where the priority is reading fluency, number sense and confidence with the unit-of-inquiry approach rather than exam technique. The Middle Years Programme, ages 11 to 16, is where subjects start splitting into separate disciplines and criterion-based grading first appears in a serious way — this is the stage where study habits for DP either get built or don't. Then comes the Diploma Programme itself, ages 16 to 19, with its six-subject structure, HL and SL choices, and the IA/EE/TOK layer that most parents are searching for when they land on this page.

Treating these as one continuous journey matters practically. A student who struggled with MYP Criterion C tasks (organisation and structure) often struggles with the same thing in a DP IA. A tutor who has taught across programme boundaries recognises this pattern early rather than treating a Grade 11 IA weakness as a new problem. If your child is younger, IB Gram can still help — the same matching approach applies at PYP and MYP level — but the rest of this page focuses on DP, since that is what most Faridabad parents searching for exam-stage support need.

DP (ages 16-19): six subjects, HL/SL, IA/EE/TOK

contentBlocks.heading: Home, Online or Hybrid — What Actually Works in Faridabad
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring in Faridabad works best in compact, well-connected pockets — Sector 15, Sector 16, Sector 21 and the Surajkund-side sectors — where a tutor can realistically commit to a fixed weekly slot without losing an hour to traffic each way. It suits younger DP students who need someone physically present to hold focus, and families who value a tutor walking in, opening books and starting immediately without a technology step in between. It is also more limited: a home tutor's subject range is whatever they personally teach, and travel time caps how many sessions a week are realistic, especially around Neharpar and Greater Faridabad where distances stretch further.

Online tutoring removes the geography problem entirely. For a rare HL combination, urgent IA feedback two days before a deadline, or exam-season doubt-solving at 9pm, an online specialist based anywhere in the NCR can usually respond faster than arranging a home visit. Screen-sharing a past paper or marking a TOK draft together works well on video. Hybrid plans are common for DP: a home tutor for weekly accountability on one or two subjects, plus an online specialist for HL Math or Physics where depth matters more than proximity. Which mix makes sense depends on the subject, the student's independence, and how much structure the family wants at home.

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth That Faridabad DP Students Ask For Most
contentBlocks.body:
Five subjects account for most of the DP tutoring requests IB Gram sees from Faridabad: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry and Economics, with English A writing support close behind. Math AA HL is the one families worry about earliest — the calculus and proof-based sections punish gaps from Grade 10, and a tutor needs to rebuild fluency, not just re-explain the current topic. Math AI HL students usually need different help: modelling, technology use in the GDC, and translating a real-world scenario into a workable equation.

Physics and Chemistry requests cluster around Paper 2 and Paper 3 practice — applying content under time pressure and handling the data-based questions — plus lab report write-ups that need to satisfy IB criteria rather than a generic format. Economics tutoring in Faridabad is often exam-technique focused: structuring a 25-mark essay, drawing diagrams correctly under time pressure, and using real-world examples that examiners find convincing rather than generic. English A support usually means close reading, comparative essay structure for Paper 2, and Individual Oral preparation. None of this is unique to Faridabad, but the tutor pool willing to take on HL-level depth locally is smaller than in Delhi or Gurugram, which is one reason online specialists get requested for these particular subjects.

Economics: 25-mark essay structure and diagram technique

IB Gram groups Faridabad requests loosely by where families live rather than by naming specific schools, since school affiliation changes and we are not tied to any particular institution. The central Faridabad cluster — Sector 15, Sector 16 and Sector 21 — tends to ask for after-school home sessions on weekday evenings, often two subjects a week alongside school homework. Whatever the school, the underlying ask is usually similar: help translating classroom teaching into IB-format answers, a second opinion on IA drafts before submission, and steady past-paper practice as mocks approach. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any school unless specifically stated on that school's page. If your child's school runs its own internal IA deadlines or mock schedule that differs from the general IB calendar, mention that when you request a tutor — it changes how a session plan gets built for the weeks immediately ahead.

contentBlocks.heading: Signs of Real Progress by Week Four
contentBlocks.body:
Trust in a tutoring relationship builds through visible, specific progress, not reassurance. In the first session, expect the tutor to look at recent school assessments or a past paper attempt and name, out loud, two or three concrete gaps — not a vague 'needs to work harder' but something specific: loses marks on the command term evaluate because responses stay descriptive, or the IA introduction lacks a clear research question. That specificity is a test of whether a tutor actually understands DP assessment criteria.

By week four, a parent should be able to see a short, plain-language record of what was covered each session, which command terms or paper types were practised, and where the student stood at the start versus now — not a vague 'good progress' message. If a mock score or a piece of school feedback has not moved, an honest tutor says so and proposes a change: more targeted paper practice, a different explanation approach, or admitting the pairing is not producing results. Weekly academic goals that a parent can see, rather than being told to trust the process, are what separate structured tutoring from unstructured hand-holding. If four weeks pass with no visible change in weak areas, that is a moment to ask IB Gram for a different tutor rather than waiting through the exam session.

contentBlocks.heading: Screening Tutors Before They Reach a DP Family
contentBlocks.body:
Before a tutor is suggested to a Faridabad family, IB Gram checks subject-level qualifications against the specific DP subject and level requested — a Math AA HL request is matched against someone with demonstrated HL-level Math background, not a general math graduate. We look at prior IB teaching or tutoring experience specifically, since IB assessment language and criteria differ enough from CBSE or ICSE that board-tutoring experience alone does not transfer cleanly. Where a tutor has handled IA supervision, EE mentoring or TOK facilitation before, that is noted, because guiding those pieces correctly — supporting a student's thinking without writing or overly directing their assessed work — is a skill of its own, tied directly to IB academic honesty rules.

None of this is a guarantee of outcome; no honest tutoring platform can promise a grade, and IB Gram does not. What we can control is the matching input: subject depth, level, IB-specific experience and communication style, checked before a session is booked rather than discovered by trial and error afterward. If something does not add up during screening — vague answers about which HL topics a tutor has actually taught, for instance — that tutor is not put forward for DP-level requests, whatever their board-tutoring background elsewhere looks like on paper.

Starting is simple in mechanics, even if the decision behind it is not: tell IB Gram the subjects and levels involved, the target exam session — May 2026 or November 2026 — and roughly what is going wrong, whether that is a specific paper type, IA anxiety, or just general slippage since Grade 10 ended. faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: Say so as soon as you notice it — waiting through a full month hoping it improves usually just costs the student time before mocks or an IA deadline. IB Gram can suggest a different tutor without treating it as a failure on the student's part; subject teaching styles genuinely do not suit every learner, and that is a normal, fixable mismatch. Ask about progress specifically: which command terms are still weak, whether a mock score moved, whether IA feedback was concrete. Vague answers are a signal to switch.

faqs.question: Does online IB tutoring actually work as well as home tuition?
faqs.answer: For DP-level work, often yes — and sometimes better. Screen-sharing a past paper, marking an essay live, or walking through a graph in Math AI works fine on video, and it opens up specialists who would never be reachable for a home visit in Faridabad. Where online is weaker is with a student who genuinely needs someone physically present to stay focused, typically younger or easily distracted learners. For most DP subjects — Math HL, Physics, Economics, IA support — online is a realistic, often stronger option, not a compromise.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay, or is that only the school's job?
faqs.answer: The school supervisor remains the official EE guide, but a subject tutor can help around that role — narrowing a broad topic into a researchable question, checking sources are used analytically rather than just summarised, and reviewing structure against the assessment criteria before a draft goes to the supervisor. What a tutor should not do is write or heavily rewrite sections; that crosses into academic honesty territory IB takes seriously, and a tutor who offers to fix an EE draft that way is not one to work with.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with my child's IB World School in Faridabad?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with any school, including schools in Sector 15, 16, 21 or elsewhere in Faridabad, unless a specific school page states otherwise. We are also not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate Organization itself. What we do is match families with tutors who understand DP requirements and, where relevant, that school's own internal deadlines for IA submission or mock exams, which parents should share with us directly since these vary school to school.

faqs.question: My child is behind after Grade 10 — is it too late to start DP tutoring well?
faqs.answer: It depends heavily on when in the two-year DP cycle you are starting and which subjects are behind. Early in Grade 11, there is real room to rebuild fundamentals before HL content compounds — waiting until deep into Grade 12 narrows options to damage control: prioritising a few papers, tightening exam technique, and being honest about which targets are realistic. A tutor who promises to fully close a large gap in a few months regardless of the subject is not being straight with you.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a DP student typically need?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed number — it depends on how many subjects need support, how close the exam session is, and how independently the student works. A student managing well needs one session a week per weak subject; someone heading into mocks with several gaps might need two. Loading up on five sessions a week helps little if the student cannot keep up with the practice work — tutoring adds structure to independent study, it does not replace it. We suggest starting lighter and adjusting after a few sessions show what is needed.

faqs.question: What happens in a first session, and is it a sales pitch?
faqs.answer: No — a first session is treated as a working diagnostic, not a demonstration to win you over. The tutor looks at recent school work, a past paper attempt, or an IA draft if there is one, and talks through specific strengths and gaps rather than general encouragement. By the end, you should know roughly what the next few weeks will focus on and how many sessions a week make sense. If a tutor spends the whole session on generic motivation talk instead of the student's work, mention it to IB Gram.

mainEntity.name: Can a tutor help with the Extended Essay, or is that only the school's job?

acceptedAnswer.text: The school supervisor remains the official EE guide, but a subject tutor can help around that role — narrowing a broad topic into a researchable question, checking sources are used analytically rather than just summarised, and reviewing structure against the assessment criteria before a draft goes to the supervisor. What a tutor should not do is write or heavily rewrite sections; that crosses into academic honesty territory IB takes seriously, and a tutor who offers to fix an EE draft that way is not one to work with.

mainEntity.name: Is IB Gram affiliated with my child's IB World School in Faridabad?

mainEntity.name: My child is behind after Grade 10 — is it too late to start DP tutoring well?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends heavily on when in the two-year DP cycle you are starting and which subjects are behind. Early in Grade 11, there is real room to rebuild fundamentals before HL content compounds — waiting until deep into Grade 12 narrows options to damage control: prioritising a few papers, tightening exam technique, and being honest about which targets are realistic. mainEntity.name: How many sessions a week does a DP student typically need?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no fixed number — it depends on how many subjects need support, how close the exam session is, and how independently the student works. A student managing well needs one session a week per weak subject; someone heading into mocks with several gaps might need two. Loading up on five sessions a week helps little if the student cannot keep up with the practice work — tutoring adds structure to independent study, it does not replace it. We suggest starting lighter and adjusting after a few sessions show what is needed.

contentBlocks.heading: What Faridabad Parents Type Into Google, and What Actually Moves an MYP Grade
contentBlocks.body:
Most searches start the same way: 'MYP tutor near me' or 'best MYP tutor in Faridabad,' typed in after a term report shows a criterion level lower than expected. That search returns a list of names. It doesn't tell you why your child's Individuals and Societies criterion C score dropped, or why a Sciences lab report keeps losing marks on criterion B despite hours of revision. The Middle Years Programme runs on criterion-related assessment — each subject is graded against published rubrics (A, B, C, D, sometimes more), not against a class average. A tutor who doesn't teach to those specific criterion descriptors is, in practice, doing extra homework help and calling it MYP tutoring.

What actually moves a Grade 7 or Grade 9 MYP score in Faridabad is narrower: reading the command terms in an assignment brief correctly, structuring a response the way the criterion rubric expects, and practising the ATL (Approaches to Learning) skills — research, self-management, communication — that MYP quietly assumes a student already has. IB Gram's matching starts from this gap rather than from a generic subject label. Before anyone is recommended, we ask which subject group, which criterion is weak, and which term of the school calendar the family is in — Faridabad's Central, Green Fields-Surajkund and Neharpar school clusters don't all run on the same rhythm.

Command-term literacy matters more than raw hours
ATL skills sit underneath every MYP subject

contentBlocks.heading: MYP Has Eight Subject Groups. Most Faridabad Requests Cluster Around Four.
contentBlocks.body:
The Middle Years Programme has eight subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. In practice, Faridabad requests concentrate on four — Mathematics, Sciences (usually the Physics and Chemistry strands), Individuals and Societies, and Language and Literature. This isn't because the others don't matter; it's because these four carry the heaviest criterion load and set up Diploma Programme subject choices two or three years out. A Grade 9 student struggling with MYP Sciences criterion B (inquiry and design) is often the same student who will need serious support in DP Physics or Chemistry HL later — Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology and English A are the subjects Faridabad's DP-bound families ask about most, and MYP is where the habits for those get built, or missed.

Design and Arts get fewer tutoring requests but aren't lower priority when a student is weak there — a poor Design grade can flatten an otherwise strong MYP record. Language Acquisition requests usually come from students switching schools mid-cycle, or adding a language ahead of DP. We ask which subject and which criterion before suggesting a tutor, because 'Maths tutor' and 'a tutor who can fix criterion D problem-solving in Maths' aren't the same request, even though they sound identical typed into a search box.

MYP Sciences and Maths habits carry forward into DP HL choices
Design and Arts still matter for the overall record
Language Acquisition requests often follow a school change
Subject plus weak criterion, not just subject name, drives the match

contentBlocks.heading: Where MYP Sits Between PYP and the Diploma
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram works across the full sequence — Primary Years Programme learners age 3 to 12, Middle Years Programme students age 11 to 16, and Diploma Programme candidates age 16 to 19 — because Faridabad families often ask about more than one stage at once. A parent enquiring about MYP support for a Grade 8 student frequently also wants to know what DP will demand in two years. That context changes what good MYP tutoring should look like.

MYP itself runs five years, typically Grade 6 through Grade 10 in schools that map onto it, though sequencing varies by school and grade labels can shift a year either way — worth checking your child's actual MYP year rather than assuming from the grade number alone. Year 5 is the exit point: students complete the Personal Project, an independent inquiry supervised by a mentor, and some schools run the optional on-screen eAssessment for select subjects. Both are graded against IB criteria, and both reward a student who can plan, research and reflect independently far more than one who has simply been told the answers. A tutor's job late in MYP is to build that independence, not replace it — pushing a student through a Personal Project write-up defeats the exercise, and can raise academic honesty concerns with the school.

Online tutoring solves a different problem: subject depth. Online also holds up better during exam weeks, when in-person scheduling around school PTMs and mock timetables gets difficult.

Hybrid plans — one in-person session for accountability and structure, one or two online for subject depth — are common for Grade 9 and Grade 10 students preparing for the Personal Project or eAssessment. Which mode fits depends on the sector, the subject and how self-directed the student already is; we ask about all three before suggesting a plan, not just the postcode.

Availability for a specific area or subject combination depends on which tutors are free that term, and we say so rather than promising a name on the spot.

contentBlocks.heading: Four Weeks Into MYP Tutoring in Faridabad: What Should Actually Change
contentBlocks.body:
We won't promise a grade jump, a specific criterion score, or a guaranteed outcome — nobody honestly can, and any platform that does is telling you what you want to hear rather than what's true. What we can describe is what a reasonable first month should look like, so you have something concrete to check the tutor against instead of just trusting a gut feeling.

By the end of week one, you should know which criterion the sessions are targeting and roughly what 'good' looks like for it. By week two, homework review should be specific — not 'did the work,' but 'criterion B reasoning was weak here, here's why.' By week four, there should be a visible shift in how the student approaches a new task independently, even if the graded score hasn't moved yet; criterion scores often lag behind the underlying skill by a few weeks because school assessment cycles don't align neatly with tutoring calendars.

One honest limitation: if a student starts serious MYP support only a few weeks before the Personal Project deadline or an eAssessment window, a tutor can tighten structure and catch obvious gaps, but can't rebuild two years of missing ATL habits in that window. Starting in Grade 8 or early Grade 9, rather than the final term of Grade 10, gives a tutor room to actually build the independence MYP is designed to assess — worth saying plainly rather than promising a late rescue that overstates what's realistic.

Week 2: specific homework feedback tied to a rubric, not just completion

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for MYP, or is it worse than in-person?

faqs.question: What is the MYP Personal Project, and can a tutor help with it?
faqs.answer: It's an independent inquiry MYP students complete in Year 5 (usually Grade 10), supervised by a school-assigned mentor and graded against IB criteria for planning, research, skill development and reflection. A tutor can help a student choose a workable topic, structure their process journal, and stay on a realistic timeline — but shouldn't write sections of the report or make the core decisions for the student. Schools do check for this, and over-involvement can raise academic honesty concerns, not just weaken the work.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with our school or with the IB Organization?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform, not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate Organization, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel, or any specific school in Faridabad, unless we've stated a specific arrangement for that page. Tutors we work with may have taught at or attended particular schools, and we'll mention that background when relevant, but that's a tutor's individual history, not an institutional partnership.

faqs.question: What if my child's grades still aren't moving after a month?
faqs.answer: That's worth a direct conversation rather than pushing through quietly. Sometimes it's the tutor-student fit, sometimes the weekly frequency is too low for the gap, and sometimes the target criterion was misdiagnosed at the start. We'd rather revisit the plan at week four than let two months pass on an approach that isn't showing the visible shifts described earlier — independent task approach, specific rubric-tied feedback — even if the graded score itself is still catching up.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor continue into DP once my child finishes MYP?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, if the subject and level match — an MYP Mathematics tutor comfortable with DP Math AA or AI HL content can often continue, for example. But DP is a step up in depth and workload, and not every strong MYP tutor teaches DP-level HL content. We'll flag this when matching a Grade 9 or 10 student, and can shortlist a DP-ready tutor for continuity if that's useful to plan ahead for, particularly for Faridabad families thinking about Math, Physics, Chemistry or Economics HL routes.

A tutor can help a student choose a workable topic, structure their process journal, and stay on a realistic timeline — but shouldn't write sections of the report or make the core decisions for the student. Schools do check for this, and over-involvement can raise academic honesty concerns, not just weaken the work.

mainEntity.name: Is IB Gram affiliated with our school or with the IB Organization?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform, not affiliated with the International Baccalaureate Organization, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel, or any specific school in Faridabad, unless we've stated a specific arrangement for that page. Tutors we work with may have taught at or attended particular schools, and we'll mention that background when relevant, but that's a tutor's individual history, not an institutional partnership.

mainEntity.name: What if my child's grades still aren't moving after a month?

acceptedAnswer.text: That's worth a direct conversation rather than pushing through quietly. Sometimes it's the tutor-student fit, sometimes the weekly frequency is too low for the gap, and sometimes the target criterion was misdiagnosed at the start. We'd rather revisit the plan at week four than let two months pass on an approach that isn't showing the visible shifts described earlier — independent task approach, specific rubric-tied feedback — even if the graded score itself is still catching up.

mainEntity.name: Can the same tutor continue into DP once my child finishes MYP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, if the subject and level match — an MYP Mathematics tutor comfortable with DP Math AA or AI HL content can often continue, for example. But DP is a step up in depth and workload, and not every strong MYP tutor teaches DP-level HL content. We'll flag this when matching a Grade 9 or 10 student, and can shortlist a DP-ready tutor for continuity if that's useful to plan ahead for, particularly for Faridabad families thinking about Math, Physics, Chemistry or Economics HL routes.

contentBlocks.heading: The Difference Between a PYP Classroom Teacher and a Tutor in Faridabad
contentBlocks.body: A PYP classroom teacher in Faridabad is managing twenty to twenty-five children through a shared unit of inquiry, a fixed timetable, and a curriculum map that has to move forward whether or not every child has caught up. That is the job, and it is a demanding one. A tutor's job is narrower, and in a useful way, slower: one child, forty-five minutes or an hour, no obligation to cover the next unit before Friday. For a Grade 1 to Grade 5 learner, an IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) tutor in Faridabad usually spends the first few sessions on the basics the school assumes are already solid: reading fluency, number sense, spelling patterns, and the vocabulary a unit of inquiry keeps using without explaining twice. PYP does not test the way a board exam does, so a tutor working with this age group watches for confidence and comprehension rather than marks. This matters more in Faridabad than families sometimes expect, because international schools here vary in pace and homework style, and a child moving between schools or joining mid-year can fall behind on vocabulary and inquiry habits even while doing fine academically elsewhere. A tutor closes that specific gap. A school teacher cannot, not because of skill, because of headcount.

contentBlocks.heading: Reading, Number Sense and Inquiry Units, Not Yet HL Physics
contentBlocks.body: PYP does not have subjects the way the Diploma Programme does. There is no Math AA HL or Economics paper at this stage. What a Grade 1 to Grade 5 child is actually working on is transdisciplinary: language (reading, writing, phonics or spelling depending on age), mathematics (number sense, patterns, measurement), and units of inquiry that pull in science and social studies together rather than as separate subjects. A tutor working with this age group in Faridabad spends real time on reading fluency and comprehension, because a child who cannot read a unit's key vocabulary confidently will struggle with the inquiry work itself, not because the concept is hard. Number sense gets similar attention: PYP maths leans on understanding why an operation works, not memorising a procedure, which trips up children coming from a more traditional early-years background. It helps parents to see where this is heading. As a child moves from PYP into MYP and eventually the Diploma years, this early inquiry habit becomes the foundation for subjects families ask about later: Math AA or AI, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology, and English A at Higher or Standard Level. A PYP tutor is not teaching those subjects yet. They are building the reading stamina and number confidence that make them possible later.

Units of inquiry combining science and social studies themes

No formal exam papers at this stage; focus stays on confidence

contentBlocks.heading: Where PYP Sits Before MYP and the Diploma Years
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram supports the full arc from Primary Years Programme (roughly ages 3 to 12) through Middle Years Programme (ages 11 to 16) to the Diploma Programme (ages 16 to 19), and it helps to know where PYP sits in that sequence before deciding what a tutor should focus on now. Across IB Gram's Faridabad network, that continuum runs from Grade 1 through Grade 12, though a PYP-specific request stays focused on the early years rather than DP-level work. PYP is not a scaled-down version of MYP. It runs on units of inquiry rather than discrete subjects, and its assessment is criterion-related and largely internal, with no external board exam pulling the pace. That freedom is useful, but it also means a family cannot lean on exam results to know if a child is on track the way a Class 10 board score would tell them. A tutor's weekly notes end up doing that job instead. Faridabad families with an older sibling preparing for the May 2026 or November 2026 Diploma sessions, often in Math, Physics, Chemistry, Economics or English, sometimes ask a PYP tutor for early habits rather than early content: reading stamina, finishing a written response properly, comfort asking 'why' instead of just 'what'. Those habits carry forward, and the same instinct resurfaces years later in an Extended Essay question or a TOK discussion.

PYP tutoring, done properly, follows the school's actual unit of inquiry, respects the command-term language the school uses, and focuses on reading and number confidence rather than rote drilling, because PYP itself is not assessed the way a board exam is. faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my child's unit-of-inquiry project without doing it for them?
faqs.answer: That is exactly the line a good PYP tutor is trained to hold. Support means helping a child plan research questions, structure a written response, or rehearse a presentation, not writing the poster captions or building the model themselves. IB Gram's verification process specifically checks how tutors handle this, because a child who gets used to a tutor doing the work loses the independence PYP is meant to build, and it shows later in MYP.

faqs.question: What happens if we see no progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Say so directly, and expect a real conversation rather than a defensive one. Four weeks is usually enough to tell whether the pace, the tutor's approach, or the session frequency needs adjusting. faqs.question: Do you only tutor for exams, or is this useful for a child who is doing fine?
faqs.answer: PYP has no board exam at this stage, so this is not exam-prep in the usual sense. Families often use a tutor even when a child is doing fine at school, to build reading stamina ahead of MYP, keep numeracy sharp over a long school break, or simply because a new sibling or move has eaten into homework time at home. contentBlocks.heading: What Breaks When a DP Student Changes Tutors Mid-Year
contentBlocks.body:
A Grade 12 student in Indirapuram loses her Physics tutor six weeks before mocks. The replacement she gets is competent, but wastes two full sessions reading through IA drafts, working out which topics were already covered, and guessing at what feedback the school itself gave. That gap is what most families searching for an IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutor in Ghaziabad are actually trying to avoid, whether they realise it yet or not.

Finding an IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutor in Ghaziabad is easy enough. WhatsApp groups, school parent networks and a dozen tuition centres across Indirapuram and Vaishali all claim to teach IB. What is harder is finding one who stays through a full DP cycle, or who hands over cleanly if they cannot. Switching tutors mid-course is common enough, school transfers, subject level changes from SL to HL, a tutor's own schedule shifting, that a family should plan for the handover before it becomes a crisis, not after.

This page is about how IB Gram approaches that problem for Ghaziabad families: matching by subject and level first, keeping a visible record of what has been covered, and being honest about when home tutoring works, when it does not, and where online support fills a gap the local tutor market cannot.

Topics re-taught from scratch, eating into a Grade 11 or 12 student's limited weekly hours

No shared record of which assessment criterion a piece of coursework was aiming for

contentBlocks.heading: How a Match Gets Made Before the First Session
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with specifics, not a general enquiry form. A parent in Vaishali looking for an IB DP tutor in Ghaziabad for Math AA HL is not looking for the same person as a parent in Raj Nagar Extension needing English A support for a Grade 11 student building toward the Extended Essay. IB Gram asks for grade, subject, level, SL or HL, and whether IA, EE or general revision is the immediate concern, before suggesting anyone.

From there, the process runs roughly like this: subject and level get checked against a tutor's actual IB teaching or examining background, not just a degree certificate; area or online preference is matched next, since Indirapuram travel logistics are different from a fully online Physics HL request; and a short introductory conversation happens before anything is booked, so both sides can flag a mismatch early rather than after two paid sessions.

A match can be reviewed and adjusted later. Level changes from SL to HL happen, subject combinations shift once Grade 11 options are finalised, and a tutor who was right in September is not always right by January. Availability depends on the subject: specialist HL combinations and less common subject requests take longer to place than a standard Math or English one.
items: Grade, subject and SL/HL level confirmed before any tutor is suggested
Tutor's IB-specific teaching background checked, not just a general degree
Area or online preference matched to realistic travel time
Short introductory call before the first paid session
Match reviewed again if level or subject combination changes later

contentBlocks.heading: From PYP to DP: What Changes at Each Stage
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram works across the full IB range in Ghaziabad, Grade 1 through Grade 12, covering the Primary Years Programme, Middle Years Programme and Diploma Programme. Each stage needs a genuinely different kind of tutor, and treating them the same is where a lot of generic tuition falls short.

A PYP learner, roughly ages 3 to 12, usually needs help that looks nothing like formal tutoring: reading fluency, number sense, and talking through a unit of inquiry in language the child can actually use in class, not answer sheets. An MYP student, ages 11 to 16, is dealing with something new, turning a broad classroom topic into work that hits specific assessment criteria across several subject groups at once, which is where capable students often lose marks simply from not understanding what the rubric wants.

By the Diploma Programme, ages 16 to 19, the kind of IB Diploma Programme tuition that helps in Ghaziabad narrows to something higher-stakes: HL or SL subject depth, internal assessment planning, Extended Essay mentoring, Theory of Knowledge support, and timed paper practice against real command terms. A DP tutor who was fine for MYP two years earlier is not automatically right for HL Chemistry now. Subject specialism matters more as the programme progresses, not less.
items: PYP, roughly Grade 1 to 5: reading, numeracy, unit-of-inquiry conversation support
MYP, roughly Grade 6 to 10: criterion-based coursework across subject groups
DP, Grade 11 to 12: HL/SL depth, IA planning, EE mentoring, TOK support
Tutor subject specialism matters more as a student moves toward DP
Support can be reviewed and adjusted as a student moves between stages

contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits Work in Some Ghaziabad Pockets, Online Works Everywhere
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring in Ghaziabad is not equally practical everywhere. It tends to work reasonably well in Indirapuram and Vaishali, where tutor availability and travel routes make regular in-person sessions realistic. Some parents specifically search for IB DP home tuition in Ghaziabad expecting a fixed weekly home slot; that expectation holds up well in these two clusters and gets shakier further out. Raj Nagar Extension and Crossings Republik, off the main tutor routes along NH 58 and NH 24, are harder to service consistently, not impossible, but a family there should expect fewer tutor options and more scheduling friction.

Others look for online IB DP tuition in Ghaziabad specifically because a home visit isn't practical from where they live, and for DP subjects this often works out better anyway. A Math AA HL or Physics specialist willing to travel to Vasundhara on a weekday evening is a smaller pool than the same specialist available online. IA review, urgent pre-mock doubts and last-minute command-term clarification all suit an online session better than waiting days for a home slot.

Hybrid plans are common in practice: a home tutor for weekly accountability and steady pace, an online specialist brought in for one HL subject or the final stretch before May or November exams. A plan built for Grade 11 syllabus pace often needs to shift toward online-heavy support once a student is deep into IA drafts and mock revision in Grade 12.
items: Home tutoring: more feasible in Indirapuram and Vaishali
Home tutoring: fewer options and longer lead times in Raj Nagar Extension, Crossings Republik
Online: wider access to HL and less common subject specialists
Online: better suited to IA review and last-minute doubt-solving
Hybrid: home tutor for pace, online specialist for one subject or phase
Mode can be revisited once a student moves into exam-season revision

contentBlocks.heading: The DP Subjects Ghaziabad Parents Ask About Most
contentBlocks.body:
Seven subjects come up more than any others when Ghaziabad parents contact IB Gram about DP support: Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English A. That is not the full IB subject list, it is simply where demand concentrates in this city's international-school population. IB DP exam preparation in Ghaziabad tends to intensify in two windows: the run-up to mocks, and the final weeks before the actual May or November papers.

Math AA HL generates the most urgent requests, usually from parents who realise partway through Grade 11 that the gap between school teaching pace and what HL actually demands is wider than expected. Math AI HL requests are fewer but no less specific; families want someone comfortable with the applications-and-interpretation style of problem, a genuinely different skill from AA teaching. Physics and Chemistry requests cluster around IA planning season and again before mocks, when IB DP past paper practice in Ghaziabad under timed conditions becomes the priority.

Economics tutoring here often centres on essay technique and applying theory to real case studies; the command terms, evaluate, to what extent, examine, trip up strong students almost as often as weak ones. Biology follows a similar pattern to Chemistry. English A requests usually come from families wanting a second, more critical eye on written commentary before submission, alongside general literary analysis practice for Paper 1 and Paper 2.

Math AI HL, applications-and-interpretation style, a different skill from AA
Physics and Chemistry, IA planning and timed past-paper practice
Economics, essay technique and command-term precision

English A, commentary review, Paper 1 and Paper 2 practice
