contentBlocks.heading: Where Tutoring Help Ends and the Student's Own Work Begins
contentBlocks.body:
IB is explicit about academic honesty, and any DP tutor working in Ghaziabad needs to operate inside that line, not around it. A tutor's job on an IA draft is to ask the questions a student hasn't thought to ask, is this claim actually supported by the data, does this paragraph answer the command term it opens with, is the source properly acknowledged, not to rewrite the paragraph for them. And the same applies to EE mentoring and TOK exhibitions: the ideas and the writing have to stay the student's.

This matters practically, not just ethically. A student handed polished answers for two years struggles the moment they sit an unseen Paper 2 under timed conditions, because the skill that was supposed to be built, applying a concept under pressure, structuring an argument from a blank page, was never actually practised. IB's concept-based, inquiry-driven approach assumes the student did the thinking.

So the honest answer to "can a tutor improve my child's IA" is this: a good tutor improves the thinking that produces the IA, through feedback tied to the actual assessment criteria the school is using, not by doing the work. Parents who want the second thing are better served elsewhere. A decent tutor will say so upfront rather than take the booking.
items: IA, EE and TOK feedback stays feedback, not rewritten paragraphs
Criterion-related comments tied to the school's actual assessment rubric
Command-term precision practised, not shortcut with pre-written answers
Timed, unseen practice matters because real exams are unseen and timed
A tutor who offers to 'do the IA' isn't the right match, and should say so

A family looking for a private IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutor in Ghaziabad is really asking one thing: has this person's subject depth actually been checked, not just claimed. A general Math degree doesn't automatically translate into someone who can teach AA HL, and a Chemistry background doesn't automatically mean someone understands how IA marking criteria work in practice. IB Gram reviews subject-specific teaching or examining background before a tutor profile is shown to a parent, and checks stated experience against what the tutor can demonstrate in an actual sample conversation, not just a resume line.

Identity and contact details are verified before a tutor is allowed to take home-tutoring requests in areas like Indirapuram or Vaishali, given that a stranger is entering a family's home. For online-only tutors, the bar on subject-depth verification is if anything higher, since there is no in-person first impression to fall back on.

None of this produces a number worth quoting, no tutor count, no satisfaction score, because those figures are easy to publish and hard to verify, and a parent shouldn't have to take them on faith. What a parent can reasonably ask for instead: a short call with the proposed tutor before committing, a clear look at what the first month's sessions will cover, and the option to flag a mismatch early rather than sit through a term that isn't working.

contentBlocks.heading: Starting a DP Tutoring Plan in Ghaziabad This Term
contentBlocks.body:
Starting is simpler than most parents expect once the subject and level are clear. Share the grade, the subject or subjects, whether it is SL or HL, and a rough sense of home, online or hybrid preference. A match can usually be proposed within a few days, subject to tutor availability for that specific subject and level; HL combinations and less common subjects can take longer than a standard request.

The first session isn't a test, though it should feel like a real diagnostic. A tutor going in cold usually spends it reviewing recent school assessments, asking what the IA topic is, if one exists yet, or where the syllabus currently stands, and setting two or three concrete goals for the coming month rather than a vague "get better at Physics." That plan should be visible to the parent, not just implied.

By four weeks in, a parent should be able to point to something specific: a completed IA outline, a stronger Paper 1 practice score, a student who can explain a command term correctly without prompting. If that isn't visible, it's worth a direct conversation about adjusting the plan, the tutor, or both, well before May or November exam pressure makes changing course harder than it needs to be.

faqs.question: How much does an IB DP tutor cost in Ghaziabad?
faqs.answer: Fees vary by subject, level and mode rather than following a flat city rate. A Math AA HL or Physics HL specialist visiting an Indirapuram home usually costs more per hour than an online SL revision session, because specialist availability and travel both factor into pricing. IB Gram shares exact fees once grade, subject and SL or HL level are confirmed, rather than quoting one number that would not hold across different requests. It is reasonable to ask for a fee breakdown before booking the first session.

faqs.question: Can we switch tutors partway through the DP if it isn't working?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mismatches happen, particularly once HL depth or IA pressure exposes a gap that a first conversation missed. The match can be reviewed and, if needed, changed. What actually protects the student is the handover: ask the outgoing tutor for a short note on IA status, topics already covered and command terms the student still struggles with, so the new tutor isn't rebuilding from zero. IB Gram's four-week goal-setting is designed partly to catch a mismatch before it costs a full term.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring really work for something as demanding as DP Physics HL or Math AA HL?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes, particularly for IA review, urgent doubts and the run-up to mocks, where a specialist's subject depth matters more than physical presence. It depends on the student, though: a less self-motivated learner sometimes drifts in a purely online setup and does better with in-person accountability. A hybrid plan, home tutor for pace, online specialist for HL depth, is often the practical middle ground rather than an either-or choice.

faqs.question: What if there's no real progress after a few weeks?
faqs.answer: By four weeks, a parent should be able to point to something concrete: a completed IA outline, a stronger timed Paper 1 or Paper 2 score, a command term the student can now use correctly without prompting. If none of that is visible, say so directly rather than waiting out the term. The plan, the pace or the tutor can be adjusted. IB Gram does not promise a grade outcome, only a process that is honest about whether it's working.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic in Raj Nagar Extension or Crossings Republik?
faqs.answer: It's harder than in Indirapuram or Vaishali, mainly because these areas sit further from where most tutors already travel regularly. Home tutoring requests from Raj Nagar Extension and Crossings Republik can still be reviewed, but a family there should expect fewer available specialists and longer lead times, especially for HL subjects. Online tutoring, or a hybrid plan with occasional home sessions, tends to be the more reliable option for families in these pockets, particularly during IA and mock season.

faqs.question: My child needs Math AA HL support and an Extended Essay mentor. Can one tutor do both?
faqs.answer: Usually not the same person. EE mentoring needs someone with depth in the EE's specific subject area, which may or may not be Math, while day-to-day Math AA HL support is a separate, ongoing need. IB Gram typically matches these as two parallel relationships rather than forcing one tutor to cover both. It helps to confirm the EE subject area early, since that determines who the right mentor actually is.

faqs.question: Ghaziabad has fewer IB schools than Delhi or Noida. Does that limit tutor options?
faqs.answer: It limits the local, in-person pool somewhat, yes. That's the honest answer. It doesn't limit online options, since a DP specialist working from Delhi, Noida or Greater Noida can teach a Ghaziabad student just as effectively over a video call, especially for HL subjects or IA review. Families comparing Ghaziabad against the wider NCR market usually end up choosing local home tutoring for younger learners and online tutoring for specialist DP subject matching.

faqs.question: Will the tutor actually write parts of the IA or EE?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers to is not someone to work with. IB's academic honesty rules mean feedback has to stay feedback: pointing out an unsupported claim, an unclear command-term response or a source problem, without rewriting the paragraph. This isn't just about rules. A student who hasn't practised structuring an argument alone struggles the moment they face an unseen Paper 2 under exam conditions.

faqs.question: Can tutoring start close to the May or November exam session, or is it too late?
faqs.answer: It depends on how much syllabus and IA work is already behind. Starting six to eight weeks before mocks or finals can still meaningfully help with paper technique, command-term precision and prioritised topic revision. It won't recover a missed IA deadline or rebuild two years of syllabus gaps in six weeks, and it's worth being told that upfront rather than promised otherwise. The realistic goal late in the cycle is focused revision, not full coverage.

faqs.answer: Start with specifics, not a general search: grade, subject, SL or HL level, and whether the immediate need is IA support, syllabus pace or exam revision. 'Best' depends entirely on that fit. A tutor's actual IB teaching or examining background matters more than a general degree, and a short introductory call before booking lets you judge fit directly rather than trust a profile description alone.

contentBlocks.heading: Exam-Season Firefighting Is Not the Same Job as Year-Long MYP Support
contentBlocks.body: Parents searching for the best IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) tutor in Ghaziabad are usually asking one of two different questions, though they don't always realise it. One is a mock exam three weeks away and a Criterion C score that dropped without warning. The other is a family in September, at the start of the year, asking how to keep a Grade 8 or Grade 9 student on track before things get urgent. Both are legitimate reasons to look for support, but they need different plans. A student in crisis needs someone who can read the unit rubric fast, identify exactly where marks were lost against the criteria, and run focused sessions on that gap, not a general revision course. A student starting early has room for something slower: building command-term fluency, practicing how MYP wants evidence structured, and getting comfortable with eAssessment-style questions well before Grade 10 or Grade 11 pressure arrives. IB Gram does not run one script for both. When you submit a request, tell us which situation you are actually in. A tutor who is excellent at calm, paced MYP subject teaching may not be the right fit for a two-week rescue job, and the reverse is also true. Matching starts with that honest distinction, not a generic profile.

contentBlocks.heading: What MYP Subject Help Actually Covers in Ghaziabad
contentBlocks.body: MYP is organised into eight subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. In practice, most Ghaziabad requests cluster around four or five of these. Math and Sciences dominate, partly because criterion-based science reports and math investigations are where students lose confidence fastest, and partly because parents are already thinking ahead to Diploma Programme subject levels. Math AA HL versus Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Economics come up often even while a child is still in Grade 9 or Grade 10. English A and Language Acquisition requests tend to focus on structuring written responses against the criteria rather than general grammar. Individuals and Societies is the subject families most often underestimate; a tutor here needs to know how to build a source-based investigation, not just explain history or geography content. Design and Arts requests are less frequent through IB Gram but do come in, usually tied to a specific unit deadline. Whatever the subject, the actual skill parents are paying for is the same: turning what was taught in class into evidence that matches MYP's criterion language, without a tutor doing the work themselves.

Individuals and Societies: source-based investigation skills, not just content
English A and Language Acquisition: structuring responses, not grammar drilling
Early conversations about Math AA HL vs AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics

contentBlocks.heading: Placing MYP Correctly Between PYP and the Diploma
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram works with IB tutors in Ghaziabad across the Primary Years Programme, the Middle Years Programme and the Diploma Programme, and it helps to know where MYP actually sits. PYP runs roughly ages 3 to 12 and is built around units of inquiry, gentle and exploratory rather than exam-driven. DP runs ages 16 to 19 and is the two-year, exam-heavy stage most parents already recognise, with HL and SL subject levels, internal assessments and final Paper 1, 2 and 3 sessions. MYP sits in between, roughly ages 11 to 16, and it is easy to underestimate because it looks less high-stakes than DP. It isn't, for two reasons. First, MYP builds the habits, criterion-based thinking, command-term literacy, structured written evidence, that make or break DP performance two years later. Second, Ghaziabad schools increasingly run eAssessment at the end of MYP Year 5, which is a real, gradeable exam with its own format and time pressure. A student who treats Grade 9 and Grade 10 as a holding pattern before real IB starts in DP usually arrives underprepared for the writing and evidence standards it assumes. Across Grade 1 to Grade 12, IB Gram can review requests at any stage, but MYP is where the foundation work happens.

MYP (roughly ages 11-16): builds criterion-based habits DP depends on
DP (ages 16-19): HL/SL levels, IAs, Paper 1/2/3 exam sessions
MYP eAssessment at Year 5 is a real, gradeable exam
Requests reviewed across Grade 1 to Grade 12

contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits, Online Sessions or Both: How Ghaziabad Families Decide
contentBlocks.body: Home tutoring can be feasible in Indirapuram and Vaishali clusters, where tutor travel routes make weekly in-person sessions realistic. It tends to work well for younger MYP students, Grade 6 to Grade 8, who benefit from someone sitting beside them, checking notebooks and building study routine face to face. Once a family is in Raj Nagar Extension, Crossings Republik or further along NH 24, home tutoring gets harder to sustain reliably; traffic and distance start working against consistency, and a tutor who is excellent but based across town may cancel more often than either side wants. Online tutoring solves that distance problem and adds something home tutoring often can't: access to a specialist for a less common subject or a particular DP subject level, rather than whoever happens to live nearby. For IA-style support, urgent doubt-clearing before a test, or keeping sessions running through exam-season traffic disruptions, online is usually the stronger option even for families who prefer in-person teaching normally. A hybrid plan, regular online sessions plus an occasional home visit around a deadline or report card, is what many Ghaziabad families settle on after the first month, once they know which subjects actually need a specialist and which just need consistency.

contentBlocks.body: Before a tutor profile is suggested to a Ghaziabad family, IB Gram checks subject background, relevant IB or international curriculum teaching experience, and whether the tutor's stated mode availability (home, online, hybrid) is realistic for the area and schedule involved. That's the screening step. The actual test is the trial session, and parents should treat it that way rather than as a formality. A good trial session shows a tutor working through an actual MYP task with the student: reading a rubric aloud, asking the student to explain their reasoning rather than just checking the final answer, and being specific about what would move a piece of work from one criterion level to the next. A tutor who spends the whole trial talking rather than watching the student attempt something hasn't shown you much. It's fair to ask direct questions in that first session: how they'd approach an eAssessment-style question, how they handle a student who's stuck on Criterion B, what a four-week plan would actually contain. Fit matters as much as credentials here; a tutor can be strong on paper and still be the wrong pace or personality for a particular student, and that only becomes clear once you've watched a real session.

contentBlocks.heading: No Guarantees, No Invented Numbers, No Shortcuts on Academic Honesty
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram won't promise a grade jump or a specific eAssessment result, and any tutor who does should be a warning sign, not a selling point. MYP's assessment criteria are set by the school and the IB, not by a tutoring platform, and a good tutor's job is to help a student meet those criteria through their own work: explaining a command term, checking reasoning, pointing out where evidence is thin, not producing the response themselves. That distinction matters more in MYP than parents sometimes expect, because criterion-related assessment rewards process as much as final answers, and a student who's been handed finished work tends to struggle the moment the format changes even slightly. Here's the honest limitation: tutoring started two weeks before an eAssessment or a major internal assessment can improve exam technique and calm nerves, but it can't rebuild two years of missing foundation. If a student is genuinely behind, the more useful conversation is about a realistic multi-month plan, not a rescue package. IB Gram's role is to review your request, suggest fits based on subject and mode, and be upfront when a timeline is unrealistic, including telling a parent that a tutor slot isn't available yet, rather than filling it with someone who isn't the right match.

faqs.question: What does an IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) tutor in Ghaziabad actually work on, week to week?
faqs.answer: Most weeks combine two things: whatever the school assigned that week, reviewed against the actual unit criteria, and background skill-building: command-term practice, structuring an Individuals and Societies investigation, or working through eAssessment-style questions for Math or Sciences. A tutor should be able to show you, not just tell you, what a session covered: which criterion was the focus, what the student attempted, and where the gap still is. If a tutor can't point to specifics after four weeks, that's worth raising directly rather than assuming it'll improve on its own.

faqs.question: How much does MYP tutoring cost in Ghaziabad?
faqs.answer: Fees depend on subject, tutor experience, session mode and frequency, so IB Gram doesn't publish one fixed number; a Math AA specialist and a general English A tutor aren't priced the same, and neither are home and online sessions. When you submit a request, the profiles you receive include each tutor's rate, so you can compare before choosing anyone to trial. It's reasonable to ask a tutor directly whether their rate changes for exam-season intensive sessions versus regular weekly ones, since some do adjust pricing around mocks and eAssessment periods.

faqs.question: Does online MYP tutoring actually work, or is home tutoring always better?
faqs.answer: It depends on the student and the subject, not a blanket rule. Younger MYP students, Grade 6 or 7, often focus better with someone physically present, checking notebooks and building routine. Older students needing a specific subject specialist, IA-style support, or last-minute doubt-clearing usually do fine online, and sometimes better, because you're not limited to tutors who can travel to your specific Ghaziabad pocket. If a student is easily distracted at a screen, that's a real factor to weigh before choosing online, not something to ignore because it's more convenient.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic if we live in Raj Nagar Extension or further along NH 24?
faqs.answer: It's possible but less consistent than in Indirapuram or Vaishali, mainly because fewer tutors have a natural travel route through that stretch on a weekday evening, and traffic on NH 24 can make timing unreliable. IB Gram will still review a home tutoring request from Raj Nagar Extension or Crossings Republik, but be aware that fewer matches usually come back, and the ones that do may involve a tutor committing to a longer commute than usual. Online tutoring, or a hybrid plan with occasional home sessions, tends to hold up better for these areas.

faqs.question: What if we start tutoring and don't see progress after a month?
faqs.answer: Say so, early, rather than waiting it out. A working plan should show something visible within four weeks: better structured written responses, more confident reasoning on Math or Sciences problems, or at least a clearer sense of what the criteria are actually asking for. If none of that is showing up, the honest options are adjusting the plan, changing the tutor, or reconsidering whether the mode, home or online, is actually suiting the student. IB Gram treats a mismatch as normal, not a failure, and can review a different tutor profile without starting the whole process over.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors if it isn't working out?
faqs.answer: Yes. A trial session exists precisely because fit isn't always obvious from a profile, and even after a few regular sessions, a family might reasonably decide the pace, personality or teaching style isn't right. That's not unusual and it isn't something to feel awkward about. Tell IB Gram what specifically wasn't working, too fast, too slow, not enough structure, mismatched communication style, since that detail helps the next suggested profile actually fit better instead of repeating the same mismatch with a different name.

faqs.question: Our child is in Grade 9 and struggling with the Individuals and Societies investigation. Is that a common request?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's one of the more frequent requests IB Gram sees from Ghaziabad families, more than parents usually expect. Individuals and Societies investigations ask for a structured, source-based argument, which is a different skill from writing a history or geography essay, and schools don't always spend much class time teaching that structure explicitly. A tutor working on this should focus on how to frame a research question, select and evaluate sources, and build an argument against the specific criteria, not on re-teaching subject content the student likely already knows.

faqs.question: How is MYP eAssessment tutoring different from regular subject tutoring?
faqs.answer: eAssessment has its own format: on-screen tasks, specific time limits per paper, and command terms that expect a particular kind of answer structure. A tutor preparing a student for it should be running practice under those actual conditions close to the exam, not just teaching the subject content in isolation. Earlier in the year, regular subject tutoring and eAssessment preparation look similar; closer to the exam session, the format-specific practice matters more. If your child's school has already run a mock eAssessment, share those results with the tutor; they're more useful than a generic diagnostic.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with our child's school or with the IB Organization?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform; it isn't affiliated with the IB Organization, Cambridge, Pearson Edexcel or any specific school unless that's explicitly stated on a particular page. Tutors are matched based on the student's actual coursework, notebook and teacher feedback, not on any formal relationship with the school. If a tutor ever claims official school or IB affiliation, that's worth double-checking directly, since IB Gram's role is limited to reviewing requests and suggesting suitable, independently vetted profiles.

contentBlocks.heading: What PYP Tutoring Actually Looks Like in Ghaziabad
contentBlocks.body:
The Primary Years Programme does not run on chapters and unit tests the way a CBSE or ICSE syllabus does. A Grade 3 student in Ghaziabad following PYP is more likely to come home talking about a central idea or a line of inquiry than a chapter number, and that changes what home study should look like.

Good study habits at this stage are less about revision and more about talking through ideas, reading aloud, keeping a curiosity journal, and finishing the small research or reflection tasks the school sets between units. A tutor who imports CBSE-style drilling into a PYP household usually creates friction rather than progress.

So finding the right IB PYP tutor in Ghaziabad matters more than finding the cheapest one, and families searching for a primary years IB tutor in Ghaziabad are usually asking exactly this. Parents in Indirapuram, Vaishali and Raj Nagar Extension often type 'IB PYP tutor near me in Ghaziabad' expecting a fast local match, but the better question is whether the tutor has actually taught inside an IB or IB-aligned school, not just prepared students for it from outside.

IB Gram's approach starts with the child's gap, not the tutor list.

contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram can review home tutoring requests across Indirapuram, Vaishali, Raj Nagar Extension, Crossings Republik and Kaushambi, along with nearby residential pockets in Ghaziabad. contentBlocks.heading: Home Visits, Online Sessions, or a Mix of Both
contentBlocks.body:
For a PYP-age child, the mode of tutoring matters as much as the tutor. An IB PYP home tutor in Indirapuram or Vaishali typically visits twice a week, since enough tutors live close enough to commit without losing an hour each way in traffic. A younger learner, especially one still building reading confidence, often does better at their own desk with their own books than adjusting to a screen.

Online tutoring opens up a wider pool: Ghaziabad's market for IB PYP online tuition runs deeper than its home-visit market, since a tutor does not need to live nearby to teach the same content well. For families in Raj Nagar Extension or Crossings Republik, where regular home visits are harder to sustain, online sessions are often the more dependable choice, especially once school reopens after a break and roads get congested again.

Hybrid plans, one weekly home session for accountability, plus one or two online sessions for flexibility, suit families who want a consistent adult presence without limiting themselves to whoever lives nearby. None of these is automatically better. The right call depends on the child's age, how independently they can already work on a screen, and how much the evening schedule can absorb travel time.

contentBlocks.heading: The Building Blocks Before Subjects Have Names
contentBlocks.body:
PYP does not divide learning into Math period and Science period the way later stages do. Instead, six transdisciplinary themes, who we are, how the world works, how we organise ourselves and similar strands, pull literacy, numeracy, science and social understanding into a single unit of inquiry.

A tutor supporting this stage in Ghaziabad is really working on foundations: phonics and reading comprehension, number operations and early problem-solving, written expression, and the research and presentation skills a child will need for the PYP exhibition in the final year.

These foundations matter beyond PYP itself. A student who struggles with number sense at age 8 often struggles later with Math AA HL or Math AI HL in the Diploma years; one who never learns to write a structured paragraph in Grade 4 finds English A analysis harder in Grade 11. IB Gram's tutor network spans this full arc, so a family that starts with a PYP tutor for reading and numeracy can, years later, look for the same platform for Physics, Chemistry, Biology or Economics support at DP level. That continuity is not required, plenty of families change platforms or tutors between programmes, but it does mean the groundwork done now is not disconnected from what comes at 16 or 17.

Phonics, comprehension and number sense are the real priorities
PYP exhibition builds research and presentation skills in the final year
Weak numeracy now often resurfaces in DP-level Math later
Same platform can support a child from PYP through DP

contentBlocks.heading: How a Tutor Gets Matched to Your Child
contentBlocks.body:
Matching starts with a short conversation, not a profile scroll. A parent describes the child's age, current school, which units of inquiry are giving trouble, and whether home or online sessions are preferred.

From there, the process typically runs in four steps. First, IB Gram checks which tutors have relevant PYP or lower-primary IB experience and are available for the requested area or online slot. Second, it filters by practical fit: travel distance for Indirapuram or Vaishali home requests, or flexible availability for online families elsewhere in Ghaziabad. Third, a shortlist of two or three tutors is shared with the parent, with enough detail to judge fit, not just a name and a rating. Fourth, the first session itself acts as a trial: the tutor observes the child's reading level, comfort with numbers and general classroom pace, and reports back with a realistic four-week plan.

Nothing here promises a fixed outcome by a fixed date.

Availability of a good match depends on level, area and current tutor schedules, and can be reviewed rather than guaranteed on a first call. What the process does guarantee is that a parent sees the reasoning behind a match, not just a result.

Step 2: filter by travel distance or online fit
Step 3: share a short shortlist, not just names
Step 4: first session doubles as an assessment
Availability depends on area, level and tutor schedule

contentBlocks.heading: From PYP Through MYP to the Diploma Years
contentBlocks.body:
IB Gram works across all three programmes: the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19. Each stage asks something different of a tutor.

PYP tutoring, the focus here, is about literacy, numeracy and inquiry skills, delivered gently and without turning home time into a second school day. MYP tutoring shifts toward criterion-related assessment, where a tutor has to understand how a school grades against specific criteria rather than a flat percentage, and help a student turn a broad classroom brief into criterion-ready work. DP tutoring is the most specialised: subject-level depth in Math AA or AI, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics or English A, IA structuring, EE mentoring, TOK support and mock exam planning, aimed at the May 2026 and November 2026 sessions.

Academic honesty runs through all three. A PYP tutor helping too directly with an exhibition slide, or a DP tutor writing IA content instead of guiding it, undermines the very skills the programme is trying to build. IB Gram's briefing to tutors is explicit about this line: help a student think and structure their own work, never produce the assessed work for them.

MYP (ages 11-16): criterion-related assessment, A to D
DP (ages 16-19): subject depth, IA, EE, TOK, mocks
May 2026 and November 2026 exam sessions for DP

faqs.question: Does the IB Primary Years Programme have exams like CBSE or ICSE?
faqs.answer: No, not in the way CBSE or ICSE do. PYP relies on continuous, criterion-based assessment built into each unit of inquiry, along with the PYP exhibition in the final year, rather than term-end papers. A good IB PYP tutor in Ghaziabad focuses on strengthening reading, numeracy and inquiry skills week to week instead of last-minute revision. If your child's school does set periodic reviews, a tutor can help prepare for those, but treating PYP tutoring like exam coaching usually misreads what the programme actually assesses.

faqs.question: Is online IB PYP tutoring actually effective for a young child?
faqs.answer: It depends heavily on the child's age and attention span. A 5 or 6-year-old often needs a parent or helper present during online sessions to keep engagement steady, while a Grade 4 or 5 student can usually manage independently with a good tutor. Online tutoring does open access to more experienced IB PYP tutors across Ghaziabad and nearby Delhi or Noida, which matters if local home-tutor options are limited in areas like Raj Nagar Extension or Crossings Republik. For very young learners, a hybrid mix often works better than fully online.

faqs.question: What do fees for a PYP tutor in Ghaziabad usually depend on?
faqs.answer: Fees are not fixed city-wide; they depend on the tutor's experience, whether sessions are home-based or online, session length, and how many sessions are booked weekly. A tutor with actual IB school teaching experience typically charges more than one who has only tutored the programme from outside. IB Gram shares fee expectations before the first booking rather than after, so there are no surprises once sessions begin. If a quoted fee changes mid-term without explanation, that is worth questioning directly.

faqs.question: Can we change tutors if the first one is not working out for our child?
faqs.answer: Yes. A mismatch at this age is common and not a reflection on either the tutor or the child; some pairings simply do not click. If a family raises concerns after a fair trial, usually two to three sessions, IB Gram can suggest a replacement tutor, subject to availability for the same area or online slot. What is not useful is switching after a single difficult session, since a young child often needs a session or two to settle into a new adult's teaching style.

faqs.question: Is home tutoring realistic in Raj Nagar Extension or Crossings Republik?
faqs.answer: It is possible but less reliable than in Indirapuram or Vaishali, simply because fewer tutors are based close enough to commit to regular travel on NH 58 or NH 24. Some families do find a nearby home tutor, particularly for younger children, but many end up choosing online sessions instead, or a hybrid plan with an occasional in-person visit. If home tutoring matters strongly to your family in these areas, mention that upfront so matching can prioritise proximity over experience level.

faqs.question: How is a PYP tutor different from a regular home tutor for young children?
faqs.answer: A regular home tutor for a CBSE or state-board child usually focuses on textbook chapters and homework completion. A PYP tutor works differently: supporting a child's thinking within whatever unit of inquiry the school is currently running, using IB's command-term language, and avoiding rote drilling that can conflict with how the school is teaching concepts. It is less about finishing worksheets and more about helping a child reason, question and express ideas clearly, which takes a tutor familiar with IB's approach rather than general subject knowledge alone.

faqs.question: What happens in the first session with a new PYP tutor?
faqs.answer: The first session is mostly diagnostic. The tutor checks reading level, comfort with numbers, and how the child talks about their current unit of inquiry, then shares a short, plain-language plan for the next four weeks rather than diving straight into worksheets. Parents are welcome to sit in on part of this session. If the plan feels vague or generic after the first meeting, that is a fair reason to ask questions before committing to a regular weekly schedule.

faqs.question: What if my child shows no real progress after a month of PYP tutoring?
faqs.answer: First, it is worth checking what 'progress' was actually defined as in week one; vague goals make it impossible to judge four weeks later. If clear weekly goals were set and genuinely not met, the honest options are adjusting the plan, changing the session frequency, or requesting a different tutor. IB Gram treats this as normal troubleshooting rather than failure. What should not happen is a tutor insisting more sessions alone will fix a mismatch in teaching style or pace.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram only work with families already enrolled in international schools in Ghaziabad?
faqs.answer: No. Most PYP tutoring requests come from families whose children attend an IB-authorised or IB-aligned school in or near Ghaziabad, commonly around Indirapuram, Vaishali or the wider NCR corridor toward Noida and Delhi, but a tutor match is not restricted to any specific school. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school unless stated, and works with any family whose child is genuinely following the PYP curriculum, home-schooled or transitioning included.

contentBlocks.heading: What to Check Before You Book an IB DP Tutor in Greater Noida
contentBlocks.body: Before you commit to a tutor, ask what programme level the student is actually working at right now, not the label on the school report. IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutoring in Greater Noida is not the same job as CBSE or ICSE tuition, even for a subject that shares a name like Physics or Economics. A DP tutor needs to be comfortable with IB command terms — analyse, evaluate, discuss — because a Class 12 board answer and a Paper 2 answer are graded on different criteria entirely. Second, check whether the student needs HL or SL depth. Math AA HL and Math AI HL, for instance, are different subjects in practice, and a tutor strong in one is not automatically strong in the other. Third, work out what stage of the DP calendar the student is in. A first-year DP student mostly needs concept building and steady subject habits. A student heading into the May 2026 or November 2026 session needs past-paper timing, IA deadlines tracked, and mock exam feedback that is specific rather than encouraging. Fourth, decide honestly whether home tutoring is realistic given your address and the tutor's travel route, or whether online tutoring solves the scheduling problem better. None of this is complicated, but skipping it is the single biggest reason families switch tutors twice in one academic year.
items: Ask what DP subject level (HL or SL) the student is actually placed in
Confirm the tutor has handled IA structuring and command-term marking before
Check which exam session — May 2026 or November 2026 — the plan is built around
Match travel realism against your area before assuming home tutoring is possible
Ask what a parent sees after the first four weeks, not just after the first session

For IA and EE requests, IB Gram looks specifically for tutors who understand academic honesty rules and criterion-related assessment, because an IA mentor's job is to question and redirect a student's thinking, not to write sections of the work. If no strong home-tutoring match exists nearby, IB Gram is direct about that and suggests online or hybrid instead, rather than offering a mismatched local tutor. This is availability language on purpose: every match is subject to tutor availability and depends on level, subject and schedule, not a fixed slot promised in advance.

contentBlocks.heading: Where DP Sits Inside the Wider IB Programme Structure
contentBlocks.body: The Diploma Programme is the last of three IB stages, sitting after the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12 and the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16. A student arriving at DP from within the same school has usually built inquiry habits and criterion-based assessment already; a student joining DP after CBSE or ICSE, or moving in from outside Greater Noida, often needs a term of adjustment to command-term language and concept-based learning before subject content becomes the main focus. This matters for tutoring because a DP tutor's real job includes explaining how the IB thinks about a subject, not only the content of it. Physics HL is not simply 'harder Physics' — it expects a student to construct extended response answers, apply command terms like 'evaluate' and 'construct' correctly, and treat the internal assessment as original scientific investigation rather than a lab report copied from a template. English A asks for literary analysis built on interpretation, not memorised points. IB Gram's tutoring across Greater Noida spans Grade 1 to Grade 12, which means a family can, in principle, keep continuity of academic support from MYP into DP if that suits them, though DP subject tutors are usually specialists rather than generalists who also taught the student's MYP years. Parents moving a child mid-DP, especially between the May and November exam sessions, should flag that transition clearly so a tutor can assess gaps rather than assume a clean continuation from the previous school's syllabus pacing.

Middle Years Programme: ages 11 to 16

contentBlocks.heading: Home Tutoring, Online Support or a Hybrid Plan — What Actually Fits

contentBlocks.heading: Subject Depth for DP: Math AA/AI, Sciences, Economics and English A
contentBlocks.body: Math AA HL and Math AI HL are requested most often by DP families in Greater Noida, and the two need genuinely different tutoring approaches — AA leans into proof and pure technique, AI leans into applied, calculator-supported problem solving, and a tutor strong in one is not automatically the right fit for the other. Physics and Chemistry requests usually come bundled with IA questions: what makes a research question 'focused enough', how to structure a lab-based internal assessment, and how to avoid the academic-honesty pitfalls of over-relying on a template. Economics tutoring at DP level tends to need essay-structuring support for Paper 1 alongside data-response practice for Paper 2, since the two papers reward different writing habits. Biology sits similarly to Chemistry in IA structure but often needs more support around evaluating experimental limitations honestly rather than glossing over them. English A tutoring is rarely about grammar at this level; it is about building a defensible literary argument and using textual evidence precisely under exam time pressure. contentBlocks.heading: The Honest Limits of Any DP Tutoring Promise in Greater Noida

What IB Gram can commit to is a matching process built around actual subject fit, checked teaching background and realistic scheduling, rather than a marketing number pulled from nowhere. Availability for any given area or subject is genuinely conditional — it can be reviewed, it depends on level and schedule, and it is subject to tutor availability at the time of the request, which changes week to week as existing students book more sessions or a tutor's own calendar fills up. A parent should expect a first session to cover a diagnostic conversation: what the student currently understands in the subject, where the gaps sit relative to the syllabus stage, and what a realistic four-week goal looks like given the exam session ahead. contentBlocks.heading: Checking a DP Tutor's IB Background Before the First Session
contentBlocks.body: Checking a tutor for DP work is not the same exercise as checking a tutor for board tuition, and treating it the same way is how families end up with a subject-competent tutor who is still the wrong fit for the IB specifically. The first check is subject and level history: has this person actually taught Math AA HL, or Chemistry HL, at the level the student needs, and for how many DP cohorts, rather than a general claim of 'IB experience' with no specifics attached. The second is command-term fluency — a tutor should be able to explain, unprompted, the difference between what 'evaluate' and 'discuss' expect in an answer, because that distinction is where students lose marks even when the underlying content knowledge is solid. The third is IA and EE conduct: a tutor mentoring an internal assessment or extended essay needs to understand academic honesty boundaries clearly enough to question a student's direction without drafting content for them, since IB moderation can flag work that reads as adult-authored. The fourth is exam-session awareness — whether a tutor is actively tracking the May 2026 and November 2026 timelines, or working from an outdated sense of when deadlines fall. None of this replaces a parent's own judgement after the first couple of sessions; it narrows the field before that judgement gets applied, so the first session is spent testing fit rather than discovering a basic subject-level mismatch.

contentBlocks.heading: One MYP Year in Greater Noida, September to the Next One
contentBlocks.body: In September, most MYP students in Greater Noida arrive at a new global context and a set of subject criteria that look nothing like a percentage-based report card. Parents searching for an IB Middle Years Programme (MYP) tutor in Greater Noida are usually reacting to that gap — the school says the student is 'developing' against Criterion C, and nobody at home can translate what that means for the next assessed task. By the time eAssessment or the end-of-year school evaluation approaches, the picture should look different. A student who understood command terms like 'evaluate' or 'justify' in October should be applying them without prompting by March. That is the honest measure of progress in MYP, not a jump in marks alone, because MYP does not grade the way board exams do. For students in the upper years of MYP, tutoring also starts quietly pointing toward the Diploma Programme — not by teaching IA or TOK content early, since those belong to DP, but by building the habit of structured argument, evidence and referencing that IA and TOK will later demand. A tutor who only drills content, or one who treats MYP as a shrunken DP, misses the point, since the assessment criteria genuinely differ. IB Gram's role is narrower and more honest: help a family in Greater Noida work out, subject by subject, whether the gap is confidence, content, or simply not knowing what the school is asking for — then match a tutor who has taught against MYP criteria before, not just IB in general.

Notice that several of those labels — AA, AI, HL — are Diploma Programme terms, not MYP ones. That is deliberate. What a Math or Science tutor does with an eleven- or twelve-year-old in MYP directly shapes whether that student can realistically choose Math AA HL two or three years later, or whether Math AI at standard level is the honest, kinder choice. A tutor who only chases the current unit test misses this. English A tutoring in MYP is not essay-polishing; it is teaching a student to read a text for the writer's choices, which is exactly the skill DP English A rewards later. Economics rarely appears formally before the Diploma, but MYP Individuals and Societies work — argument structure, source evaluation, cause-and-effect reasoning — is where that later comfort with Economics gets built. Biology and Chemistry tutoring at this stage means lab-report habits and scientific writing discipline, not memorised definitions. Support IB Gram tutors are typically asked to provide includes school assignment review and past-paper or practice-task revision; IA structure and TOK-style reasoning come later, in DP, but the underlying habits start here. A subject tutor who cannot explain how today's work connects to that later choice is, frankly, not the right match for an MYP family thinking ahead.

contentBlocks.heading: MYP's Place Between the Primary Years and the Diploma
contentBlocks.body: IB Gram's Greater Noida requests span the Primary Years Programme for ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for ages 16 to 19 — together covering roughly Grade 1 to Grade 12 across the families who ask. Notice the overlap: ages 11 and 12 sit inside both PYP's final year and MYP's first year at many schools, which is exactly when parents first look for outside academic support, because the shift from unit-of-inquiry learning to formal subject criteria is real and sometimes sudden. A PYP student needs gentle reading, numeracy and inquiry-skill support; nobody is asking that student to write against Criterion B yet. An MYP student is being asked to argue, evaluate and justify inside named subjects, often for the first time, and that is where most Greater Noida tutoring requests concentrate. faqs.question: What exactly is MYP eAssessment, and does a tutor prepare a student for it?
faqs.answer: MYP eAssessment is the on-screen, criterion-based assessment some schools use at the end of MYP, built around the same command terms and criteria (A to D) a student has used all year, not a separate syllabus. A tutor's job here is mostly familiarity and pacing: running mock eAssessment tasks on-screen under timed conditions, and checking the student is actually answering what the command term asks rather than writing everything they know. It is closer to exam-technique coaching than new content teaching, since by that stage the content itself should already be familiar from regular schoolwork.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring really effective for an 11 to 13 year old, or is that too young for screen-based learning?
faqs.answer: It depends more on the student than the age alone, but younger MYP students generally do need more structure around an online session than a 15 or 16 year old would — a parent nearby for the first few sessions, a fixed desk setup, and a tutor who actively checks engagement rather than just talking through a screen. Where that structure exists, online tutoring works for most subjects, including Math and Sciences. Where it does not, a home tutor or a hybrid plan, with in-person sessions for younger years, usually holds attention better.

faqs.question: How are fees decided, and can we know the cost before committing to sessions?

faqs.question: What if the tutor and my child just don't click?
faqs.answer: This happens, and it is not something to push through out of politeness. If the fit is wrong on subject pace, teaching style or personality, say so within the first two or three sessions rather than after a full term — the earlier a mismatch is raised, the easier it is to fix without disrupting the student's momentum. IB Gram treats a change request as a normal part of matching, not a complaint to justify. A replacement is reviewed the same way the original request was: by subject, MYP year, mode and area, so the second match starts from what specifically did not work the first time.

faqs.question: My child is starting MYP tutoring late, already halfway through the year — is it still worth it?
faqs.answer: Starting mid-year limits what is realistic, and it is worth being upfront about that rather than promising a full turnaround in a few months. A tutor coming in mid-year usually needs the first two or three sessions just to work out where the actual gaps are against the current criteria, since the student may look fine on the surface while missing structural skills like argument or evidence use. What is realistic afterward is steady improvement in specific, named criteria, not a jump to top marks by year end. Starting is still worth it for most students; it just means expectations should be set around the shorter runway.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram check if a tutor has actually taught IB or MYP before, or just general tutoring experience?
faqs.answer: Both are checked, and the distinction matters. General tutoring experience does not automatically transfer to MYP, because the criteria, command-term language and academic-honesty expectations are specific to the programme. Where a tutor claims MYP or broader IB experience, that background is reviewed rather than accepted at face value, alongside subject qualification and, where relevant, prior exam-board familiarity. This does not mean only IB-school teachers are considered; a strong subject specialist who has taken the time to understand MYP's criterion structure can be a good match too. What is checked is whether that understanding is actually there, not just claimed.

For a PYP learner, who is still building basic reading, numeracy and the habit of explaining her own thinking, that kind of reset can cost weeks of quiet regression before a parent even notices. contentBlocks.body: For a PYP child, home tutoring inside a society cluster like Jaypee Greens or Omega usually works better than it does for an older DP student, simply because a five or eight-year-old benefits from a physical presence, a shared notebook, and someone who can read a facial expression when a concept has not landed. That is one honest limitation of pushing everything online at this age: a screen can deliver instruction, but it does not always catch confusion the way sitting beside a child does. Home tutoring may be feasible within these society clusters, provided the tutor's travel routes make it realistic and school timings leave a usable evening window. Where a suitable home tutor is not available nearby, or where the family wants continuity through a relocation, online tutoring remains available across Greater Noida and is often the more dependable option for scheduling consistency, since it does not depend on traffic on the Yamuna Expressway or peak-hour congestion near Pari Chowk. Hybrid plans exist for a reason: a family might keep a weekly in-person session for reading and writing habits while using a short online slot for a specific gap, or for continuity when travel is not possible one week. None of these modes is universally better; the right one depends on the child's age, how far the tutor has to travel, and how firm the family's evening schedule actually is.

contentBlocks.heading: What a PYP Tutor Covers Now, and What Comes Later
contentBlocks.body: A Primary Years Programme student is not sitting HL or SL papers, so the tutoring here looks different from what a Class 11 or 12 IB Diploma student needs. At the PYP stage, support usually centres on reading fluency, numeracy foundations, and helping a child connect classroom units of inquiry to home practice, using the same command-term language and academic honesty expectations the school already uses, so nothing feels contradictory between tutor and classroom. This matters more than it sounds: a tutor who teaches shortcuts the school does not use, or does an assignment for the child instead of guiding the thinking, works against the programme's own criteria rather than with it. As a child moves from PYP into the Middle Years Programme and eventually the Diploma Programme, subject depth becomes the priority instead, and IB Gram's wider tutor network includes specialists across Math AA HL, Math AI HL, Physics, Chemistry, Economics, Biology and English A for families who will need that later, or who already have an older sibling at that stage. Greater Noida families frequently ask about this continuity directly, because they want one platform they can return to rather than restarting the search for every stage of school. IB Gram can review requests either way, whether the immediate need is a PYP reading tutor for a Grade 2 student or a DP Physics specialist preparing for a May 2026 or November 2026 session.

IB Gram reviews this against tutor profiles for relevant background: subject or age-group experience, familiarity with IB's concept-based approach and criterion-related assessment, and, where relevant, exam-board familiarity for MYP or DP families. A shortlist is offered rather than a single forced choice, because fit for a seven-year-old learning to structure a paragraph is a different skill from fit for a seventeen-year-old managing an Economics IA under deadline pressure. The first session is treated as a checkpoint, not a formality: it should confirm the child's actual level against what the parent believes it is, note the specific unit of inquiry or topic in progress, and set a small, parent-visible goal for the coming weeks rather than a vague promise of improvement. If the first tutor is not the right personality fit for the child, that is treated as normal information, not a failure, and a second match can be reviewed. Availability for any specific tutor is naturally subject to their existing schedule and location, so timelines can shift depending on demand in a given area.

contentBlocks.heading: PYP, MYP and DP: Where Greater Noida Families Usually Are
contentBlocks.body: The Primary Years Programme runs for Ages 3 to 12, the Middle Years Programme for Ages 11 to 16, and the Diploma Programme for Ages 16 to 19, and a lot of confusion in first conversations comes from parents describing their child's needs in board-exam language that does not quite map onto IB's structure. A PYP parent asking for 'exam preparation' usually means help with a unit of inquiry task, a reading assessment, or building the habit of independent work, since formal external exams are not part of this stage. An MYP parent is often looking for someone who can turn open-ended criteria into a structured piece of work without simply supplying the answer. A DP parent in Greater Noida is usually thinking about IA structure, EE mentoring, TOK support, or past-paper revision ahead of the May 2026 or November 2026 session, alongside review of school assignments and mock exam planning. IB Gram's tutor network spans all three stages, which matters for families with more than one child, or a single child who will eventually move through all of them. Naming the actual stage correctly at the start saves a wasted first session; a tutor experienced with DP Economics is not automatically the right fit for a Grade 2 reading gap, and the reverse is equally true.

faqs.question: What happens if our tutor becomes unavailable partway through the year?

The Diploma is scored out of 45, made from six subject grades out of 7 plus up to three points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. contentBlocks.heading: This Week, This Month, This Term: DP Decisions Gurugram Parents Face
contentBlocks.body:
Parents rarely arrive with a two-year plan. They arrive with a deadline.

This week is usually one thing: a draft due Friday, a test coming back badly, a coordinator email that used the word concern. The useful response is narrow. Find out what the actual task is asking, work out which part the student cannot do, and get one session in before the deadline rather than three sessions after it.

This month is where most of the damage is either done or avoided. Internal assessments in six subjects do not arrive evenly. They cluster, and in most Gurugram schools they cluster in the same two windows every year, which is why a student who is fine in October falls apart in November. A month is enough time to sequence the drafts, decide which ones get a full effort and which get a competent one, and stop the Extended Essay from being the thing that slides.

This term is the real planning horizon. Subject levels can still change early in DP1. Predicted grades are built from work produced across the whole of DP1 and the first half of DP2, not from a final sprint. So the families who get the most out of an IB Diploma Programme (DP) tutor in Gurugram are the ones who start before the term that scares them.

contentBlocks.heading: Where DP Home Tutoring in Gurugram Is Worth the Drive
contentBlocks.body:
Home tutoring may be arranged across Golf Course Road, the DLF phases, Sushant Lok, Sector 57 and Sohna Road, depending on which tutors have a free evening near you. Whether it is worth arranging is a separate question from whether it is possible.

A Diploma student in DP2 has a finite number of usable hours per week. Every hour a tutor spends in a car is an hour priced into the session, and every hour the student spends waiting for a delayed tutor is an hour of homework not done. Along Golf Course Road, with Sector 53 and Sector 54 on the Rapid Metro corridor, that maths works out. It works for DLF Phase 5 near The Crest and DLF Park Place too, and usually for South City 1, DLF Phase 1 and DLF Phase 4.

Sector 57, Sushant Lok 3 and Golf Course Extension Road sit on the boundary: fine at six, unpredictable at eight. Sohna Road towards Vatika Chowk and the Sector 49 to Sector 50 stretch is where the arithmetic usually fails on weekdays, as does Sector 65 and Nirvana Country. Families in those pockets tend to keep home sessions for Saturdays. And for a student travelling in daily from Delhi, Noida or Faridabad, adding another journey to the week rarely helps anyone.

DLF Phase 1, 4 and 5 and South City 1: usually workable midweek
Sector 57 and Golf Course Extension Road: fine early, slow later

contentBlocks.heading: Fitting DP Sessions Into a Gurugram School Night
contentBlocks.body:
Count the hours honestly before choosing a mode. A DP2 student in Gurugram is at school until roughly three, home somewhere between four and five, and carrying homework from six subjects plus creativity, activity and service commitments that a school will not waive. What is left for tuition is around two usable evening slots and part of a weekend.

Online sessions fit into that shape better because they can be shorter and still worth running. Forty minutes on one Paper 3 question set is a real session online; the same forty minutes with travel attached is not worth anyone booking. Online also opens up tutors outside the city entirely, which matters most for the subjects Gurugram has fewer local specialists in, and for anyone needing a late slot after a long activity day.

In-person work justifies itself for specific tasks. Sitting with a returned mock script and going through the mark scheme line by line. Planning an Extended Essay structure with sources spread across a table. The week before an internal exam, when the student is running on fumes and a video call becomes background noise. Hybrid is the common pattern here: home at the weekend, screen midweek, and both dropped for a few days when the school schedule turns brutal.
items: Two weekday slots and part of a weekend is realistic for DP2
Short online sessions still earn their place; short home sessions do not
Online widens access to less common HL subject specialists
Marked mock scripts and EE planning suit in-person work
Pause sessions during school assessment weeks rather than stacking them

contentBlocks.heading: Six Subjects, Three at Higher Level, and Where They Break
contentBlocks.body:
The Diploma asks for one subject from each of six groups, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard. Higher Level runs 240 teaching hours against 150 at Standard, and the extra hours are extra content and extra assessment rather than a slower pace.

Each subject fails in its own way. Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and the choice made in DP1 shapes university options; both Higher Level routes carry a Paper 3 that Standard Level does not, and both need the Exploration written up as an internal assessment. In Language A, students lose marks in Paper 1 by summarising an unseen text instead of analysing how it works, and in the Individual Oral by choosing a global issue too broad to evidence. Sciences turn on the scientific investigation and on data handling under time. Economics and the other Individuals and Societies subjects reward evaluation, which is a skill, not a paragraph added at the end.

Internal assessments across the six typically carry twenty to thirty per cent each, depending on the subject. That is the part a tutor can affect steadily over months, unlike a final paper sat once.
items: Three HL at 240 hours, three SL at 150 hours
Maths AA and AI split, with Paper 3 at Higher Level only
Language A: Paper 1 unseen analysis, Paper 2 comparison, Individual Oral
Sciences: the scientific investigation plus timed data questions
IA weightings run roughly twenty to thirty per cent per subject

contentBlocks.heading: From Enquiry to Shortlist: How a Diploma Tutor Match Is Made
contentBlocks.body:
Start by telling us the subject, the level, the school, the exam session and the deadline you are worried about. Those five details decide almost everything. A request that says maths help needed produces a guess; a request that says Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, DP1, Exploration draft due in three weeks, weak on modelling produces a match.

An advisor then reads the request and asks follow-up questions, usually about the last two assessment grades and whether the student can articulate their own weak point. We check which tutors hold genuine availability in your time band, not tutors who might free up. You receive a shortlist with each person teaching background, the levels they cover, and whether they can travel to your address or work online only.

The first session is a diagnostic. It should end with a written summary naming what was tested, what broke, and what the next few weeks look like. Where a family needs support across two subjects, we usually recommend staggering the starts by a fortnight rather than beginning both at once, because a DP2 student who suddenly has four extra commitments a week tends to drop the wrong one. Changing tutor after the first session is normal and costs nothing beyond a week.
items: Five details that make a match: subject, level, school, session, deadline
Follow-up questions on the last assessment grades
Shortlist shows levels covered and travel or online only
Diagnostic first session, written summary afterwards
Stagger a second subject by a fortnight rather than starting together

contentBlocks.heading: How MYP and IGCSE Students Land in the Diploma Programme
contentBlocks.body:
Students reach DP1 from two directions in Gurugram, and they arrive with different gaps.

Students coming through the Middle Years Programme are used to criterion-based marking and to writing against descriptors, which is a genuine advantage in the first term. What they often lack is volume and speed: MYP tasks are longer and fewer, and Diploma papers demand quick, dense answers under strict timing. Students arriving from IGCSE tend to be the reverse. They are drilled on past papers and comfortable with timed writing, then meet criterion-referenced internal assessment and Theory of Knowledge and find there is no model answer to memorise.

The core catches both groups equally. Theory of Knowledge runs across both years and produces an essay of 1,600 words on a prescribed title plus an exhibition of three objects with a 950-word commentary. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words with a supervisor, formal reflection sessions and the viva voce at the end. Together they earn up to three points on the diploma matrix, and an E grade in either is a failing condition regardless of how strong the six subject grades are. Creativity, activity and service is not graded, but an incomplete record blocks the diploma.
items: MYP entrants: strong on criteria, short on timed volume
IGCSE entrants: strong on past papers, new to criterion marking
TOK: 1,600-word essay plus a 950-word exhibition commentary
EE: 4,000 words, supervisor, reflections and viva voce
Up to three core points; an E grade in either is a failing condition

contentBlocks.heading: DP Schools in Gurugram Set Their Own Internal Calendar
contentBlocks.body:
The names that come up most often in conversations here are Pathways World School, Lancers International School on Golf Course Road, Scottish High International School in Sector 57 and GD Goenka World School out past Sohna Road. IB Gram is an independent tutoring platform and is not officially affiliated with these schools unless specifically stated. Tutors do not represent them, do not see internal marks and have no part in predicted grades.

The practical point is that the external exam timetable is fixed but almost nothing else is. Each school decides when internal assessment drafts are due, when mocks run, when Extended Essay reflection meetings happen and when predicted grades are finalised for university applications. Two students in the same session, living a few sectors apart, can be working to calendars a month or more out of step.

So the first thing worth doing is getting your school assessment calendar in front of the tutor. Everything else is scheduled backwards from it. A plan built around the published exam dates alone will miss the internal deadlines that consume the autumn term of DP2, and those deadlines are where students actually lose marks and sleep.

contentBlocks.heading: What Gets Verified Before a Diploma Programme Tutor Is Suggested
contentBlocks.body:
Identity documents are checked first. Then qualifications, against the exact subject and level being claimed, because Higher Level teaching experience and Standard Level teaching experience are not interchangeable in practice. Teaching history is discussed in detail: which curricula, which years, which assessment components they have actually handled rather than read about.

There is a Diploma-specific conversation as well. A tutor working with DP students should be able to explain how the points total is built, what the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge matrix does, and which conditions can prevent a diploma being awarded even when the total looks acceptable. They should know the assessment objectives behind the command terms, because a student answering evaluate as though it said describe loses marks that have nothing to do with knowledge.

Academic honesty gets covered plainly. A tutor may explain a criterion, question a research question, and point out that an argument is not supported. A tutor may not draft internal assessment or Extended Essay text, or supply work to be submitted. The candidate signs for their own work. References are taken where someone has taught in a school, and feedback from families is reviewed as the arrangement continues.
items: Identity checked before any introduction
Qualifications matched to the exact subject and level
Curriculum history discussed component by component
Working knowledge of points, core bonus and failing conditions
Academic honesty boundary agreed in writing

contentBlocks.heading: The Points Arithmetic Nobody Explains at the Parent Meeting
contentBlocks.body:
Here is the part worth understanding before you spend money on tutoring. Six subjects, each graded 1 to 7, gives a maximum of 42. The Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge together add up to three more, for 45 in total. Twenty-four points is the minimum for the diploma, and there are separate conditions on top: a grade 1 anywhere, too many 2s, or an E in the Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge can prevent an award even when the arithmetic looks fine.

That structure changes where tutoring is worth spending. Moving a subject from 6 to 7 is expensive in hours and worth one point. Moving a weak subject from 3 to 5 is usually cheaper in hours and worth two, and it removes a risk to the diploma itself. An unfinished Extended Essay threatens everything and often needs structure rather than teaching.

What no tutor can offer is a promised outcome. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, points or percentage improvements, and does not publish student results as proof. What can be described honestly is the process: diagnosis, a written plan, work reviewed against the actual criteria, and a review after four weeks with the option to change tutor or stop.
items: 42 subject points plus up to 3 core points, 45 maximum
24 points minimum, with separate conditions that can still block an award
Lifting a weak subject usually buys more than polishing a strong one
An unfinished EE is a structural risk, not a knowledge gap
No guaranteed points, grades or improvement percentages

contentBlocks.heading: Starting DP Tutoring in Gurugram Without Overcommitting
contentBlocks.body:
Begin with the single subject causing the most pressure this month, not with a full timetable. Families who book support in four subjects at once almost always cut back within a fortnight, and the cut is made under stress rather than on evidence.

Tell us the subject and level, the school, the exam session, and the deadline you are actually worried about. An advisor will come back with a shortlist and honest availability notes. Some tutors can travel to Sushant Lok or DLF Phase 4, others work online only, and availability depends on level and schedule and is subject to tutor availability, particularly in the weeks before mocks when demand rises sharply.

Run one diagnostic session and read the summary. If it does not tell you something you did not already know, that is useful information about the tutor. From there, most families settle into one or two sessions a week and review after a month. Students entered for May 2026 should be planning across the current term, since internal deadlines land well before the exams. November 2026 candidates and retake students work to a different calendar and can begin later, though the Extended Essay rarely waits well.
items: Start with one subject, add a second later if it earns its place
Share subject, level, school, session and the deadline in question
Availability tightens in the weeks before mocks
One diagnostic session, then a four-week review point
May 2026 planning starts this term; November 2026 runs later

faqs.question: How many points does my child realistically need for university applications?
faqs.answer: It varies by country and course far more than parents expect. Competitive UK courses often ask in the mid to high thirties with named Higher Level subjects at 6 or 7. Many strong universities elsewhere sit lower. Indian universities accepting the diploma publish their own conversion rules. Work backwards from the actual offers for the actual courses your child is considering, then decide where tutoring hours go. Chasing a round number without checking subject-specific requirements wastes a term.

faqs.question: My child is taking four Higher Level subjects and drowning. Should they drop one?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and earlier is better. A fourth Higher Level subject adds ninety taught hours and another set of assessment components, and only the best three Higher Level grades count towards the relevant point conditions. If it is dragging down the other five subjects and the Extended Essay, the drop usually protects more points than it costs. The decision belongs to the school coordinator and there is a cut-off date, so raise it now rather than after mocks.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one Diploma subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, for combinations that genuinely overlap, such as Mathematics with Physics or Economics with Business Management. More often it is a poor idea. Diploma subjects are assessed against different criteria and different command term expectations, and a tutor stretched across two of them usually does one well and one adequately. We would rather match separately and stagger the start dates, so the student is not absorbing two new working relationships in the same week.

faqs.question: How does a tutor help with the Extended Essay without writing it?
faqs.answer: By working on structure and thinking rather than text. That means testing whether the research question can actually be answered in four thousand words, checking that the method matches the question, reading an argument and saying where the evidence stops supporting it, and preparing the student for reflection sessions and the viva voce with their supervisor. The supervisor at school stays the official guide and signs the reflection form. Tutors do not draft, rewrite or supply passages for submission.

faqs.question: We are between DP1 and DP2 over the summer. Is that a wasted holiday or a chance?
faqs.answer: It is the single most useful gap in the two years, and it is short. Realistic uses are getting the Extended Essay to a full first draft, finishing internal assessment data collection while the topic is still fresh, and repairing one subject that went badly in the DP1 exams. Trying to revise all six subjects over a holiday achieves very little and starts DP2 tired. Pick two goals, protect actual rest, and leave the rest for the term.

faqs.question: What does DP tutoring in Gurugram cost per session?
faqs.answer: It depends on level, subject, session length, frequency and whether the tutor travels. Higher Level generally costs more than Standard Level, and less common subjects cost more than widely taught ones. Home sessions carry travel time and price accordingly. A short intensive block before mocks and a steady weekly arrangement across two years are quoted differently. We give a range against your specific request instead of a headline rate, and fees can be reviewed if the arrangement changes.

faqs.question: The school says everything is fine but the predicted grade came back low. What now?
faqs.answer: Ask which pieces of work the prediction is built from. Predicted grades usually draw on internal assessments, mock papers and classwork across DP1 and early DP2, so a low prediction points at a pattern rather than one bad afternoon. Get the marked scripts and read the examiner comments with the student. In most cases a specific component is dragging, often an internal assessment or a particular paper, and that is the thing tutoring should target first.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring genuinely enough for Theory of Knowledge?
faqs.answer: Yes, arguably better than most subjects. Theory of Knowledge work is discussion, argument and written structure, none of which needs a shared table. The essay responds to a prescribed title and the exhibition needs three objects tied to a prompt, and both improve through being questioned out loud. A screen suits that. What matters more is finding someone who has read the current assessment instruments rather than someone treating it as general philosophy.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is good but my child simply does not respond to them?
faqs.answer: Say so early. Fit is not a soft consideration in a two-year programme, and a student who dreads the session will find reasons to miss it. Tell the advisor what specifically is not working, since the answer is sometimes a change of approach rather than a change of person. If a swap is right, we arrange a different match and the new tutor gets the notes from the previous sessions so nothing is repeated from scratch.
